segs.e: Numbered Discourses 10.1
1. Benefits
What’s the Goal?
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:
“Sir, what is the goal and benefit of skillful ethics?”
“Ānanda, having no regrets is the goal and benefit of skillful ethics.”
“But what is the goal and benefit of having no regrets?”
“Joy is the goal and benefit of having no regrets.”
“But what is the goal and benefit of joy?”
“Rapture …”
“But what is the goal and benefit of rapture?”
“Tranquility …”
“But what is the goal and benefit of tranquility?”
“Bliss …”
“But what is the goal and benefit of bliss?”
“Immersion …”
“But what is the goal and benefit of immersion?”
“Truly knowing and seeing …”
“But what is the goal and benefit of truly knowing and seeing?”
“Disillusionment and dispassion …”
“But what is the goal and benefit of disillusionment and dispassion?”
“Knowledge and vision of freedom is the goal and benefit of disillusionment and dispassion.

segs.p: Iti kho, ānanda, kusalāni sīlāni avippaṭisāratthāni avippaṭisārānisaṁsāni;
segs.e: So, Ānanda, the goal and benefit of skillful ethics is not having regrets.
Joy is the goal and benefit of not having regrets.
Rapture is the goal and benefit of joy.
Tranquility is the goal and benefit of rapture.
Bliss is the goal and benefit of tranquility.
Immersion is the goal and benefit of bliss.
Truly knowing and seeing is the goal and benefit of immersion.
Disillusionment and dispassion is the goal and benefit of truly knowing and seeing.
Knowledge and vision of freedom is the goal and benefit of disillusionment and dispassion.

segs.p: Iti kho, ānanda, kusalāni sīlāni anupubbena aggāya parentī”ti.
segs.e: So, Ānanda, skillful ethics progressively lead up to the highest.”
Numbered Discourses 10.2
1. Benefits
Making a Wish
“Mendicants, an ethical person, who has fulfilled ethical conduct, need not make a wish:
‘May I have no regrets!’

segs.p: Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṁ sīlavato sīlasampannassa avippaṭisāro uppajjati.
segs.e: It’s only natural that an ethical person has no regrets.
When you have no regrets you need not make a wish:
‘May I feel joy!’

segs.p: Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṁ avippaṭisārissa pāmojjaṁ jāyati.
segs.e: It’s only natural that joy springs up when you have no regrets.
When you feel joy you need not make a wish:
‘May I experience rapture!’

segs.p: Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṁ pamuditassa pīti uppajjati.
segs.e: It’s only natural that rapture arises when you’re joyful.
When your mind is full of rapture you need not make a wish:
‘May my body become tranquil!’

segs.p: Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṁ pītimanassa kāyo passambhati.
segs.e: It’s only natural that your body becomes tranquil when your mind is full of rapture.
When your body is tranquil you need not make a wish:
‘May I feel bliss!’

segs.p: Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṁ passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vediyati.
segs.e: It’s only natural to feel bliss when your body is tranquil.
When you feel bliss you need not make a wish:
‘May my mind be immersed in samādhi!’

segs.p: Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṁ sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.
segs.e: It’s only natural for the mind to be immersed in samādhi when you feel bliss.
When your mind is immersed in samādhi you need not make a wish:
‘May I truly know and see!’

segs.p: Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṁ samāhito yathābhūtaṁ jānāti passati.
segs.e: It’s only natural to truly know and see when your mind is immersed in samādhi.

segs.p: Yathābhūtaṁ, bhikkhave, jānato passato na cetanāya karaṇīyaṁ:
segs.e: When you truly know and see you need not make a wish:
‘May I become disillusioned and dispassionate!’

segs.p: Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṁ yathābhūtaṁ jānaṁ passaṁ nibbindati virajjati.
segs.e: It’s only natural to become disillusioned and dispassionate when you truly know and see.

segs.p: Nibbinnassa, bhikkhave, virattassa na cetanāya karaṇīyaṁ:
segs.e: When you’re disillusioned and dispassionate you need not make a wish:
‘May I realize the knowledge and vision of freedom!’

segs.p: Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṁ nibbinno viratto vimuttiñāṇadassanaṁ sacchikaroti.
segs.e: It’s only natural to realize the knowledge and vision of freedom when you’re disillusioned and dispassionate.

segs.p: Iti kho, bhikkhave, nibbidāvirāgo vimuttiñāṇadassanattho vimuttiñāṇadassanānisaṁso;
segs.e: And so, mendicants, the knowledge and vision of freedom is the goal and benefit of disillusionment and dispassion.
Disillusionment and dispassion is the goal and benefit of truly knowing and seeing.
Truly knowing and seeing is the goal and benefit of immersion.
Immersion is the goal and benefit of bliss.
Bliss is the goal and benefit of tranquility.
Tranquility is the goal and benefit of rapture.
Rapture is the goal and benefit of joy.
Joy is the goal and benefit of not having regrets.
Not having regrets is the goal and benefit of skillful ethics.

segs.p: Iti kho, bhikkhave, dhammā dhamme abhisandenti, dhammā dhamme paripūrenti apārā pāraṁ gamanāyā”ti.
segs.e: And so, mendicants, good qualities flow on and fill up from one to the other, for going from the near shore to the far shore.”
Numbered Discourses 10.3
1. Benefits
Vital Conditions (1st)
“Mendicants, an unethical person, who lacks ethics, has destroyed a vital condition for having no regrets.

segs.p: avippaṭisāre asati avippaṭisāravipannassa hatūpanisaṁ hoti pāmojjaṁ;
segs.e: When there are regrets, one who has regrets has destroyed a vital condition for joy.

segs.p: pāmojje asati pāmojjavipannassa hatūpanisā hoti pīti;
segs.e: When there is no joy, one who lacks joy has destroyed a vital condition for rapture.

segs.p: pītiyā asati pītivipannassa hatūpanisā hoti passaddhi;
segs.e: When there is no rapture, one who lacks rapture has destroyed a vital condition for tranquility.

segs.p: passaddhiyā asati passaddhivipannassa hatūpanisaṁ hoti sukhaṁ;
segs.e: When there is no tranquility, one who lacks tranquility has destroyed a vital condition for bliss.

segs.p: sukhe asati sukhavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti sammāsamādhi;
segs.e: When there is no bliss, one who lacks bliss has destroyed a vital condition for right immersion.

segs.p: sammāsamādhimhi asati sammāsamādhivipannassa hatūpanisaṁ hoti yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṁ;
segs.e: When there is no right immersion, one who lacks right immersion has destroyed a vital condition for true knowledge and vision.

segs.p: yathābhūtañāṇadassane asati yathābhūtañāṇadassanavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti nibbidāvirāgo;
segs.e: When there is no true knowledge and vision, one who lacks true knowledge and vision has destroyed a vital condition for disillusionment and dispassion.

segs.p: nibbidāvirāge asati nibbidāvirāgavipannassa hatūpanisaṁ hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanaṁ.
segs.e: When there is no disillusionment and dispassion, one who lacks disillusionment and dispassion has destroyed a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, rukkho sākhāpalāsavipanno. Tassa papaṭikāpi na pāripūriṁ gacchati, tacopi … pheggupi … sāropi na pāripūriṁ gacchati.
segs.e: Suppose there was a tree that lacked branches and foliage. Its shoots, bark, softwood, and heartwood would not grow to fullness.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dussīlassa sīlavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti avippaṭisāro;
segs.e: In the same way, an unethical person, who lacks ethics, has destroyed a vital condition for having no regrets.
When there are regrets, one who has regrets has destroyed a vital condition for joy. …
One who lacks disillusionment and dispassion has destroyed a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Sīlavato, bhikkhave, sīlasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti avippaṭisāro;
segs.e: An ethical person, who has fulfilled ethics, has fulfilled a vital condition for not having regrets.

segs.p: avippaṭisāre sati avippaṭisārasampannassa upanisasampannaṁ hoti pāmojjaṁ;
segs.e: When there are no regrets, one who has no regrets has fulfilled a vital condition for joy.

segs.p: pāmojje sati pāmojjasampannassa upanisasampannā hoti pīti;
segs.e: When there is joy, one who has fulfilled joy has fulfilled a vital condition for rapture.

segs.p: pītiyā sati pītisampannassa upanisasampannā hoti passaddhi;
segs.e: When there is rapture, one who has fulfilled rapture has fulfilled a vital condition for tranquility.

segs.p: passaddhiyā sati passaddhisampannassa upanisasampannaṁ hoti sukhaṁ;
segs.e: When there is tranquility, one who has fulfilled tranquility has fulfilled a vital condition for bliss.

segs.p: sukhe sati sukhasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti sammāsamādhi;
segs.e: When there is bliss, one who has fulfilled bliss has fulfilled a vital condition for right immersion.

segs.p: sammāsamādhimhi sati sammāsamādhisampannassa upanisasampannaṁ hoti yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṁ;
segs.e: When there is right immersion, one who has fulfilled right immersion has fulfilled a vital condition for true knowledge and vision.

segs.p: yathābhūtañāṇadassane sati yathābhūtañāṇadassanasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti nibbidāvirāgo;
segs.e: When there is true knowledge and vision, one who has fulfilled true knowledge and vision has fulfilled a vital condition for disillusionment and dispassion.

segs.p: nibbidāvirāge sati nibbidāvirāgasampannassa upanisasampannaṁ hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanaṁ.
segs.e: When there is disillusionment and dispassion, one who has fulfilled disillusionment and dispassion has fulfilled a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, rukkho sākhāpalāsasampanno. Tassa papaṭikāpi pāripūriṁ gacchati, tacopi … pheggupi … sāropi pāripūriṁ gacchati.
segs.e: Suppose there was a tree that was complete with branches and foliage. Its shoots, bark, softwood, and heartwood would grow to fullness.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, sīlavato sīlasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti avippaṭisāro;
segs.e: In the same way, an ethical person, who has fulfilled ethics, has fulfilled a vital condition for not having regrets.
When there are no regrets, one who has no regrets has fulfilled a vital condition for joy. …
One who has fulfilled disillusionment and dispassion has fulfilled a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.”

Numbered Discourses 10.6
1. Benefits
Immersion

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “siyā nu kho, bhante, bhikkhuno tathārūpo samādhipaṭilābho yathā neva pathaviyaṁ pathavisaññī assa, na āpasmiṁ āposaññī assa, na tejasmiṁ tejosaññī assa, na vāyasmiṁ vāyosaññī assa, na ākāsānañcāyatane ākāsānañcāyatanasaññī assa, na viññāṇañcāyatane viññāṇañcāyatanasaññī assa, na ākiñcaññāyatane ākiñcaññāyatanasaññī assa, na nevasaññānāsaññāyatane nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññī assa, na idhaloke idhalokasaññī assa, na paraloke paralokasaññī assa; saññī ca pana assā”ti?
segs.e: “Could it be, sir, that a mendicant might gain a state of immersion like this? They wouldn’t perceive earth in earth, water in water, fire in fire, or air in air. And they wouldn’t perceive the dimension of infinite space in the dimension of infinite space, the dimension of infinite consciousness in the dimension of infinite consciousness, the dimension of nothingness in the dimension of nothingness, or the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. And they wouldn’t perceive this world in this world, or the other world in the other world. And yet they would still perceive.”

segs.p: “Siyā, ānanda, bhikkhuno tathārūpo samādhipaṭilābho yathā neva pathaviyaṁ pathavisaññī assa, na āpasmiṁ āposaññī assa, na tejasmiṁ tejosaññī assa, na vāyasmiṁ vāyosaññī assa, na ākāsānañcāyatane ākāsānañcāyatanasaññī assa, na viññāṇañcāyatane viññāṇañcāyatanasaññī assa, na ākiñcaññāyatane ākiñcaññāyatanasaññī assa, na nevasaññānāsaññāyatane nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññī assa, na idhaloke idhalokasaññī assa, na paraloke paralokasaññī assa; saññī ca pana assā”ti.
segs.e: “It could be, Ānanda, that a mendicant might gain a state of immersion like this. They wouldn’t perceive earth in earth, water in water, fire in fire, or air in air. And they wouldn’t perceive the dimension of infinite space in the dimension of infinite space, the dimension of infinite consciousness in the dimension of infinite consciousness, the dimension of nothingness in the dimension of nothingness, or the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. And they wouldn’t perceive this world in this world, or the other world in the other world. And yet they would still perceive.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana, bhante, siyā bhikkhuno tathārūpo samādhipaṭilābho yathā neva pathaviyaṁ pathavisaññī assa, na āpasmiṁ āposaññī assa na tejasmiṁ tejosaññī assa, na vāyasmiṁ vāyosaññī assa, na ākāsānañcāyatane ākāsānañcāyatanasaññī assa, na viññāṇañcāyatane viññāṇañcāyatanasaññī assa, na ākiñcaññāyatane ākiñcaññāyatanasaññī assa, na nevasaññānāsaññāyatane nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññī assa, na idhaloke idhalokasaññī assa, na paraloke paralokasaññī assa; saññī ca pana assā”ti?
segs.e: “But how could this be, sir?”
“Ānanda, it’s when a mendicant perceives:

segs.p: ‘etaṁ santaṁ etaṁ paṇītaṁ yadidaṁ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānan’ti.
segs.e: ‘This is peaceful; this is sublime—that is, the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, ānanda, siyā bhikkhuno tathārūpo samādhipaṭilābho yathā neva pathaviyaṁ pathavisaññī assa, na āpasmiṁ āposaññī assa, na tejasmiṁ tejosaññī assa, na vāyasmiṁ vāyosaññī assa, na ākāsānañcāyatane ākāsānañcāyatanasaññī assa, na viññāṇañcāyatane viññāṇañcāyatanasaññī assa, na ākiñcaññāyatane ākiñcaññāyatanasaññī assa, na nevasaññānāsaññāyatane nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññī assa, na idhaloke idhalokasaññī assa, na paraloke paralokasaññī assa; saññī ca pana assā”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant might gain a state of immersion like this. They wouldn’t perceive earth in earth, water in water, fire in fire, or air in air. And they wouldn’t perceive the dimension of infinite space in the dimension of infinite space, the dimension of infinite consciousness in the dimension of infinite consciousness, the dimension of nothingness in the dimension of nothingness, or the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. And they wouldn’t perceive this world in this world, or the other world in the other world. And yet they would still perceive.”
Numbered Discourses 10.7
1. Benefits
Sāriputta

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to Sāriputta:

segs.p: “Siyā nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhuno tathārūpo samādhipaṭilābho yathā neva pathaviyaṁ pathavisaññī assa, na āpasmiṁ āposaññī assa, na tejasmiṁ tejosaññī assa, na vāyasmiṁ vāyosaññī assa, na ākāsānañcāyatane ākāsānañcāyatanasaññī assa, na viññāṇañcāyatane viññāṇañcāyatanasaññī assa, na ākiñcaññāyatane ākiñcaññāyatanasaññī assa, na nevasaññānāsaññāyatane nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññī assa, na idhaloke idhalokasaññī assa, na paraloke paralokasaññī assa; saññī ca pana assā”ti?
segs.e: “Could it be, reverend Sāriputta, that a mendicant might gain a state of immersion like this? They wouldn’t perceive earth in earth, water in water, fire in fire, or air in air. And they wouldn’t perceive the dimension of infinite space in the dimension of infinite space, the dimension of infinite consciousness in the dimension of infinite consciousness, the dimension of nothingness in the dimension of nothingness, or the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. And they wouldn’t perceive this world in this world, or the other world in the other world. And yet they would still perceive.”

segs.p: “Siyā, āvuso ānanda, bhikkhuno tathārūpo samādhipaṭilābho yathā neva pathaviyaṁ pathavisaññī assa …pe… na paraloke paralokasaññī assa; saññī ca pana assā”ti.
segs.e: “It could be, Reverend Ānanda.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana, āvuso sāriputta, siyā bhikkhuno tathārūpo samādhipaṭilābho yathā neva pathaviyaṁ pathavisaññī assa …pe… saññī ca pana assā”ti?
segs.e: “But how could this be?”

segs.p: “Ekamidāhaṁ, āvuso ānanda, samayaṁ idheva sāvatthiyaṁ viharāmi andhavanasmiṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend Ānanda, this one time I was staying right here at Sāvatthī in the Dark Forest.

segs.p: Tatthāhaṁ tathārūpaṁ samādhiṁ samāpajjiṁ yathā neva pathaviyaṁ pathavisaññī ahosiṁ, na āpasmiṁ āposaññī ahosiṁ, na tejasmiṁ tejosaññī ahosiṁ, na vāyasmiṁ vāyosaññī ahosiṁ, na ākāsānañcāyatane ākāsānañcāyatanasaññī ahosiṁ, na viññāṇañcāyatane viññāṇañcāyatanasaññī ahosiṁ, na ākiñcaññāyatane ākiñcaññāyatanasaññī ahosiṁ, na nevasaññānāsaññāyatane nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññī ahosiṁ, na idhaloke idhalokasaññī ahosiṁ, na paraloke paralokasaññī ahosiṁ; saññī ca pana ahosin”ti.
segs.e: There I gained a state of immersion like this. I didn’t perceive earth in earth, water in water, fire in fire, or air in air. And I didn’t perceive the dimension of infinite space in the dimension of infinite space, the dimension of infinite consciousness in the dimension of infinite consciousness, the dimension of nothingness in the dimension of nothingness, or the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. And I didn’t perceive this world in this world, or the other world in the other world. And yet I still perceived.”
“But at that time what did Reverend Sāriputta perceive?”

segs.p: “‘Bhavanirodho nibbānaṁ bhavanirodho nibbānan’ti kho me, āvuso, aññāva saññā uppajjati aññāva saññā nirujjhati.
segs.e: “One perception arose in me and another perception ceased: ‘The cessation of continued existence is extinguishment. The cessation of continued existence is extinguishment.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, sakalikaggissa jhāyamānassa aññāva acci uppajjati aññāva acci nirujjhati;
segs.e: Suppose there was a burning pile of twigs. One flame would arise and another would cease.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, ‘bhavanirodho nibbānaṁ bhavanirodho nibbānan’ti aññāva saññā uppajjati aññāva saññā nirujjhati.
segs.e: In the same way, one perception arose in me and another perception ceased: ‘The cessation of continued existence is extinguishment. The cessation of continued existence is extinguishment.’

segs.p: ‘Bhavanirodho nibbānan’ti saññī ca panāhaṁ, āvuso, tasmiṁ samaye ahosin”ti.
segs.e: At that time I perceived that the cessation of continued existence is extinguishment.”
Numbered Discourses 10.8
1. Benefits
Inspiring All Around: the Absorptions

segs.p: “Saddho ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hoti, no ca sīlavā;
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant is faithful but not ethical.
So they’re incomplete in that respect,
and should fulfill it, thinking:
‘How can I become faithful and ethical?’

segs.p: Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti sīlavā ca, evaṁ so tenaṅgena paripūro hoti.
segs.e: When the mendicant is faithful and ethical, they’re complete in that respect.

segs.p: Saddho ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hoti sīlavā ca, no ca bahussuto …pe…
segs.e: A mendicant is faithful and ethical, but not learned. …
they’re not a Dhamma speaker …
they don’t frequent assemblies …

segs.p: parisāvacaro ca, no ca visārado parisāya dhammaṁ deseti …
segs.e: they don’t teach Dhamma to the assembly with assurance …

segs.p: visārado ca parisāya dhammaṁ deseti, no ca vinayadharo …
segs.e: they’re not an expert in the monastic law …

segs.p: vinayadharo ca, no ca āraññiko pantasenāsano …
segs.e: they don’t stay in the wilderness, in remote lodgings …

segs.p: āraññiko ca pantasenāsano, no ca catunnaṁ jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī …
segs.e: they don’t get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty …

segs.p: catunnañca jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, no ca āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: they don’t realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.
So they’re incomplete in that respect,
and should fulfill it, thinking:

segs.p: ‘kintāhaṁ saddho ca assaṁ, sīlavā ca, bahussuto ca, dhammakathiko ca, parisāvacaro ca, visārado ca parisāya dhammaṁ deseyyaṁ, vinayadharo ca, āraññiko ca pantasenāsano, catunnañca jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī assaṁ akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyyan’ti.
segs.e: ‘How can I become faithful, ethical, and learned, a Dhamma speaker, one who frequents assemblies, one who teaches Dhamma to the assembly with assurance, an expert in the training, one who lives in the wilderness, in remote lodgings, one who gets the four absorptions when they want, and one who lives having realized the ending of defilements?’

segs.p: Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti, sīlavā ca, bahussuto ca, dhammakathiko ca, parisāvacaro ca, visārado ca parisāya dhammaṁ deseti, vinayadharo ca, āraññiko ca pantasenāsano, catunnañca jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati;
segs.e: When they’re faithful, ethical, and learned, a Dhamma speaker, one who frequents assemblies, one who teaches Dhamma to the assembly with assurance, an expert in the training, one who lives in the wilderness, in remote lodgings, one who gets the four absorptions when they want, and one who lives having realized the ending of defilements,
they’re complete in that respect.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu samantapāsādiko ca hoti sabbākāraparipūro cā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant who possesses these ten qualities is impressive all around, and is complete in every respect.”
Numbered Discourses 10.9

Inspiring All Around: the Peaceful Liberations

segs.p: “Saddho ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hoti, no ca sīlavā …pe…

they’re not learned. …
they’re not a Dhamma speaker …
they don’t frequent assemblies …

Numbered Discourses 10.10
1. Benefits
Inspiring All Around: the Three Knowledges

segs.p: “Saddho ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hoti, no ca sīlavā.
segs.e: “A mendicant is faithful, but not ethical.
So they’re incomplete in that respect,
and should fulfill it, thinking:
‘How can I become faithful and ethical?’

segs.p: Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti, sīlavā ca, evaṁ so tenaṅgena paripūro hoti.
segs.e: When the mendicant is faithful and ethical, they’re complete in that respect.

segs.e: A mendicant is faithful and ethical, but not learned …
they’re not a Dhamma speaker …

segs.e: they don’t frequent assemblies …

segs.p: no ca visārado parisāya dhammaṁ deseti visārado ca parisāya dhammaṁ deseti,
segs.e: they don’t teach Dhamma to the assembly with assurance …
they’re not an expert in the monastic law …

segs.e: they don’t recollect their many kinds of past lives …

segs.p: no ca dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena …pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti dibbena ca cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena …pe…

segs.e: they don’t realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.
So they’re incomplete in that respect,
and should fulfill it, thinking:

segs.p: ‘kintāhaṁ saddho ca assaṁ, sīlavā ca, bahussuto ca, dhammakathiko ca, parisāvacaro ca, visārado ca parisāya dhammaṁ deseyyaṁ, vinayadharo ca, anekavihitañca pubbenivāsaṁ anussareyyaṁ, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ dvepi jātiyo …pe… iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussareyyaṁ, dibbena ca cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena …pe… yathākammūpage satte pajāneyyaṁ, āsavānañca khayā …pe… sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyyan’ti.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti, sīlavā ca, bahussuto ca, dhammakathiko ca, parisāvacaro ca, visārado ca parisāya dhammaṁ deseti, vinayadharo ca, anekavihitañca pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ dvepi jātiyo …pe… iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati, dibbena ca cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena …pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti, āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
