segs.e: After giving up three things you can give up faithlessness, uncharitableness, and laziness.
What three?

segs.p: Anādariyaṁ pahāya, dovacassataṁ pahāya, pāpamittataṁ pahāya—
segs.e: Disregard, being hard to admonish, and having bad friends.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme pahāya bhabbo assaddhiyaṁ pahātuṁ avadaññutaṁ pahātuṁ kosajjaṁ pahātuṁ.
segs.e: After giving up these three things you can give up faithlessness, uncharitableness, and laziness.

segs.p: Tayome, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo anādariyaṁ pahātuṁ dovacassataṁ pahātuṁ pāpamittataṁ pahātuṁ.
segs.e: After giving up three things you can give up disregard, being hard to admonish, and having bad friends.
What three?

segs.p: Ahirikaṁ pahāya, anottappaṁ pahāya, pamādaṁ pahāya—
segs.e: Lack of conscience, imprudence, and negligence.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme pahāya bhabbo anādariyaṁ pahātuṁ dovacassataṁ pahātuṁ pāpamittataṁ pahātuṁ.
segs.e: After giving up these three things you can give up disregard, being hard to admonish, and having bad friends.
Mendicants, someone who has conscience and prudence is diligent.

segs.p: So appamatto samāno bhabbo anādariyaṁ pahātuṁ dovacassataṁ pahātuṁ pāpamittataṁ pahātuṁ.
segs.e: When you’re diligent you can give up disregard, being hard to admonish, and having bad friends.

segs.p: So kalyāṇamitto samāno bhabbo assaddhiyaṁ pahātuṁ avadaññutaṁ pahātuṁ kosajjaṁ pahātuṁ.
segs.e: When you’ve got good friends you can give up faithlessness, uncharitableness, and laziness.

segs.p: So āraddhavīriyo samāno bhabbo uddhaccaṁ pahātuṁ asaṁvaraṁ pahātuṁ dussilyaṁ pahātuṁ.
segs.e: When you’re energetic you can give up restlessness, lack of restraint, and unethical conduct.

segs.p: So sīlavā samāno bhabbo ariyānaṁ adassanakamyataṁ pahātuṁ ariyadhammassa asotukamyataṁ pahātuṁ upārambhacittataṁ pahātuṁ.
segs.e: When you’re ethical you can give up not wanting to see the noble ones, not wanting to hear the teaching of the noble ones, and a fault-finding mind.

segs.p: So anupārambhacitto samāno bhabbo muṭṭhassaccaṁ pahātuṁ asampajaññaṁ pahātuṁ cetaso vikkhepaṁ pahātuṁ.
segs.e: When you don’t have a fault-finding mind you can give up unmindfulness, lack of situational awareness, and a scattered mind.

segs.p: So avikkhittacitto samāno bhabbo ayonisomanasikāraṁ pahātuṁ kummaggasevanaṁ pahātuṁ cetaso līnattaṁ pahātuṁ.
segs.e: When your mind isn’t scattered you can give up irrational application of mind, following a wrong path, and mental sluggishness.

segs.p: So alīnacitto samāno bhabbo sakkāyadiṭṭhiṁ pahātuṁ vicikicchaṁ pahātuṁ sīlabbataparāmāsaṁ pahātuṁ.
segs.e: When your mind isn’t sluggish you can give up substantialist view, doubt, and misapprehension of precepts and observances.

segs.p: So avicikiccho samāno bhabbo rāgaṁ pahātuṁ dosaṁ pahātuṁ mohaṁ pahātuṁ.
segs.e: When you have no doubts you can give up greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: So rāgaṁ pahāya dosaṁ pahāya mohaṁ pahāya bhabbo jātiṁ pahātuṁ jaraṁ pahātuṁ maraṇaṁ pahātun”ti.
segs.e: After giving up greed, hate, and delusion you can give up rebirth, old age, and death.”
Numbered Discourses 10.77
8. If You Want
A Crow
“Mendicants, a crow possesses ten bad qualities.
What ten?

segs.p: Dhaṁsī ca, pagabbho ca, tintiṇo ca, mahagghaso ca, luddo ca, akāruṇiko ca, dubbalo ca, oravitā ca, muṭṭhassati ca, necayiko ca—
segs.e: They’re rude and impudent, gluttonous and voracious, cruel and pitiless, weak and raucous, unmindful and acquisitive.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi asaddhammehi samannāgato kāko.
segs.e: A crow possesses these ten bad qualities.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dasahi asaddhammehi samannāgato pāpabhikkhu.
segs.e: In the same way, a bad mendicant possesses these ten bad qualities.
What ten?

segs.p: Dhaṁsī ca, pagabbho ca, tintiṇo ca, mahagghaso ca, luddo ca, akāruṇiko ca, dubbalo ca, oravitā ca, muṭṭhassati ca, necayiko ca—
segs.e: They’re rude and impudent, gluttonous and voracious, cruel and pitiless, weak and raucous, unmindful and acquisitive.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi asaddhammehi samannāgato pāpabhikkhū”ti.
segs.e: A bad mendicant possesses these ten bad qualities.”
Numbered Discourses 10.78
8. If You Want
Jains
“Mendicants, Jain ascetics possess ten bad qualities.
What ten?
They’re faithless and
unethical,
without conscience
or prudence,
and devoted to untrue persons.
They glorify themselves and put others down.
They’re attached to their own views, holding them tight, and refusing to let go.
They’re deceptive,
with corrupt wishes
and bad friends.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi asaddhammehi samannāgatā nigaṇṭhā”ti.
segs.e: Jain ascetics possess these ten bad qualities.”
Numbered Discourses 10.79
8. If You Want
Grounds for Resentment
“Mendicants, there are ten grounds for resentment.
What ten?
Thinking: ‘They did wrong to me,’ you harbor resentment.
Thinking: ‘They are doing wrong to me’ …
‘They will do wrong to me’ …
‘They did wrong by someone I love’ …
‘They are doing wrong by someone I love’ …
‘They will do wrong by someone I love’ …
‘They helped someone I dislike’ …
‘They are helping someone I dislike’ …
Thinking: ‘They will help someone I dislike,’ you harbor resentment.
You get angry for no reason.
These are the ten grounds for resentment.”
Numbered Discourses 10.80
8. If You Want
Getting Rid of Resentment
“Mendicants, there are these ten ways to get rid of resentment.
What ten?

segs.p: ‘Anatthaṁ me acari, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti,
segs.e: Thinking: ‘They harmed me, but what can I possibly do?’ you get rid of resentment.

segs.p: ‘anatthaṁ me carati, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti,
segs.e: Thinking: ‘They are harming me …’ …

segs.p: ‘anatthaṁ me carissati, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti,
segs.e: ‘They will harm me …’ …
‘They harmed someone I love …’ …
‘They are harming someone I love …’

segs.p: carissati, taṁ kutettha labbhāti āghātaṁ paṭivineti, appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṁ acari …pe…
segs.e: ‘They will harm someone I love …’ … They helped someone I dislike …’ …
‘They are helping someone I dislike …’ …

segs.p: atthaṁ carissati, taṁ kutettha labbhāti āghātaṁ paṭivineti,
segs.e: Thinking: ‘They will help someone I dislike, but what can I possibly do?’ you get rid of resentment.
And you don’t get angry for no reason.
These are the ten ways of getting rid of resentment.”
Numbered Discourses 10.81
9. Senior Mendicants
With Bāhuna

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā campāyaṁ viharati gaggarāya pokkharaṇiyā tīre.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Campā on the banks of the Gaggarā Lotus Pond.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā vāhano yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā vāhano bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Bāhuna went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “katihi nu kho, bhante, dhammehi tathāgato nissaṭo visaṁyutto vippamutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharatī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, how many things has the Realized One escaped from, so that he lives detached, liberated, with mind free of boundaries?”

segs.p: “Dasahi kho, vāhana, dhammehi tathāgato nissaṭo visaṁyutto vippamutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharati.
segs.e: “Bāhuna, the Realized One has escaped from ten things, so that he lives detached, liberated, with mind free of boundaries.
What ten?

segs.p: Rūpena kho, vāhana, tathāgato nissaṭo visaṁyutto vippamutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharati,
segs.e: Form …
feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness …
rebirth …
old age …
death …
suffering …

segs.p: kilesehi kho, vāhana, tathāgato nissaṭo visaṁyutto vippamutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharati.
segs.e: defilements …

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, vāhana, uppalaṁ vā padumaṁ vā puṇḍarīkaṁ vā udake jātaṁ udake saṁvaḍḍhaṁ udakā paccuggamma ṭhitaṁ anupalittaṁ udakena;
segs.e: Suppose there was a blue water lily, or a pink or white lotus. Though it sprouted and grew in the water, it would rise up above the water and stand with no water clinging to it.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, vāhana, imehi dasahi dhammehi tathāgato nissaṭo visaṁyutto vippamutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharatī”ti.
segs.e: In the same way, the Realized One has escaped from ten things, so that he lives detached, liberated, with mind free of boundaries.”
Numbered Discourses 10.82
9. Senior Mendicants
With Ānanda

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘assaddho samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “Ānanda, it is quite impossible for a faithless mendicant to achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training.

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘dussīlo samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It is quite impossible for a mendicant who is unethical …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘appassuto samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: unlearned …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘dubbaco samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: hard to admonish …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘pāpamitto samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: with bad friends …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘kusīto samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: lazy …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘muṭṭhassati samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: unmindful …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘asantuṭṭho samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: lacking contentment …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘pāpiccho samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: of corrupt wishes …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘micchādiṭṭhiko samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: of wrong view to achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training.

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘imehi dasahi dhammehi samannāgato imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It is quite impossible for a mendicant with these ten qualities to achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training.

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘saddho samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It is quite possible for a faithful mendicant to achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training.

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘sīlavā samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It is quite possible for a mendicant who is ethical …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘bahussuto sutadharo samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: a learned memorizer …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘suvaco samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: easy to admonish …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘kalyāṇamitto samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: with good friends …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘āraddhavīriyo samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: energetic …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘upaṭṭhitassati samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: mindful …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘santuṭṭho samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: contented …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘appiccho samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: of few desires …

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘sammādiṭṭhiko samāno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: of right view to achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training.

segs.p: So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘imehi dasahi dhammehi samannāgato imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: It is quite possible for a mendicant with these ten qualities to achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training.”
Numbered Discourses 10.83
9. Senior Mendicants
With Puṇṇiya

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā puṇṇiyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā puṇṇiyo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Puṇṇiya went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo yena appekadā tathāgataṁ dhammadesanā paṭibhāti appekadā nappaṭibhātī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why sometimes the Realized One feels inspired to teach, and other times not?”

segs.p: “Saddho ca, puṇṇiya, bhikkhu hoti, no ca upasaṅkamitā; neva tāva tathāgataṁ dhammadesanā paṭibhāti.
segs.e: “Puṇṇiya, when a mendicant has faith but doesn’t approach, the Realized One doesn’t feel inspired to teach.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, puṇṇiya, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti upasaṅkamitā ca, evaṁ tathāgataṁ dhammadesanā paṭibhāti.
segs.e: But when a mendicant has faith and approaches, the Realized One feels inspired to teach.

segs.p: Saddho ca, puṇṇiya, bhikkhu hoti upasaṅkamitā ca, no ca payirupāsitā …pe…
segs.e: When a mendicant has faith and approaches, but doesn’t pay homage …
they pay homage, but don’t ask questions …

segs.p: paripucchitā ca, no ca ohitasoto dhammaṁ suṇāti …
segs.e: they ask questions, but don’t actively listen to the teaching …

segs.p: ohitasoto ca dhammaṁ suṇāti, no ca sutvā dhammaṁ dhāreti …
segs.e: they actively listen to the teaching, but don’t remember the teaching they’ve heard …

segs.p: sutvā ca dhammaṁ dhāreti, no ca dhātānaṁ dhammānaṁ atthaṁ upaparikkhati …
segs.e: they remember the teaching they’ve heard, but don’t examine the meaning of the teachings they’ve remembered …

segs.p: dhātānañca dhammānaṁ atthaṁ upaparikkhati no ca atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammappaṭipanno hoti …
segs.e: they examine the meaning of the teachings they’ve remembered, but, not having understood the meaning and the teaching, they don’t practice in line with the principle of the teaching …

segs.p: atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammappaṭipanno ca hoti, no ca kalyāṇavāco hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagaḷāya atthassa viññāpaniyā …
segs.e: they practice in line with the teaching, but they’re not a good speaker and do not enunciate well. Their voice is not polished, clear, articulate, and doesn’t express the meaning …

segs.p: kalyāṇavāco ca hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagaḷāya atthassa viññāpaniyā, no ca sandassako hoti samādapako samuttejako sampahaṁsako sabrahmacārīnaṁ, neva tāva tathāgataṁ dhammadesanā paṭibhāti.
segs.e: They’re a good speaker who enunciates well, but they don’t educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire their spiritual companions. The Realized One doesn’t feel inspired to teach.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, puṇṇiya, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti, upasaṅkamitā ca, payirupāsitā ca, paripucchitā ca, ohitasoto ca dhammaṁ suṇāti, sutvā ca dhammaṁ dhāreti, dhātānañca dhammānaṁ atthaṁ upaparikkhati, atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammappaṭipanno ca hoti, kalyāṇavāco ca hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagaḷāya atthassa viññāpaniyā, sandassako ca hoti samādapako samuttejako sampahaṁsako sabrahmacārīnaṁ—
segs.e: But when a mendicant has faith, approaches, pays homage, asks questions, actively listens to the teachings, remembers the teachings, examines the meaning, practices in line with the principle of the teaching, has a good voice, and encourages their spiritual companions,
the Realized One feels inspired to teach.

segs.p: Imehi kho, puṇṇiya, dasahi dhammehi samannāgatā ekantapaṭibhānā tathāgataṁ dhammadesanā hotī”ti.
segs.e: When someone possesses these ten qualities, the Realized One feels totally inspired to teach.”
Numbered Discourses 10.84
9. Senior Mendicants
Declaration

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There Venerable Mahāmoggallāna addressed the mendicants:
“Reverends, mendicants!”

segs.p: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend,” they replied.
Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this:
“Take a mendicant who declares enlightenment:

segs.p: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo samanuyuñjati samanuggāhati samanubhāsati.
segs.e: They’re pursued, pressed, and grilled by the Realized One, or by one of his disciples who is a meditator skilled in attainments, in the minds of others, and in encompassing another’s mind.

segs.p: So tathāgatena vā tathāgatasāvakena vā jhāyinā samāpattikusalena paracittakusalena paracittapariyāyakusalena samanuyuñjiyamāno samanuggāhiyamāno samanubhāsiyamāno irīṇaṁ āpajjati vicinaṁ āpajjati anayaṁ āpajjati byasanaṁ āpajjati anayabyasanaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: Grilled in this way they get stuck or lose their way. They fall to ruin and disaster.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca manasi karoti:
segs.e: The Realized One or one of his disciples encompasses their mind and investigates:
‘Why does this venerable declare enlightenment, saying:

segs.p: khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti?
segs.e: “I understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place’”?’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti:
segs.e: They understand:
‘This venerable gets irritable,
and often lives with a heart full of anger.

segs.p: Kodhapariyuṭṭhānaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
segs.e: But being full of anger means decline in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.
This venerable is acrimonious …

segs.p: Upanāhapariyuṭṭhānaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: prone to disdain …

segs.p: Makkhapariyuṭṭhānaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: contemptuous …

segs.p: Paḷāsapariyuṭṭhānaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: jealous …

segs.p: Issāpariyuṭṭhānaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: stingy …

segs.p: Maccherapariyuṭṭhānaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: devious …

segs.p: Sāṭheyyapariyuṭṭhānaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: deceitful …

segs.p: Māyāpariyuṭṭhānaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: This venerable has corrupt wishes,
and often lives with a heart full of desire.

segs.p: Icchāpariyuṭṭhānaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
segs.e: But being full of desire means decline in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.

segs.p: Sati kho pana ayamāyasmā uttari karaṇīye oramattakena visesādhigamena antarā vosānaṁ āpanno.
segs.e: When there is still more to be done, this venerable stopped half-way after achieving some trifling distinction.

segs.p: Antarā vosānagamanaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ’.
segs.e: But stopping half-way means decline in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.’

segs.p: So vatāvuso, bhikkhu ‘ime dasa dhamme appahāya imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It is quite impossible for a mendicant to achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training without giving up these ten qualities.

segs.p: So vatāvuso, bhikkhu ‘ime dasa dhamme pahāya imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: It is quite possible for a mendicant to achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training after giving up these ten qualities.”
Numbered Discourses 10.85
9. Senior Mendicants
A Boaster

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā mahācundo cetīsu viharati sahajātiyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Mahācunda was staying in the land of the Cetīs at Sahajāti.

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā mahācundo bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There he addressed the mendicants:
“Reverends, mendicants!”

segs.p: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahācundassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend,” they replied.
Venerable Mahācunda said this:
“Take a mendicant who boasts and brags about their achievements:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ catutthaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipī’ti.
segs.e: ‘I enter and emerge from the first absorption, the second absorption, the third absorption, and the fourth absorption. And I enter and emerge from the dimensions of infinite space, infinite consciousness, nothingness, and neither perception nor non-perception. And I enter and emerge from the cessation of perception and feeling.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo samanuyuñjati samanuggāhati samanubhāsati.
segs.e: They’re pursued, pressed, and grilled by the Realized One, or by one of his disciples who has the absorptions, and is skilled in attainments, in the minds of others, and in encompassing another’s mind.

segs.p: So tathāgatena vā tathāgatasāvakena vā jhāyinā samāpattikusalena paracittakusalena paracittapariyāyakusalena samanuyuñjiyamāno samanuggāhiyamāno samanubhāsiyamāno irīṇaṁ āpajjati vicinaṁ āpajjati anayaṁ āpajjati byasanaṁ āpajjati anayabyasanaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: Grilled in this way they get stuck or lose their way. They fall to ruin and disaster.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca manasi karoti:
segs.e: The Realized One or one of his disciples encompasses their mind and investigates:

segs.p: ‘kiṁ nu kho ayamāyasmā katthī hoti vikatthī adhigamesu—
segs.e: ‘Why does this venerable boast and brag about their achievements, saying,
“I enter and emerge from the first absorption …
and the cessation of perception and feeling.”’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti:
segs.e: They understand,

segs.p: ‘Dīgharattaṁ kho ayamāyasmā khaṇḍakārī chiddakārī sabalakārī kammāsakārī na santatakārī na santatavutti sīlesu.
segs.e: ‘For a long time this venerable’s deeds have been broken, tainted, spotty, and marred. Their deeds and behavior are inconsistent.
This venerable is unethical,

segs.p: Dussilyaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
segs.e: and unethical conduct means decline in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.
This venerable is unfaithful,

segs.p: assaddhiyaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
segs.e: and lack of faith means decline …
This venerable is unlearned and unpracticed,

segs.p: appasaccaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
segs.e: and lack of learning means decline …
This venerable is hard to admonish,

segs.p: dovacassatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
segs.e: and being hard to admonish means decline …
This venerable has bad friends,

segs.p: pāpamittatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
segs.e: and bad friends mean decline …
This venerable is lazy,

segs.p: kosajjaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
segs.e: and laziness means decline …
This venerable is unmindful,

segs.p: muṭṭhassaccaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
segs.e: and unmindfulness means decline …
This venerable is deceptive,

segs.p: kohaññaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
segs.e: and deceitfulness means decline …
This venerable is burdensome,

segs.p: dubbharatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
segs.e: and being burdensome means decline …
This venerable is witless,

segs.p: duppaññatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ’.
segs.e: and lack of wisdom means decline in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, sahāyako sahāyakaṁ evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Suppose one friend was to say to another:

segs.p: ‘yadā te, samma, dhanena dhanakaraṇīyaṁ assa, yāceyyāsi maṁ dhanaṁ. Dassāmi te dhanan’ti.
segs.e: ‘My dear, when you need money for some payment, just ask me and I’ll give it.’

segs.p: So kiñcideva dhanakaraṇīye samuppanne sahāyako sahāyakaṁ evaṁ vadeyya: ‘attho me, samma, dhanena. Dehi me dhanan’ti.
segs.e: Then when some payment falls due, that friend says to their friend: ‘I need some money, my dear. Give me some.’
They’d say:

segs.p: ‘tena hi, samma, idha khanāhī’ti. So tatra khananto nādhigaccheyya.
segs.e: ‘Well then, my dear, dig here.’ So they dig there, but don’t find anything.
They’d say:

segs.p: ‘alikaṁ maṁ, samma, avaca; tucchakaṁ maṁ, samma, avaca—idha khanāhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘You lied to me, my dear, you spoke hollow words when you told me to dig here.’
They’d say:

segs.p: ‘nāhaṁ taṁ, samma, alikaṁ avacaṁ, tucchakaṁ avacaṁ. Tena hi, samma, idha khanāhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘My dear, I didn’t lie or speak hollow words. Well then, dig here.’
So they dig there as well, but don’t find anything.
They’d say:

segs.p: ‘alikaṁ maṁ, samma, avaca, tucchakaṁ maṁ, samma, avaca—idha khanāhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘You lied to me, my dear, you spoke hollow words when you said dig here.’
They’d say:

segs.p: ‘nāhaṁ taṁ, samma, alikaṁ avacaṁ, tucchakaṁ avacaṁ. Tena hi, samma, idha khanāhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘My dear, I didn’t lie or speak hollow words. Well then, dig here.’
So they dig there as well, but don’t find anything.
They’d say:

segs.p: ‘alikaṁ maṁ, samma, avaca, tucchakaṁ maṁ, samma, avaca—idha khanāhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘You lied to me, my dear, you spoke hollow words when you said dig here.’
They’d say:

segs.p: ‘nāhaṁ taṁ, samma, alikaṁ avacaṁ, tucchakaṁ avacaṁ. Api ca ahameva ummādaṁ pāpuṇiṁ cetaso vipariyāyan’ti.
segs.e: ‘My dear, I didn’t lie or speak hollow words. But I had gone mad, I was out of my mind.’

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu katthī hoti vikatthī adhigamesu:
segs.e: In the same way, take a mendicant who boasts and brags about their achievements:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ catutthaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṁ saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipī’ti.
segs.e: ‘I enter and emerge from the first absorption … and the cessation of perception and feeling.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo samanuyuñjati samanuggāhati samanubhāsati.
segs.e: They’re pursued, pressed, and grilled by the Realized One, or by one of his disciples …

segs.p: So tathāgatena vā tathāgatasāvakena vā jhāyinā samāpattikusalena paracittakusalena paracittapariyāyakusalena samanuyuñjiyamāno samanuggāhiyamāno samanubhāsiyamāno irīṇaṁ āpajjati vicinaṁ āpajjati anayaṁ āpajjati byasanaṁ āpajjati anayabyasanaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: Grilled in this way they get stuck or lose their way. They fall to ruin and disaster.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca manasi karoti:
segs.e: The Realized One or one of his disciples encompasses their mind and investigates:

segs.p: ‘kiṁ nu kho ayamāyasmā katthī hoti vikatthī adhigamesu—
segs.e: ‘Why does this venerable boast and brag about their achievements, saying,
“I enter and emerge from the first absorption …
and the cessation of perception and feeling.”’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti:
segs.e: They understand,

segs.p: ‘Dīgharattaṁ kho ayamāyasmā khaṇḍakārī chiddakārī sabalakārī kammāsakārī, na santatakārī na santatavutti sīlesu.
segs.e: ‘For a long time this venerable’s deeds have been broken, tainted, spotty, and marred. Their deeds and behavior are inconsistent.
This venerable is unethical,

segs.p: dussilyaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
segs.e: and unethical conduct means decline in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.
This venerable is unfaithful …

segs.p: assaddhiyaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: unlearned and unpracticed …

segs.p: appasaccaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: hard to admonish …

segs.p: dovacassatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: with bad friends …

segs.p: pāpamittatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: lazy …

segs.p: kosajjaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: unmindful …

segs.p: muṭṭhassaccaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: deceptive …

segs.p: kohaññaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: burdensome …

segs.p: dubbharatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: This venerable is witless,

segs.p: duppaññatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ’.
segs.e: and lack of wisdom means decline in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.’

segs.p: So vatāvuso, bhikkhu ‘ime dasa dhamme appahāya imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It is quite impossible for a mendicant to achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training without giving up these ten qualities.

segs.p: So vatāvuso, bhikkhu ‘ime dasa dhamme pahāya imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: It is quite possible for a mendicant to achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training after giving up these ten qualities.”
Numbered Discourses 10.86
9. Senior Mendicants
Overestimation

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā mahākassapo rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Mahākassapa was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā mahākassapo bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There he addressed the mendicants:
“Reverends, mendicants!”

segs.p: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahākassapassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend,” they replied.
Venerable Mahākassapa said this:
“Take a mendicant who declares enlightenment:

segs.p: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo samanuyuñjati samanuggāhati samanubhāsati.
segs.e: They’re pursued, pressed, and grilled by the Realized One, or by one of his disciples who has the absorptions, and is skilled in attainments, in the minds of others, and in encompassing another’s mind.

segs.p: So tathāgatena vā tathāgatasāvakena vā jhāyinā samāpattikusalena paracittakusalena paracittapariyāyakusalena samanuyuñjiyamāno samanuggāhiyamāno samanubhāsiyamāno irīṇaṁ āpajjati vicinaṁ āpajjati anayaṁ āpajjati byasanaṁ āpajjati anayabyasanaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: Grilled in this way they get stuck or lose their way. They fall to ruin and disaster.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca manasi karoti:
segs.e: The Realized One or one of his disciples encompasses their mind and investigates:
‘Why does this venerable declare enlightenment, saying,

segs.p: khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.
segs.e: “I understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place’”?’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti:
segs.e: They understand,

segs.p: ‘Adhimāniko kho ayamāyasmā adhimānasacco, appatte pattasaññī, akate katasaññī, anadhigate adhigatasaññī.
segs.e: ‘This venerable overestimates themselves and takes that to be the truth. They perceive that they’ve attained what they haven’t attained, done what they haven’t done, and achieved what they haven’t achieved.
And they declare enlightenment out of overestimation:

segs.p: khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.
segs.e: “I understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca manasi karoti:
segs.e: The Realized One or one of his disciples encompasses their mind and investigates:

segs.p: ‘kiṁ nu kho ayamāyasmā nissāya adhimāniko adhimānasacco, appatte pattasaññī, akate katasaññī, anadhigate adhigatasaññī.
segs.e: ‘Why does this venerable overestimate themselves and take that to be the truth? Why do they perceive that they’ve attained what they haven’t attained, done what they haven’t done, and achieved what they haven’t achieved?
And why do they declare enlightenment out of overestimation:

segs.p: khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.
segs.e: “I understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti:
segs.e: They understand,

segs.p: ‘Bahussuto kho pana ayamāyasmā sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
segs.e: ‘This venerable is very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

segs.p: Tasmā ayamāyasmā adhimāniko adhimānasacco, appatte pattasaññī, akate katasaññī, anadhigate adhigatasaññī.
segs.e: Therefore this venerable overestimates themselves and takes that to be the truth. …’

segs.p: khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.
Tamenaṁ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti:
segs.e: They understand,
‘This venerable is covetous,
and often lives with a heart full of covetousness.

segs.p: Abhijjhāpariyuṭṭhānaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
segs.e: But being full of covetousness means decline in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.
This venerable has ill will …

segs.p: Byāpādapariyuṭṭhānaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: dullness and drowsiness …

segs.p: Thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhānaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: restlessness …

segs.p: Uddhaccapariyuṭṭhānaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.

segs.e: doubt …

segs.p: Vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
Kammārāmo kho pana ayamāyasmā kammarato kammārāmataṁ anuyutto.
segs.e: This venerable relishes work. They love it and like to relish it …

segs.p: Kammārāmatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
Bhassārāmo kho pana ayamāyasmā bhassarato bhassārāmataṁ anuyutto.
segs.e: This venerable relishes talk …

segs.p: Bhassārāmatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
Niddārāmo kho pana ayamāyasmā niddārato niddārāmataṁ anuyutto.
segs.e: sleep …

segs.p: Niddārāmatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
Saṅgaṇikārāmo kho pana ayamāyasmā saṅgaṇikarato saṅgaṇikārāmataṁ anuyutto.
segs.e: company …

segs.p: Saṅgaṇikārāmatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ.
Sati kho pana ayamāyasmā uttari karaṇīye oramattakena visesādhigamena antarā vosānaṁ āpanno.
segs.e: When there is still more to be done, this venerable stopped half-way after achieving some trifling distinction.

segs.p: Antarā vosānagamanaṁ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṁ’.
segs.e: But stopping half-way means decline in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.’

segs.p: So vatāvuso, bhikkhu ‘ime dasa dhamme appahāya imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: It is quite impossible for a mendicant to achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training without giving up these ten qualities.

segs.p: So vatāvuso, bhikkhu ‘ime dasa dhamme pahāya imasmiṁ dhammavinaye vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: It is quite possible for a mendicant to achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training after giving up these ten qualities.”
Numbered Discourses 10.87
9. Senior Mendicants
Disciplinary Issues

segs.p: Tatra kho bhagavā kālaṅkataṁ bhikkhuṁ ārabbha bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants concerning the mendicant Kalandaka:
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu adhikaraṇiko hoti, adhikaraṇasamathassa na vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: “Firstly, a mendicant raises disciplinary issues and doesn’t praise the settling of disciplinary issues.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu adhikaraṇiko hoti adhikaraṇasamathassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This quality doesn’t conduce to fondness, respect, esteem, harmony, and unity.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na sikkhākāmo hoti, sikkhāsamādānassa na vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is not eager to train, and doesn’t praise taking up the training. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na sikkhākāmo hoti sikkhāsamādānassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pāpiccho hoti, icchāvinayassa na vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant has corrupt wishes, and doesn’t praise getting rid of wishes. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pāpiccho hoti icchāvinayassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kodhano hoti, kodhavinayassa na vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is irritable, and doesn’t praise getting rid of anger. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kodhano hoti kodhavinayassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu makkhī hoti, makkhavinayassa na vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant denigrates others, and doesn’t praise getting rid of denigration. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu makkhī hoti makkhavinayassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṭho hoti, sāṭheyyavinayassa na vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is devious, and doesn’t praise getting rid of deviousness. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṭho hoti sāṭheyyavinayassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu māyāvī hoti, māyāvinayassa na vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is deceitful, and doesn’t praise getting rid of deceitfulness. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu māyāvī hoti māyāvinayassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammānaṁ na nisāmakajātiko hoti, dhammanisantiyā na vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant doesn’t pay attention to the teachings, and doesn’t praise attending to the teachings. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammānaṁ na nisāmakajātiko hoti dhammanisantiyā na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na paṭisallīno hoti, paṭisallānassa na vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is not in retreat, and doesn’t praise retreat. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na paṭisallīno hoti paṭisallānassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ na paṭisanthārako hoti, paṭisanthārakassa na vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is inhospitable to their spiritual companions, and doesn’t praise hospitality.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ na paṭisanthārako hoti paṭisanthārakassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This quality doesn’t conduce to fondness, respect, esteem, harmony, and unity.

segs.p: Evarūpassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno kiñcāpi evaṁ icchā uppajjeyya:
segs.e: Even though a mendicant such as this might wish:

segs.p: ‘aho vata maṁ sabrahmacārī sakkareyyuṁ garuṁ kareyyuṁ māneyyuṁ pūjeyyun’ti, atha kho naṁ sabrahmacārī na ceva sakkaronti na garuṁ karonti na mānenti na pūjenti.
segs.e: ‘If only my spiritual companions would honor, respect, esteem, and venerate me!’ Still they don’t honor, respect, esteem, and venerate them.
Why is that?

segs.p: Tathāhissa, bhikkhave, viññū sabrahmacārī te pāpake akusale dhamme appahīne samanupassanti.
segs.e: Because their sensible spiritual companions see that they haven’t given up those bad unskillful qualities.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, assakhaḷuṅkassa kiñcāpi evaṁ icchā uppajjeyya:
segs.e: Suppose a wild colt was to wish:

segs.p: ‘aho vata maṁ manussā ājānīyaṭṭhāne ṭhapeyyuṁ, ājānīyabhojanañca bhojeyyuṁ, ājānīyaparimajjanañca parimajjeyyun’ti, atha kho naṁ manussā na ceva ājānīyaṭṭhāne ṭhapenti na ca ājānīyabhojanaṁ bhojenti na ca ājānīyaparimajjanaṁ parimajjanti.
segs.e: ‘If only the humans would put me in a thoroughbred’s place, feed me a thoroughbred’s food, and give me a thoroughbred’s grooming.’ Still the humans wouldn’t put them in a thoroughbred’s place, feed them a thoroughbred’s food, or give them a thoroughbred’s grooming.
Why is that?

segs.p: Tathāhissa, bhikkhave, viññū manussā tāni sāṭheyyāni kūṭeyyāni jimheyyāni vaṅkeyyāni appahīnāni samanupassanti.
segs.e: Because sensible humans see that they haven’t given up their tricks, bluffs, ruses, and feints.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, evarūpassa bhikkhuno kiñcāpi evaṁ icchā uppajjeyya:
segs.e: In the same way, even though a mendicant such as this might wish:

segs.p: ‘aho vata maṁ sabrahmacārī sakkareyyuṁ garuṁ kareyyuṁ māneyyuṁ pūjeyyun’ti, atha kho naṁ sabrahmacārī na ceva sakkaronti na garuṁ karonti na mānenti na pūjenti.
segs.e: ‘If only my spiritual companions would honor, respect, esteem, and venerate me!’ Still they don’t honor, respect, esteem, and venerate them.
Why is that?

segs.p: Tathāhissa, bhikkhave, viññū sabrahmacārī te pāpake akusale dhamme appahīne samanupassanti.
segs.e: Because their sensible spiritual companions see that they haven’t given up those bad unskillful qualities.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na adhikaraṇiko hoti, adhikaraṇasamathassa vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Next, a mendicant doesn’t raise disciplinary issues and praises the settling of disciplinary issues.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na adhikaraṇiko hoti adhikaraṇasamathassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo piyatāya garutāya bhāvanāya sāmaññāya ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This quality conduces to fondness, respect, esteem, harmony, and unity.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sikkhākāmo hoti, sikkhāsamādānassa vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is eager to train, and praises taking up the training. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sikkhākāmo hoti sikkhāsamādānassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo piyatāya garutāya bhāvanāya sāmaññāya ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appiccho hoti, icchāvinayassa vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant has few desires, and praises getting rid of desires. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appiccho hoti icchāvinayassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo …pe… ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akkodhano hoti, kodhavinayassa vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is not irritable, and praises getting rid of anger. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akkodhano hoti kodhavinayassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo …pe… ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu amakkhī hoti, makkhavinayassa vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant doesn’t denigrate others, and praises getting rid of denigration. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu amakkhī hoti makkhavinayassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo …pe… ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asaṭho hoti, sāṭheyyavinayassa vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant isn’t devious, and praises getting rid of deviousness. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asaṭho hoti sāṭheyyavinayassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo …pe… ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu amāyāvī hoti, māyāvinayassa vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant isn’t deceitful, and praises getting rid of deceitfulness. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu amāyāvī hoti māyāvinayassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo …pe… ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammānaṁ nisāmakajātiko hoti, dhammanisantiyā vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant pays attention to the teachings, and praises attending to the teachings. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammānaṁ nisāmakajātiko hoti dhammanisantiyā vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo …pe… ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisallīno hoti, paṭisallānassa vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is in retreat, and praises retreat. …

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisallīno hoti paṭisallānassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo …pe… ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ paṭisanthārako hoti, paṭisanthārakassa vaṇṇavādī.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is hospitable to their spiritual companions, and praises hospitality.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ paṭisanthārako hoti paṭisanthārakassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo piyatāya garutāya bhāvanāya sāmaññāya ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This quality conduces to fondness, respect, esteem, harmony, and unity.

segs.p: Evarūpassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno kiñcāpi na evaṁ icchā uppajjeyya:
segs.e: Even though a mendicant such as this might never wish:

segs.p: ‘aho vata maṁ sabrahmacārī sakkareyyuṁ garuṁ kareyyuṁ māneyyuṁ pūjeyyun’ti, atha kho naṁ sabrahmacārī sakkaronti garuṁ karonti mānenti pūjenti.
segs.e: ‘If only my spiritual companions would honor, respect, esteem, and venerate me!’ Still they honor, respect, esteem, and venerate them.
Why is that?

segs.p: Tathāhissa, bhikkhave, viññū sabrahmacārī te pāpake akusale dhamme pahīne samanupassanti.
segs.e: Because their sensible spiritual companions see that they’ve given up those bad unskillful qualities.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, bhaddassa assājānīyassa kiñcāpi na evaṁ icchā uppajjeyya:
segs.e: Suppose a fine thoroughbred never wished:

segs.p: ‘aho vata maṁ manussā ājānīyaṭṭhāne ṭhapeyyuṁ, ājānīyabhojanañca bhojeyyuṁ, ājānīyaparimajjanañca parimajjeyyun’ti, atha kho naṁ manussā ājānīyaṭṭhāne ca ṭhapenti ājānīyabhojanañca bhojenti ājānīyaparimajjanañca parimajjanti.
segs.e: ‘If only the humans would put me in a thoroughbred’s place, feed me a thoroughbred’s food, and give me a thoroughbred’s grooming.’ Still the humans would put them in a thoroughbred’s place, feed them a thoroughbred’s food, and give them a thoroughbred’s grooming.
Why is that?

segs.p: Tathāhissa, bhikkhave, viññū manussā tāni sāṭheyyāni kūṭeyyāni jimheyyāni vaṅkeyyāni pahīnāni samanupassanti.
segs.e: Because sensible humans see that they’ve given up their tricks, bluffs, ruses, and feints.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, evarūpassa bhikkhuno kiñcāpi na evaṁ icchā uppajjeyya:
segs.e: In the same way, even though a mendicant such as this might never wish:

segs.p: ‘aho vata maṁ sabrahmacārī sakkareyyuṁ garuṁ kareyyuṁ māneyyuṁ pūjeyyun’ti, atha kho naṁ sabrahmacārī sakkaronti garuṁ karonti mānenti pūjenti.
segs.e: ‘If only my spiritual companions would honor, respect, esteem, and venerate me!’ Still they honor, respect, esteem, and venerate them.
Why is that?

segs.p: Tathāhissa, bhikkhave, viññū sabrahmacārī te pāpake akusale dhamme pahīne samanupassantī”ti.
segs.e: Because their sensible spiritual companions see that they’ve given up those bad unskillful qualities.”
Numbered Discourses 10.88
9. Senior Mendicants
An Abuser

segs.p: “Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akkosakaparibhāsako ariyūpavādī sabrahmacārīnaṁ ṭhānametaṁ avakāso yaṁ so dasannaṁ byasanānaṁ aññataraṁ byasanaṁ nigaccheyya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, any mendicant who abuses and insults their spiritual companions, denouncing the noble ones, will, without a doubt, fall into one or other of these ten disasters.
What ten?

segs.p: Anadhigataṁ nādhigacchati, adhigatā parihāyati, saddhammassa na vodāyanti, saddhammesu vā adhimāniko hoti anabhirato vā brahmacariyaṁ carati, aññataraṁ vā saṅkiliṭṭhaṁ āpattiṁ āpajjati, gāḷhaṁ vā rogātaṅkaṁ phusati, ummādaṁ vā pāpuṇāti cittakkhepaṁ, sammūḷho kālaṁ karoti, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: They don’t achieve the unachieved. What they have achieved falls away. They don’t refine their good qualities. They overestimate their good qualities. Or they lead the spiritual life dissatisfied. Or they commit a corrupt offense. Or they contract a severe illness. Or they go mad and lose their mind. They feel lost when they die. And when their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akkosakaparibhāsako ariyūpavādī sabrahmacārīnaṁ, ṭhānametaṁ avakāso yaṁ so imesaṁ dasannaṁ byasanānaṁ aññataraṁ byasanaṁ nigaccheyyā”ti.
segs.e: Any mendicant who abuses and insults their spiritual companions, denouncing the noble ones, will, without a doubt, fall into one or other of these ten disasters.”
Numbered Discourses 10.89
9. Senior Mendicants
With Kokālika

segs.p: Atha kho kokāliko bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho kokāliko bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the mendicant Kokālika went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “pāpicchā, bhante, sāriputtamoggallānā, pāpikānaṁ icchānaṁ vasaṁ gatā”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, Sāriputta and Moggallāna have corrupt wishes. They’ve fallen under the sway of corrupt wishes.”
“Don’t say that, Kokālika! Don’t say that, Kokālika!
Have confidence in Sāriputta and Moggallāna,
they’re good monks.”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho kokāliko bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a second time Kokālika said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “kiñcāpi me, bhante, bhagavā saddhāyiko paccayiko, atha kho pāpicchāva sāriputtamoggallānā, pāpikānaṁ icchānaṁ vasaṁ gatā”ti.
segs.e: “Despite my faith and trust in the Buddha, Sāriputta and Moggallāna have corrupt wishes. They’ve fallen under the sway of corrupt wishes.”
“Don’t say that, Kokālika! Don’t say that, Kokālika!
Have confidence in Sāriputta and Moggallāna,
they’re good monks.”

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho kokāliko bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a third time Kokālika said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “kiñcāpi me, bhante, bhagavā saddhāyiko paccayiko, atha kho pāpicchāva sāriputtamoggallānā, pāpikānaṁ icchānaṁ vasaṁ gatā”ti.
segs.e: “Despite my faith and trust in the Buddha, Sāriputta and Moggallāna have corrupt wishes. They’ve fallen under the sway of corrupt wishes.”
“Don’t say that, Kokālika! Don’t say that, Kokālika!
Have confidence in Sāriputta and Moggallāna,
they’re good monks.”

segs.p: Atha kho kokāliko bhikkhu uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then Kokālika rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Acirapakkantassa ca kokālikassa bhikkhuno sāsapamattīhi pīḷakāhi sabbo kāyo phuṭo ahosi.
segs.e: Not long after he left his body erupted with boils the size of mustard seeds.

segs.p: Sāsapamattiyo hutvā muggamattiyo ahesuṁ, muggamattiyo hutvā kalāyamattiyo ahesuṁ, kalāyamattiyo hutvā kolaṭṭhimattiyo ahesuṁ, kolaṭṭhimattiyo hutvā kolamattiyo ahesuṁ, kolamattiyo hutvā āmalakamattiyo ahesuṁ, āmalakamattiyo hutvā tiṇḍukamattiyo ahesuṁ, tiṇḍukamattiyo hutvā, beḷuvasalāṭukamattiyo ahesuṁ, beḷuvasalāṭukamattiyo hutvā billamattiyo ahesuṁ, billamattiyo hutvā pabhijjiṁsu, pubbañca lohitañca pagghariṁsu.
segs.e: The boils grew to the size of mung beans, then chickpeas, then jujube seeds, then jujubes, then myrobalans, then unripe wood-apples, then ripe wood-apples. Finally they burst open, and pus and blood oozed out.

segs.p: So sudaṁ kadalipattesu seti macchova visagilito.
segs.e: He just laid down on banana leaves like a poisoned fish.

segs.p: Atha kho turū paccekabrahmā yena kokāliko bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā vehāse ṭhatvā kokālikaṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Tudu the independent divinity went to Kokālika, and standing in the air he said to him,
“Kokālika, have confidence in Sāriputta and Moggallāna,
they’re good monks.”
“Who are you, reverend?”
“I am Tudu the independent divinity.”

segs.p: “Nanu tvaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā anāgāmī byākato, atha kiñcarahi idhāgato?
segs.e: “Didn’t the Buddha declare you a non-returner? So what then are you doing back here?
See how far you have strayed!”

segs.p: Atha kho turū paccekabrahmā kokālikaṁ bhikkhuṁ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Tudu addressed Kokālika in verse:
“A person is born
with an axe in their mouth.
A fool cuts themselves with it
when they say bad words.
When you praise someone worthy of criticism,
or criticize someone worthy of praise,
you choose a losing hand with your own mouth:
you’ll never find happiness that way.
A losing hand at dice is a trivial thing,
if all you lose is your money
and all you own, even yourself.
What’s a really terrible hand
is to hate the holy ones.
For a hundred thousand times a hundred million
times five hundred and thirty-six times <j>a thousand times ten million years
a slanderer of noble ones goes to hell,
having aimed bad words and thoughts at them.”

segs.p: Atha kho kokāliko bhikkhu teneva ābādhena kālamakāsi.
segs.e: Then the mendicant Kokālika died of that illness.

segs.p: Kālaṅkato ca kokāliko bhikkhu padumaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṁ āghātetvā.
segs.e: He was reborn in the Pink Lotus hell because of his resentment for Sāriputta and Moggallāna.

segs.p: Atha kho brahmā sahampati abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho brahmā sahampati bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then, late at night, the glorious divinity Sahampati, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him,
“Sir, the mendicant Kokālika has passed away.

segs.p: Kālaṅkato ca, bhante, kokāliko bhikkhu padumaṁ nirayaṁ upapanno sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṁ āghātetvā”ti.
segs.e: He was reborn in the Pink Lotus hell because of his resentment for Sāriputta and Moggallāna.”
That is what the divinity Sahampati said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
segs.e: Then he bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then, when the night had passed, the Buddha told the mendicants all that had happened.

segs.p: “imaṁ, bhikkhave, rattiṁ brahmā sahampati abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho, bhikkhave, brahmā sahampati maṁ etadavoca:
kālaṅkato ca, bhante, kokāliko bhikkhu padumaṁ nirayaṁ upapanno sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṁ āghātetvā’ti.
Idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyī”ti.
Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “kīva dīghaṁ nu kho, bhante, padume niraye āyuppamāṇan”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, how long is the lifespan in the Pink Lotus hell?”
“It’s long, mendicant.
It’s not easy to calculate

segs.p: ‘ettakāni vassānīti vā ettakāni vassasatānīti vā ettakāni vassasahassānīti vā ettakāni vassasatasahassānīti vā’”ti.
segs.e: how many years, how many hundreds or thousands or hundreds of thousands of years it lasts.”
“But sir, is it possible to give a simile?”
“It’s possible,” said the Buddha.

segs.p: “seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsatikhāriko kosalako tilavāho tato puriso vassasatassa vassasatassa accayena ekamekaṁ tilaṁ uddhareyya.
segs.e: “Suppose there was a Kosalan load of twenty packs of sesame seed. And at the end of every hundred years someone would remove a single seed from it.

segs.p: Khippataraṁ kho so, bhikkhu, vīsatikhāriko kosalako tilavāho iminā upakkamena parikkhayaṁ pariyādānaṁ gaccheyya, na tveva eko abbudo nirayo.
segs.e: By this means the Kosalan load of twenty packs of sesame seed would run out faster than a single lifetime in the Abbuda hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati abbudā nirayā; evameko nirabbudo nirayo.
segs.e: Now, twenty lifetimes in the Abbuda hell equal one lifetime in the Nirabbuda hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati nirabbudā nirayā; evameko ababo nirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the Nirabbuda hell equal one lifetime in the Ababa hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati ababā nirayā; evameko aṭaṭo nirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the Ababa hell equal one lifetime in the Aṭaṭa hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati aṭaṭā nirayā; evameko ahaho nirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the Aṭaṭa hell equal one lifetime in the Ahaha hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati ahahā nirayā; evameko kumudo nirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the Ahaha hell equal one lifetime in the Yellow Lotus hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati kumudā nirayā; evameko sogandhiko nirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the Yellow Lotus hell equal one lifetime in the Fragrant Water Lily hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati sogandhikā nirayā; evameko uppalako nirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the Fragrant Water Lily hell equal one lifetime in the Blue Water Lily hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati uppalakā nirayā; evameko puṇḍarīko nirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the Blue Water Lily hell equal one lifetime in the White Lotus hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati puṇḍarīkā nirayā; evameko padumo nirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the White Lotus hell equal one lifetime in the Pink Lotus hell.

segs.p: Padumaṁ kho pana, bhikkhu, nirayaṁ kokāliko bhikkhu upapanno sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṁ āghātetvā”ti.
segs.e: The mendicant Kokālika has been reborn in the Pink Lotus hell because of his resentment for Sāriputta and Moggallāna.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
segs.e: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“A person is born
with an axe in their mouth.
A fool cuts themselves with it
when they say bad words.
When you praise someone worthy of criticism,
or criticize someone worthy of praise,
you choose a losing hand with your own mouth:
you’ll never find happiness that way.
A losing hand at dice is a trivial thing,
if all you lose is your money
and all you own, even yourself.
What’s a really terrible hand
is to hate the holy ones.
For a hundred thousand times a hundred million,
times five hundred and thirty-six times <j>a thousand times ten million years
a slanderer of noble ones goes to hell,
having aimed bad words and thoughts at them.”
Numbered Discourses 10.90
9. Senior Mendicants
The Powers of One Who has Ended Defilements

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Sāriputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “kati nu kho, sāriputta, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balāni, yehi balehi samannāgato khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ paṭijānāti:
segs.e: “Sāriputta, how many powers does a mendicant who has ended the defilements have that qualify them to claim:
‘My defilements have ended.’”

segs.p: “Dasa, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balāni, yehi balehi samannāgato khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ paṭijānāti:
segs.e: “Sir, a mendicant who has ended the defilements has ten powers that qualify them to claim:
‘My defilements have ended.’
What ten?

segs.p: Idha, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno aniccato sabbe saṅkhārā yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā honti.
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant with defilements ended has clearly seen with right wisdom all conditions as truly impermanent.

segs.p: Yampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno aniccato sabbe saṅkhārā yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā honti, idampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balaṁ hoti, yaṁ balaṁ āgamma khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ paṭijānāti:
segs.e: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim:
‘My defilements have ended.’

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā honti.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has clearly seen with right wisdom that sensual pleasures are truly like a pit of glowing coals.

segs.p: Yampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā honti, idampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balaṁ hoti, yaṁ balaṁ āgamma khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ paṭijānāti:
segs.e: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim:
‘My defilements have ended.’

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno vivekaninnaṁ cittaṁ hoti vivekapoṇaṁ vivekapabbhāraṁ vivekaṭṭhaṁ nekkhammābhirataṁ byantībhūtaṁ sabbaso āsavaṭṭhāniyehi dhammehi.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mind of a mendicant with defilements ended slants, slopes, and inclines to seclusion. They’re withdrawn, loving renunciation, and have totally eliminated defiling influences.

segs.p: Yampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno vivekaninnaṁ cittaṁ hoti vivekapoṇaṁ vivekapabbhāraṁ vivekaṭṭhaṁ nekkhammābhirataṁ byantībhūtaṁ sabbaso āsavaṭṭhāniyehi dhammehi, idampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balaṁ hoti, yaṁ balaṁ āgamma khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ paṭijānāti:
segs.e: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim:
‘My defilements have ended.’

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā honti subhāvitā.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

segs.p: Yampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā honti subhāvitā, idampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balaṁ hoti, yaṁ balaṁ āgamma khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ paṭijānāti:
segs.e: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim:
‘My defilements have ended.’

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno cattāro sammappadhānā bhāvitā honti subhāvitā …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the four right efforts. …
the four bases of psychic power …
the five faculties …
the five powers …
the seven awakening factors …

segs.p: ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvito hoti subhāvito.
segs.e: the noble eightfold path.

segs.p: Yampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvito hoti subhāvito, idampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balaṁ hoti, yaṁ balaṁ āgamma khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ paṭijānāti:
segs.e: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim:
‘My defilements have ended.’

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhante, dasa khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balāni, yehi balehi samannāgato khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ paṭijānāti:
segs.e: A mendicant who has ended the defilements possesses these ten powers that qualify them to claim:
‘My defilements have ended.’”
Numbered Discourses 10.91
10. With Upāli
Pleasure Seekers

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Buddha said to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika:
“These ten pleasure seekers are found in the world.
What ten?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena;
segs.e: First, a pleasure seeker seeks wealth using illegitimate, coercive means.

segs.p: adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena na attānaṁ sukheti na pīṇeti na saṁvibhajati na puññāni karoti.
segs.e: They don’t make themselves happy and pleased, nor share it and make merit.

segs.p: Idha pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena;
segs.e: Next, a pleasure seeker seeks wealth using illegitimate, coercive means.

segs.p: adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena attānaṁ sukheti pīṇeti, na saṁvibhajati na puññāni karoti.
segs.e: They make themselves happy and pleased, but don’t share it and make merit.

segs.p: Idha pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena;
segs.e: Next, a pleasure seeker seeks wealth using illegitimate, coercive means.

segs.p: adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena attānaṁ sukheti pīṇeti saṁvibhajati puññāni karoti.
segs.e: They make themselves happy and pleased, and they share it and make merit.

segs.p: Idha pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi;
segs.e: Next, a pleasure seeker seeks wealth using means both legitimate and illegitimate, and coercive and non-coercive.

segs.p: dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi na attānaṁ sukheti na pīṇeti na saṁvibhajati na puññāni karoti.
segs.e: They don’t make themselves happy and pleased, nor share it and make merit.

segs.p: Idha pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi;
segs.e: Next, a pleasure seeker seeks wealth using means both legitimate and illegitimate, and coercive and non-coercive.

segs.p: dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi attānaṁ sukheti pīṇeti, na saṁvibhajati na puññāni karoti.
segs.e: They make themselves happy and pleased, but don’t share it and make merit.

segs.p: Idha pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi;
segs.e: Next, a pleasure seeker seeks wealth using means both legitimate and illegitimate, and coercive and non-coercive.

segs.p: dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi attānaṁ sukheti pīṇeti saṁvibhajati puññāni karoti.
segs.e: They make themselves happy and pleased, and they share it and make merit.

segs.p: Idha pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena;
segs.e: Next, a pleasure seeker seeks wealth using legitimate, non-coercive means.

segs.p: dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena na attānaṁ sukheti na pīṇeti na saṁvibhajati na puññāni karoti.

segs.p: dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṁ sukheti pīṇeti, na saṁvibhajati na puññāni karoti.

segs.p: Idha pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena;
segs.e: Next, a pleasure seeker seeks wealth using legitimate, non-coercive means.

segs.p: dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṁ sukheti pīṇeti saṁvibhajati puññāni karoti.
segs.e: They make themselves happy and pleased, and they share it and make merit.

segs.p: Te ca bhoge gathito mucchito ajjhosanno anādīnavadassāvī anissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.
segs.e: But they enjoy that wealth tied, infatuated, attached, blind to the drawbacks, and not understanding the escape.

segs.p: Idha pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena;
segs.e: Next, a pleasure seeker seeks wealth using legitimate, non-coercive means.

segs.p: Te ca bhoge agathito amucchito anajjhosanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.

segs.p: Tatra, gahapati, yvāyaṁ kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena, adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena na attānaṁ sukheti na pīṇeti na saṁvibhajati na puññāni karoti, ayaṁ, gahapati, kāmabhogī tīhi ṭhānehi gārayho.
segs.e: Now, consider the pleasure seeker who seeks wealth using illegitimate, coercive means, and who doesn’t make themselves happy and pleased, nor share it and make merit. They may be criticized on three grounds.

segs.p: ‘Adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenā’ti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena gārayho.

But they enjoy that wealth tied, infatuated, attached, blind to the drawbacks, and not understanding the escape. They may be praised on three grounds and criticized on one.

segs.p: ‘Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenā’ti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: They seek for wealth using legitimate, non-coercive means. This is the first ground for praise.

segs.p: ‘Attānaṁ sukheti pīṇetī’ti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: They make themselves happy and pleased. This is the second ground for praise.

segs.p: ‘Saṁvibhajati puññāni karotī’ti, iminā tatiyena ṭhānena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: They share it and make merit. This is the third ground for praise.

segs.p: ‘Te ca bhoge gathito mucchito ajjhosanno anādīnavadassāvī anissaraṇapañño paribhuñjatī’ti, iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho.
segs.e: They enjoy that wealth tied, infatuated, attached, blind to the drawbacks, and not understanding the escape. This is the one ground for criticism.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, gahapati, kāmabhogī imehi tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṁso iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho.
segs.e: This pleasure seeker may be praised on these three grounds, and criticized on this one.

segs.p: Tatra, gahapati, yvāyaṁ kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena, dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṁ sukheti pīṇeti saṁvibhajati puññāni karoti, te ca bhoge agathito amucchito anajjhosanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati, ayaṁ, gahapati, kāmabhogī catūhi ṭhānehi pāsaṁso.
segs.e: Now, consider the pleasure seeker who seeks wealth using legitimate, non-coercive means, and who makes themselves happy and pleased, and shares it and makes merit. And they enjoy that wealth untied, uninfatuated, unattached, seeing the drawbacks, and understanding the escape. They may be praised on four grounds.

segs.p: ‘Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenā’ti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: They seek for wealth using legitimate, non-coercive means. This is the first ground for praise.

segs.p: ‘Attānaṁ sukheti pīṇetī’ti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: They make themselves happy and pleased. This is the second ground for praise.

segs.p: ‘Saṁvibhajati puññāni karotī’ti, iminā tatiyena ṭhānena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: They share it and make merit. This is the third ground for praise.

segs.p: ‘Te ca bhoge agathito amucchito anajjhosanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjatī’ti, iminā catutthena ṭhānena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: They enjoy that wealth untied, uninfatuated, unattached, seeing the drawbacks, and understanding the escape. This is the fourth ground for praise.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, gahapati, kāmabhogī imehi catūhi ṭhānehi pāsaṁso.
segs.e: This pleasure seeker may be praised on these four grounds.

segs.p: Ime kho, gahapati, dasa kāmabhogī santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the ten pleasure seekers found in the world.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, gahapati, dasannaṁ kāmabhogīnaṁ yvāyaṁ kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena, dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṁ sukheti pīṇeti saṁvibhajati puññāni karoti, te ca bhoge agathito amucchito anajjhosanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati, ayaṁ imesaṁ dasannaṁ kāmabhogīnaṁ aggo ca seṭṭho ca pāmokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca.
segs.e: The pleasure seeker who seeks wealth using legitimate, non-coercive means, who makes themselves happy and pleased, and shares it and makes merit, and who uses that wealth untied, uninfatuated, unattached, seeing the drawbacks, and understanding the escape is the foremost, best, chief, highest, and finest of the ten.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, gahapati, gavā khīraṁ, khīramhā dadhi, dadhimhā navanītaṁ, navanītamhā sappi, sappimhā sappimaṇḍo. Sappimaṇḍo tattha aggamakkhāyati.
segs.e: From a cow comes milk, from milk comes curds, from curds come butter, from butter comes ghee, and from ghee comes cream of ghee. And the cream of ghee is said to be the best of these.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, gahapati, imesaṁ dasannaṁ kāmabhogīnaṁ yvāyaṁ kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena, dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṁ sukheti pīṇeti saṁvibhajati puññāni karoti, te ca bhoge agathito amucchito anajjhosanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati, ayaṁ imesaṁ dasannaṁ kāmabhogīnaṁ aggo ca seṭṭho ca pāmokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro cā”ti.
segs.e: In the same way, the pleasure seeker who seeks wealth using legitimate, non-coercive means, who makes themselves happy and pleased, and shares it and makes merit, and who uses that wealth untied, uninfatuated, unattached, seeing the drawbacks, and understanding the escape is the foremost, best, chief, highest, and finest of the ten.”
Numbered Discourses 10.92
10. With Upāli
Dangers

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Yato, kho, gahapati, ariyasāvakassa pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti, catūhi ca sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, ariyo cassa ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: “Householder, when a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, possesses the four factors of stream-entry, and has clearly seen and penetrated the noble system with wisdom, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

segs.p: ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto. Sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti.
segs.e: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’

segs.p: Katamāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti?
segs.e: What are the five fears and enmities they have quelled?

segs.p: Yaṁ, gahapati, pāṇātipātī pāṇātipātapaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti, pāṇātipātā paṭivirato neva diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati na samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati na cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
segs.e: Anyone who kills living creatures brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. Anyone who refrains from killing living creatures does not brim with fear and enmity either in this life or in lives to come, and doesn’t experience mental pain and sadness.

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā paṭiviratassa evaṁ taṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ vūpasantaṁ hoti.
segs.e: So that fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from killing living creatures.
Anyone who steals …
Anyone who commits sexual misconduct …
Anyone who lies …

segs.p: surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhāyī surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānapaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato neva diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati na samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati na cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
segs.e: Anyone who consumes beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. Anyone who refrains from beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants does not brim with fear and enmity either in this life or in lives to come, and doesn’t experience mental pain and sadness.

segs.p: Surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratassa evaṁ taṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ vūpasantaṁ hoti.
segs.e: So that fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants.

segs.p: Imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti.
segs.e: These are the five fears and enmities they have quelled.
What are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti:
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha:

‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’
