They have experiential confidence in the teaching:

segs.p: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti;
segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’
They have experiential confidence in the Saṅgha:

segs.p: ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṁ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā, esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā’ti;
segs.e: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti ‘akhaṇḍehi acchiddehi asabalehi akammāsehi bhujissehi viññuppasatthehi aparāmaṭṭhehi samādhisaṁvattanikehi’.
segs.e: And a noble disciple’s ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.
These are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess.

segs.p: Katamo cassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho?
segs.e: And what is the noble system that they have clearly seen and penetrated with wisdom?
It’s when a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘iti imasmiṁ sati idaṁ hoti; imassuppādā idaṁ uppajjati;
segs.e: ‘So, when this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.

segs.p: imasmiṁ asati idaṁ na hoti; imassa nirodhā idaṁ nirujjhati, yadidaṁ—
segs.e: When this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases. That is:
Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness.
Consciousness is a requirement for name and form.
Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields.
The six sense fields are requirements for contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
Craving is a requirement for grasping.
Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.
Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.
Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

When ignorance fades away and ceases no residue left behind, choices cease. When choices cease, consciousness ceases. When consciousness ceases, name and form cease. When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease. When the six sense fields cease, contact ceases. When contact ceases, feeling ceases. When feeling ceases, craving ceases. When craving ceases, grasping ceases. When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases. When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases. When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’

segs.p: Ayañcassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho.
segs.e: This is the noble system that they have clearly seen and penetrated with wisdom.

segs.p: Yato kho, gahapati, ariyasāvakassa imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti, imehi ca catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, ayañcassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: When a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, possesses the four factors of stream-entry, and has clearly seen and penetrated the noble system with wisdom, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

segs.p: ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto; sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”ti.
segs.e: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’”
Numbered Discourses 10.93
10. With Upāli
What is Your View?

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati divā divassa sāvatthiyā nikkhami bhagavantaṁ dassanāya.
segs.e: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika left Sāvatthī in the middle of the day to see the Buddha.
Then it occurred to him,
“It’s the wrong time to see the Buddha,
as he’s in retreat.
And it’s the wrong time to see the esteemed mendicants,
as they’re in retreat.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ yena aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ ārāmo tenupasaṅkameyyan”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I visit the monastery for the wanderers of other religions?”

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ ārāmo tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Then he went to the monastery for the wanderers of other religions.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena aññatitthiyā paribbājakā saṅgamma samāgamma unnādino uccāsaddamahāsaddā anekavihitaṁ tiracchānakathaṁ kathentā nisinnā honti.
segs.e: Now at that time, the wanderers of other religions had come together, making an uproar, a colossal racket as they sat and talked about all kinds of low topics.

segs.p: Addasaṁsu kho te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
segs.e: They saw Anāthapiṇḍika coming off in the distance,
and stopped each other, saying,
“Be quiet, good fellows, don’t make a sound.

segs.p: Ayaṁ anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati ārāmaṁ āgacchati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvako.
segs.e: The householder Anāthapiṇḍika, a disciple of the ascetic Gotama, is coming into our monastery.

segs.p: Yāvatā kho pana samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakā gihī odātavasanā sāvatthiyaṁ paṭivasanti, ayaṁ tesaṁ aññataro anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati.
segs.e: He is included among the white-clothed lay disciples of the ascetic Gotama, who is residing in Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Appasaddakāmā kho pana te āyasmanto appasaddavinītā appasaddassa vaṇṇavādino.
segs.e: Such venerables like the quiet, are educated to be quiet, and praise the quiet.

segs.p: Appeva nāma appasaddaṁ parisaṁ viditvā upasaṅkamitabbaṁ maññeyyā”ti.
segs.e: Hopefully if he sees that our assembly is quiet he’ll see fit to approach.”

segs.p: Atha kho te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
segs.e: Then those wanderers of other religions fell silent.

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Anāthapiṇḍika went up to them, and exchanged greetings with those wanderers.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side. The wanderers said to him,
“Tell us, householder, what is the view of the ascetic Gotama?”

segs.p: “Na kho ahaṁ, bhante, bhagavato sabbaṁ diṭṭhiṁ jānāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Sirs, I don’t know all his views.”

segs.p: “Iti kira tvaṁ, gahapati, na samaṇassa gotamassa sabbaṁ diṭṭhiṁ jānāsi;
segs.e: “Well then, since it seems you don’t know all the views of the ascetic Gotama,
tell us, what are the views of the mendicants?”

segs.p: “Bhikkhūnampi kho ahaṁ, bhante, na sabbaṁ diṭṭhiṁ jānāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Sirs, I don’t know all the mendicants’ views.”

segs.p: “Iti kira tvaṁ, gahapati, na samaṇassa gotamassa sabbaṁ diṭṭhiṁ jānāsi napi bhikkhūnaṁ sabbaṁ diṭṭhiṁ jānāsi;
segs.e: “Well then, since it seems you don’t know all the views of the ascetic Gotama or of the mendicants,
tell us, householder, what is your view?”

segs.p: “Etaṁ kho, bhante, amhehi na dukkaraṁ byākātuṁ yaṁdiṭṭhikā mayaṁ.
segs.e: “Sirs, it’s not hard for me to explain what my views are.

segs.p: Iṅgha tāva āyasmanto yathāsakāni diṭṭhigatāni byākarontu, pacchāpetaṁ amhehi na dukkaraṁ bhavissati byākātuṁ yaṁdiṭṭhikā mayan”ti.
segs.e: But please, let the venerables explain their own convictions first. Afterwards it won’t be hard for me to explain my views.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro paribbājako anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, one of the wanderers said to him,
“The cosmos is eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.
That’s my view, householder.”

segs.p: Aññataropi kho paribbājako anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Another wanderer said,
“The cosmos is not eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.
That’s my view, householder.”

segs.p: Aññataropi kho paribbājako anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Another wanderer said,
“The cosmos is finite …” …
“The cosmos is infinite …” …
“The soul and the body are one and the same …” …
“The soul is one thing, the body another …” …
“A realized one still exists after death …” …
“A realized one no longer exists after death …” …

segs.p: hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā …
segs.e: “A realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death …” …

segs.p: neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
segs.e: “A Realized One neither still exists nor no longer exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.
That’s my view, householder.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati te paribbājake etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, Anāthapiṇḍika said this,
“Sirs, regarding the venerable who said this:
‘The cosmos is eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.
That’s my view, householder.’

segs.p: imassa ayamāyasmato diṭṭhi attano vā ayonisomanasikārahetu uppannā paratoghosapaccayā vā.
segs.e: This view of his has either arisen from his own irrational application of mind, or is conditioned by what someone else says.

segs.p: Sā kho panesā diṭṭhi bhūtā saṅkhatā cetayitā paṭiccasamuppannā.
segs.e: But that view is created, conditioned, chosen, dependently originated.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho pana kiñci bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ cetayitaṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ tadaniccaṁ.
segs.e: Whatever is created, conditioned, chosen, and dependently originated is impermanent.
And what’s impermanent is suffering.

segs.p: Yaṁ dukkhaṁ tadeveso āyasmā allīno, tadeveso āyasmā ajjhupagato.
segs.e: What he clings to and holds to is just suffering.
Regarding the venerable who said this:
‘The cosmos is not eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.
That’s my view, householder.’

segs.p: imassāpi ayamāyasmato diṭṭhi attano vā ayonisomanasikārahetu uppannā paratoghosapaccayā vā.
segs.e: This view of his has either arisen from his own irrational application of mind, or is conditioned by what someone else says.

segs.p: Sā kho panesā diṭṭhi bhūtā saṅkhatā cetayitā paṭiccasamuppannā.
segs.e: But that view is created, conditioned, chosen, dependently originated.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho pana kiñci bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ cetayitaṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ tadaniccaṁ.
segs.e: Whatever is created, conditioned, chosen, and dependently originated is impermanent.
And what’s impermanent is suffering.

segs.p: Yaṁ dukkhaṁ tadeveso āyasmā allīno, tadeveso āyasmā ajjhupagato.
segs.e: What he clings to and holds to is just suffering.
Regarding the venerable who said this:
‘The cosmos is finite …’ …
‘The cosmos is infinite …’ …
‘The soul and the body are one and the same …’ …
‘The soul is one thing, the body another …’ …
‘A realized one still exists after death …’ …
‘A realized one no longer exists after death …’ …

segs.p: hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā …
segs.e: ‘A realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death …’ …

segs.p: neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
segs.e: ‘A Realized One neither still exists nor no longer exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.
That’s my view, householder.’

segs.p: imassāpi ayamāyasmato diṭṭhi attano vā ayonisomanasikārahetu uppannā paratoghosapaccayā vā.
segs.e: This view of his has either arisen from his own irrational application of mind, or is conditioned by what someone else says.

segs.p: Sā kho panesā diṭṭhi bhūtā saṅkhatā cetayitā paṭiccasamuppannā.
segs.e: But that view is created, conditioned, chosen, dependently originated.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho pana kiñci bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ cetayitaṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ tadaniccaṁ.
segs.e: Whatever is created, conditioned, chosen, and dependently originated is impermanent.
And what’s impermanent is suffering.

segs.p: Yaṁ dukkhaṁ tadeveso āyasmā allīno, tadeveso āyasmā ajjhupagato”ti.
segs.e: What he clings to and holds to is just suffering.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte te paribbājakā anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When he said this the wanderers said to him,

segs.p: “byākatāni kho, gahapati, amhehi sabbeheva yathāsakāni diṭṭhigatāni.
segs.e: “Householder, we’ve each explained our own convictions.
Tell us, householder, what is your view?”

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho, bhante, kiñci bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ cetayitaṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ tadaniccaṁ.
segs.e: “Sirs, whatever is created, conditioned, chosen, and dependently originated is impermanent.
And what’s impermanent is suffering.

segs.p: ‘Yaṁ dukkhaṁ taṁ netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti—
segs.e: And what’s suffering is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.
That’s my view, sirs.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho, gahapati, kiñci bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ cetayitaṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ tadaniccaṁ.
segs.e: “Householder, whatever is created, conditioned, chosen, and dependently originated is impermanent.
And what’s impermanent is suffering.

segs.p: Yaṁ dukkhaṁ tadeva tvaṁ, gahapati, allīno, tadeva tvaṁ, gahapati, ajjhupagato”ti.
segs.e: What you cling to and hold to is just suffering.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho, bhante, kiñci bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ cetayitaṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ tadaniccaṁ.
segs.e: “Sirs, whatever is created, conditioned, chosen, and dependently originated is impermanent.
And what’s impermanent is suffering.

segs.p: ‘Yaṁ dukkhaṁ taṁ netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, nameso attā’ti—evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhaṁ.
segs.e: And I’ve truly seen clearly with right wisdom that what’s suffering is not mine, I am not this, it’s not my self.

segs.p: Tassa ca uttari nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ pajānāmī”ti.
segs.e: And I truly understand the escape beyond that.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte te paribbājakā tuṇhībhūtā maṅkubhūtā pattakkhandhā adhomukhā pajjhāyantā appaṭibhānā nisīdiṁsu.
segs.e: When this was said, those wanderers sat silent, dismayed, shoulders drooping, downcast, depressed, with nothing to say.

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati te paribbājake tuṇhībhūte maṅkubhūte pattakkhandhe adhomukhe pajjhāyante appaṭibhāne viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yāvatako ahosi tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṁ kathāsallāpo taṁ sabbaṁ bhagavato ārocesi.
segs.e: Seeing this, Anāthapiṇḍika rose from his seat. He went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and informed the Buddha of all they had discussed.
“Good, good, householder!

segs.p: Evaṁ kho te, gahapati, moghapurisā kālena kālaṁ sahadhammena suniggahitaṁ niggahetabbā”ti.
segs.e: That’s how you should legitimately and completely refute those futile men from time to time.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṁsesi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired the householder Anāthapiṇḍika with a Dhamma talk,

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṁsito uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: after which Anāthapiṇḍika got up from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkante anāthapiṇḍike gahapatimhi bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then, not long after Anāthapiṇḍika had left, the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vassasatupasampanno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye, sopi evamevaṁ aññatitthiye paribbājake sahadhammena suniggahitaṁ niggaṇheyya yathā taṁ anāthapiṇḍikena gahapatinā niggahitā”ti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, even a mendicant who has ordained for a hundred years in this teaching and training would legitimately and completely refute those wanderers of other religions just as the householder Anāthapiṇḍika did.”
Numbered Discourses 10.94
10. With Upāli
With Vajjiyamāhita

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā campāyaṁ viharati gaggarāya pokkharaṇiyā tīre.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Campā on the banks of the Gaggarā Lotus Pond.

segs.p: Atha kho vajjiyamāhito gahapati divā divassa campāya nikkhami bhagavantaṁ dassanāya.
segs.e: Then the householder Vajjiyamāhita left Sāvatthī in the middle of the day to see the Buddha.
Then it occurred to him,
“It’s the wrong time to see the Buddha,
as he’s in retreat.
And it’s the wrong time to see the esteemed mendicants,
as they’re in retreat.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ yena aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ ārāmo tenupasaṅkameyyan”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I visit the monastery for the wanderers of other religions?”

segs.p: Atha kho vajjiyamāhito gahapati yena aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ ārāmo tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Then he went to the monastery for the wanderers of other religions.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā saṅgamma samāgamma unnādino uccāsaddamahāsaddā anekavihitaṁ tiracchānakathaṁ kathentā nisinnā honti.
segs.e: Now at that time, the wanderers of other religions had come together, making an uproar, a colossal racket as they sat and talked about all kinds of low topics.

segs.p: Addasaṁsu kho te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā vajjiyamāhitaṁ gahapatiṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ. Disvāna aññamaññaṁ saṇṭhāpesuṁ:
segs.e: They saw Vajjiyamāhita coming off in the distance, and stopped each other, saying,
“Be quiet, good fellows, don’t make a sound.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vajjiyamāhito gahapati āgacchati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvako.
segs.e: The householder Vajjiyamāhita, a disciple of the ascetic Gotama, is coming into our monastery.

segs.p: Yāvatā kho pana samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakā gihī odātavasanā campāyaṁ paṭivasanti, ayaṁ tesaṁ aññataro vajjiyamāhito gahapati.
segs.e: He is included among the white-clothed lay disciples of the ascetic Gotama, who is residing near Campā.

segs.p: Appasaddakāmā kho pana te āyasmanto appasaddavinītā appasaddassa vaṇṇavādino.
segs.e: Such venerables like the quiet, are educated to be quiet, and praise the quiet.

segs.p: Appeva nāma appasaddaṁ parisaṁ viditvā upasaṅkamitabbaṁ maññeyyā”ti.
segs.e: Hopefully if he sees that our assembly is quiet he’ll see fit to approach.”

segs.p: Atha kho te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
segs.e: Then those wanderers of other religions fell silent.

segs.p: Atha kho vajjiyamāhito gahapati yena te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Vajjiyamāhita went up to them, and exchanged greetings with the wanderers there.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho vajjiyamāhitaṁ gahapatiṁ te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side. The wanderers said to him:

segs.p: “saccaṁ kira, gahapati, samaṇo gotamo sabbaṁ tapaṁ garahati, sabbaṁ tapassiṁ lūkhājīviṁ ekaṁsena upakkosati upavadatī”ti?
segs.e: “Is it really true, householder? Does the ascetic Gotama criticize all forms of mortification? Does he categorically condemn and denounce those fervent mortifiers who live rough?”

segs.p: “Na kho, bhante, bhagavā sabbaṁ tapaṁ garahati napi sabbaṁ tapassiṁ lūkhājīviṁ ekaṁsena upakkosati upavadati.
segs.e: “No, sirs, the Buddha does not criticize all forms of mortification. Nor does he categorically condemn and denounce those fervent mortifiers who live rough.

segs.p: Gārayhaṁ kho, bhante, bhagavā garahati, pasaṁsitabbaṁ pasaṁsati.
segs.e: The Buddha criticizes where it is due, and praises where it is due.

segs.p: Gārayhaṁ kho pana, bhante, bhagavā garahanto pasaṁsitabbaṁ pasaṁsanto vibhajjavādo bhagavā.
segs.e: In doing so he is one who speaks after analyzing the question,
and is not one-sided on this point.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro paribbājako vajjiyamāhitaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, one of the wanderers said to him,

segs.p: “āgamehi tvaṁ, gahapati, yassa tvaṁ samaṇassa gotamassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati, samaṇo gotamo venayiko appaññattiko”ti?
segs.e: “Hold on, householder! That ascetic Gotama who you praise is an exterminator who refrains from making statements.”
“On this point, also, I reasonably respond to the venerables.
The Buddha has stated ‘This is skillful’ and
‘This is unskillful’.

segs.p: Iti kusalākusalaṁ bhagavā paññāpayamāno sapaññattiko bhagavā;
segs.e: So when it comes to what is skillful and unskillful the Buddha makes a statement.
He is not an exterminator who refrains from making statements.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte te paribbājakā tuṇhībhūtā maṅkubhūtā pattakkhandhā adhomukhā pajjhāyantā appaṭibhānā nisīdiṁsu.
segs.e: When this was said, those wanderers sat silent, dismayed, shoulders drooping, downcast, depressed, with nothing to say.

segs.p: Atha kho vajjiyamāhito gahapati te paribbājake tuṇhībhūte maṅkubhūte pattakkhandhe adhomukhe pajjhāyante appaṭibhāne viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Seeing this, Vajjiyamāhita rose from his seat. He went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho vajjiyamāhito gahapati yāvatako ahosi tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṁ kathāsallāpo taṁ sabbaṁ bhagavato ārocesi.
segs.e: and informed the Buddha of all they had discussed.
“Good, good, householder!

segs.p: Evaṁ kho te, gahapati, moghapurisā kālena kālaṁ sahadhammena suniggahitaṁ niggahetabbā.
segs.e: That’s how you should legitimately and completely refute those futile men from time to time.

segs.p: Nāhaṁ, gahapati, sabbaṁ tapaṁ tapitabbanti vadāmi;
segs.e: Householder, I don’t say that all mortifications should be undergone.

segs.p: na ca panāhaṁ, gahapati, sabbaṁ tapaṁ na tapitabbanti vadāmi;
segs.e: But I don’t say that no mortifications should be undergone.

segs.p: nāhaṁ, gahapati, sabbaṁ samādānaṁ samāditabbanti vadāmi;
segs.e: I don’t say that all observances should be undertaken.

segs.p: na panāhaṁ, gahapati, sabbaṁ samādānaṁ na samāditabbanti vadāmi;
segs.e: But I don’t say that no observances should be undertaken.

segs.p: nāhaṁ, gahapati, sabbaṁ padhānaṁ padahitabbanti vadāmi;
segs.e: I don’t say that all efforts should be tried.

segs.p: na panāhaṁ, gahapati, sabbaṁ padhānaṁ na padahitabbanti vadāmi;
segs.e: But I don’t say that no efforts should be tried.

segs.p: nāhaṁ, gahapati, sabbo paṭinissaggo paṭinissajjitabboti vadāmi.
segs.e: I don’t say that everything should be given up.

segs.p: Na panāhaṁ, gahapati, sabbo paṭinissaggo na paṭinissajjitabboti vadāmi;
segs.e: But I don’t say that nothing should be given up.

segs.p: nāhaṁ, gahapati, sabbā vimutti vimuccitabbāti vadāmi;
segs.e: I don’t say that you should be liberated with all kinds of freedom.

segs.p: na panāhaṁ, gahapati, sabbā vimutti na vimuccitabbāti vadāmi.
segs.e: But I don’t say that you should not be liberated with any kind of freedom.

segs.p: Yañhi, gahapati, tapaṁ tapato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, evarūpaṁ tapaṁ na tapitabbanti vadāmi.
segs.e: When undergoing certain mortifications, unskillful qualities grow while skillful qualities decline. I say that you shouldn’t undergo those mortifications.

segs.p: Yañca khvassa, gahapati, tapaṁ tapato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, evarūpaṁ tapaṁ tapitabbanti vadāmi.
segs.e: When undergoing certain mortifications, unskillful qualities decline while skillful qualities grow. I say that you should undergo those mortifications.

segs.p: Yañhi, gahapati, samādānaṁ samādiyato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, evarūpaṁ samādānaṁ na samāditabbanti vadāmi.
segs.e: When undertaking certain observances, unskillful qualities grow while skillful qualities decline. I say that you shouldn’t undertake those observances.

segs.p: Yañca khvassa, gahapati, samādānaṁ samādiyato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, evarūpaṁ samādānaṁ samāditabbanti vadāmi.
segs.e: When undertaking certain observances, unskillful qualities decline while skillful qualities grow. I say that you should undertake those observances.

segs.p: Yañhi, gahapati, padhānaṁ padahato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, evarūpaṁ padhānaṁ na padahitabbanti vadāmi.
segs.e: When trying certain efforts, unskillful qualities grow while skillful qualities decline. I say that you shouldn’t try those efforts.

segs.p: Yañca khvassa, gahapati, padhānaṁ padahato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, evarūpaṁ padhānaṁ padahitabbanti vadāmi.
segs.e: When trying certain efforts, unskillful qualities decline while skillful qualities grow. I say that you should try those efforts.

segs.p: Yañhi, gahapati, paṭinissaggaṁ paṭinissajjato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, evarūpo paṭinissaggo na paṭinissajjitabboti vadāmi.
segs.e: When giving up certain things, unskillful qualities grow while skillful qualities decline. I say that you shouldn’t give up those things.

segs.p: Yañca khvassa, gahapati, paṭinissaggaṁ paṭinissajjato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, evarūpo paṭinissaggo paṭinissajjitabboti vadāmi.
segs.e: When giving up certain things, unskillful qualities decline while skillful qualities grow. I say that you should give up those things.

segs.p: Yañhi, gahapati, vimuttiṁ vimuccato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, evarūpā vimutti na vimuccitabbāti vadāmi.
segs.e: When being liberated with certain kinds of freedom, unskillful qualities grow while skillful qualities decline. I say that you shouldn’t be liberated with those kinds of freedom.

segs.p: Yañca khvassa, gahapati, vimuttiṁ vimuccato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, evarūpā vimutti vimuccitabbāti vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: When being liberated with certain kinds of freedom, unskillful qualities decline while skillful qualities grow. I say that you should be liberated with those kinds of freedom.”

segs.p: Atha kho vajjiyamāhito gahapati bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṁsito uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: After Vajjiyamāhita had been educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired with a Dhamma talk by the Buddha, he got up from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkante vajjiyamāhite gahapatimhi bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then, not long after Vajjiyamāhita had left, the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dīgharattaṁ apparajakkho imasmiṁ dhammavinaye, sopi evamevaṁ aññatitthiye paribbājake sahadhammena suniggahitaṁ niggaṇheyya yathā taṁ vajjiyamāhitena gahapatinā niggahitā”ti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, even a mendicant who for a long time has had little dust in their eye in this teaching and training would legitimately and completely refute those wanderers of other religions just as the householder Vajjiyamāhita did.”
Numbered Discourses 10.95
10. With Upāli
With Uttiya

segs.p: Atha kho uttiyo paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the wanderer Uttiya went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho uttiyo paribbājako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, sassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan”ti?
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, is this right: ‘The cosmos is eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”
“This has not been declared by me, Uttiya.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, asassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan”ti?
segs.e: “Then is this right: ‘The cosmos is not eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”
“This has not been declared by me, Uttiya.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, antavā loko …pe…
segs.e: “Then is this right: ‘The cosmos is finite …’ …
‘The cosmos is infinite …’ …
‘The soul and the body are one and the same …’ …
‘The soul is one thing, the body another …’ …
‘A realized one still exists after death …’ …
‘A realized one no longer exists after death …’ …

segs.p: hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā …
segs.e: ‘A realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death …’ …

segs.p: neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan”ti?
segs.e: ‘A realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”
“This has not been declared by me, Uttiya.”

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’”ti.
“‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, sassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, uttiya, mayā—
segs.e: “When asked about all these points, worthy Gotama says that they have not been declared by him.

segs.p: sassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, asassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
‘etampi kho, uttiya, abyākataṁ mayā asassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, antavā loko …pe…
hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā …
neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.

segs.e: So what then has been declared by Worthy Gotama?”

segs.p: “Abhiññāya kho ahaṁ, uttiya, sāvakānaṁ dhammaṁ desemi sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti.
segs.e: “Uttiya, I teach my disciples from my own insight in order to purify sentient beings, to get past sorrow and crying, to make an end of pain and sadness, to end the cycle of suffering, and to realize extinguishment.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panetaṁ bhavaṁ gotamo abhiññāya sāvakānaṁ dhammaṁ desesi sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, sabbo vā tena loko nīyati upaḍḍho vā tibhāgo vā”ti?
segs.e: “But when the worthy Gotama teaches in this way, is the whole world saved, or half, or a third?”
But when he said this, the Buddha kept silent.
Then Venerable Ānanda thought,

segs.p: “mā hevaṁ kho uttiyo paribbājako pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ paṭilabhi:
segs.e: “The wanderer Uttiya must not get the harmful misconception:

segs.p: ‘sabbasāmukkaṁsikaṁ vata me samaṇo gotamo pañhaṁ puṭṭho saṁsādeti, no vissajjeti, na nūna visahatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘When the ascetic Gotama was asked this all-important question he falters without answering. He just can’t do it!’

segs.p: Tadassa uttiyassa paribbājakassa dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāyā”ti.
segs.e: That would be for his lasting harm and suffering.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando uttiyaṁ paribbājakaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Ānanda said to the wanderer Uttiya,
“Well then, Reverend Uttiya, I shall give you a simile.

segs.p: Upamāya m’idhekacce viññū purisā bhāsitassa atthaṁ ājānanti.
segs.e: For by means of a simile some sensible people understand the meaning of what is said.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso uttiya, rañño paccantimaṁ nagaraṁ daḷhuddhāpaṁ daḷhapākāratoraṇaṁ ekadvāraṁ.
segs.e: Suppose there was a king’s frontier citadel with fortified embankments, ramparts, and arches, and a single gate.

segs.p: Tatrassa dovāriko paṇḍito byatto medhāvī aññātānaṁ nivāretā ñātānaṁ pavesetā.
segs.e: And it has a gatekeeper who is astute, competent, and intelligent. He keeps strangers out and lets known people in.

segs.p: So tassa nagarassa samantā anupariyāyapathaṁ anukkamati. Anupariyāyapathaṁ anukkamamāno na passeyya pākārasandhiṁ vā pākāravivaraṁ vā, antamaso biḷāranikkhamanamattampi.
segs.e: As he walks around the patrol path, he doesn’t see a hole or cleft in the wall, not even one big enough for a cat to slip out.

segs.p: No ca khvassa evaṁ ñāṇaṁ hoti: ‘ettakā pāṇā imaṁ nagaraṁ pavisanti vā nikkhamanti vā’ti.
segs.e: He doesn’t know how many creatures enter or leave the citadel.

segs.p: Atha khvassa evamettha hoti: ‘ye kho keci oḷārikā pāṇā imaṁ nagaraṁ pavisanti vā nikkhamanti vā, sabbe te iminā dvārena pavisanti vā nikkhamanti vā’ti.
segs.e: But he does know that whatever sizable creatures enter or leave the citadel, all of them do so via this gate.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso uttiya, na tathāgatassa evaṁ ussukkaṁ hoti: ‘sabbo vā tena loko nīyati, upaḍḍho vā, tibhāgo vā’ti.
segs.e: In the same way, it’s not the Realized One’s concern whether the whole world is saved by this, or half, or a third.

segs.p: Atha kho evamettha tathāgatassa hoti: ‘ye kho keci lokamhā nīyiṁsu vā nīyanti vā nīyissanti vā, sabbe te pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe, catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacittā, satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṁ bhāvetvā.
segs.e: But the Realized One knows that whoever is saved from the world—whether in the past, the future, or the present—all have given up the five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom. They have firmly established their mind in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. And they have truly developed the seven awakening factors.

segs.p: Evamete lokamhā nīyiṁsu vā nīyanti vā nīyissanti vā’ti.
segs.e: That’s how they’re saved from the world, in the past, future, or present.

segs.p: Yadeva kho tvaṁ, āvuso uttiya, bhagavantaṁ pañhaṁ apucchi tadevetaṁ pañhaṁ bhagavantaṁ aññena pariyāyena apucchi.
segs.e: Uttiya, you were just asking the Buddha the same question as before in a different way.

segs.p: Tasmā te taṁ bhagavā na byākāsī”ti.
segs.e: That’s why he didn’t answer.”
Numbered Discourses 10.96
10. With Upāli
With Kokanada

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ānando rājagahe viharati tapodārāme.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Ānanda was staying near Rājagaha in the Hot Springs Monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ paccuṭṭhāya yena tapodā tenupasaṅkami gattāni parisiñcituṁ.
segs.e: Then Ānanda rose at the crack of dawn and went to the hot springs to bathe.

segs.p: Tapodāya gattāni parisiñcitvā paccuttaritvā ekacīvaro aṭṭhāsi gattāni pubbāpayamāno.
segs.e: When he had bathed and emerged from the water he stood in one robe drying his limbs.

segs.p: Kokanudopi kho paribbājako rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ paccuṭṭhāya yena tapodā tenupasaṅkami gattāni parisiñcituṁ.
segs.e: The wanderer Kokanada also rose at the crack of dawn and went to the hot springs to bathe.

segs.p: Addasā kho kokanudo paribbājako āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
segs.e: He saw Ānanda coming off in the distance
and said to him,
“Who’s here, reverend?”
“I’m a mendicant, reverend.”
“Of which mendicants?”
“Of the ascetics who follow the Sakyan.”

segs.p: “Puccheyyāma mayaṁ āyasmantaṁ kiñcideva desaṁ, sace āyasmā okāsaṁ karoti pañhassa veyyākaraṇāyā”ti.
segs.e: “I’d like to ask the venerable about a certain point, if you’d take the time to answer.”
“Ask, reverend. When I’ve heard it I’ll know.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, bho, ‘sassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti—evaṁdiṭṭhi bhavan”ti?
segs.e: “Is this your view: ‘The cosmos is eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”
“That’s not my view, reverend.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ pana, bho, ‘asassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti—evaṁdiṭṭhi bhavan”ti?
segs.e: “Then is this your view: ‘The cosmos is not eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”
“That’s not my view, reverend.”
“Then is this your view: ‘The cosmos is finite …’ …
‘The cosmos is infinite …’ …
‘The soul and the body are one and the same …’ …
‘The soul is one thing, the body another …’ …
‘A realized one still exists after death …’ …
‘A realized one no longer exists after death …’ …

segs.p: hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā …
segs.e: ‘A realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death …’ …

segs.p: neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—evaṁdiṭṭhi bhavan”ti?
segs.e: ‘A realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”
“That’s not my view, reverend.”

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’”ti.
“Tena hi bhavaṁ na jānāti, na passatī”ti?
segs.e: “Then, sir, do you neither know nor see?”

segs.p: “Na kho ahaṁ, āvuso, na jānāmi na passāmi.
segs.e: “That’s not so, reverend.
I do know and see.”

segs.p: “‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho, sassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
segs.e: “When asked about all these points, you say that’s not your view.

segs.p: sassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ pana, bho, asassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
asassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.
Kiṁ nu kho, bho, antavā loko …pe…
hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā …
neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti vadesi.
‘Tena hi bhavaṁ na jānāti na passatī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
segs.e: Yet when asked whether you neither know nor see,

segs.p: ‘na kho ahaṁ, āvuso, na jānāmi na passāmi.
segs.e: you say, ‘That’s not so, reverend.
I do know and see.’

segs.p: Yathā kathaṁ panāvuso, imassa bhāsitassa attho daṭṭhabbo”ti?
segs.e: How then should we see the meaning of this statement?”

segs.p: “‘Sassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti kho, āvuso, diṭṭhigatametaṁ.
segs.e: “‘The cosmos is eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile:’ that’s a misconception.

segs.p: ‘Asassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti kho, āvuso, diṭṭhigatametaṁ.
segs.e: ‘The cosmos is not eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile:’ that’s a misconception.
‘The cosmos is finite …’ …
‘The cosmos is infinite …’ …
‘The soul and the body are one and the same …’ …
‘The soul is one thing, the body another …’ …
‘A realized one still exists after death …’ …
‘A realized one no longer exists after death …’ …

segs.p: hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā …
segs.e: ‘A realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death …’ …

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññan’ti kho, āvuso, diṭṭhigatametaṁ.
segs.e: ‘A realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile:’ that’s a misconception.

segs.p: Yāvatā, āvuso, diṭṭhi yāvatā diṭṭhiṭṭhānaṁ diṭṭhiadhiṭṭhānaṁ diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṁ diṭṭhisamuṭṭhānaṁ diṭṭhisamugghāto, tamahaṁ jānāmi tamahaṁ passāmi.
segs.e: I know and see the scope of convictions, the scope of grounds for views, fixation on views, obsession with views, the origin of views, and the uprooting of views.

segs.p: Tamahaṁ jānanto tamahaṁ passanto kyāhaṁ vakkhāmi:
segs.e: Knowing and seeing thus, why should I say:
‘I neither know nor see?’
I do know and see.”

segs.p: “Ko nāmo āyasmā, kathañca panāyasmantaṁ sabrahmacārī jānantī”ti?
segs.e: “What is the venerable’s name? And how are you known among your spiritual companions?”
“Reverend, my name is Ānanda.
And that’s how I’m known among my spiritual companions.”

segs.p: “Mahācariyena vata kira, bho, saddhiṁ mantayamānā na jānimha:
segs.e: “Goodness! I had no idea I was consulting such a great tutor as
Venerable Ānanda!
If I had known who
you were, I wouldn’t have said so much.
May Venerable Ānanda please forgive me.”
Numbered Discourses 10.97
10. With Upāli
Worthy of Offerings Dedicated to the Gods

segs.p: “Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with ten qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.
What ten?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segs.p: Bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo. Ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
segs.e: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.
They have good friends, companions, and associates.
They have right view, possessing right perspective.

segs.p: Anekavihitaṁ iddhividhaṁ paccanubhoti—ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti; bahudhāpi hutvā eko hoti; āvibhāvaṁ, tirobhāvaṁ; tirokuṭṭaṁ tiropākāraṁ tiropabbataṁ asajjamāno gacchati, seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṁ karoti, seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāne gacchati, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṁ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kamati, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṁmahiddhike evaṁmahānubhāve pāṇinā parāmasati parimajjati, yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṁ vatteti.
segs.e: They wield the many kinds of psychic power: multiplying themselves and becoming one again; materializing and dematerializing; going unobstructed through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; diving in and out of the earth as if it were water; walking on water as if it were earth; flying cross-legged through the sky like a bird; touching and stroking with the hand the sun and moon, so mighty and powerful. They control the body as far as the realm of divinity.

segs.p: Dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇāti dibbe ca mānuse ca ye dūre santike ca.
segs.e: With clairaudience that is purified and superhuman, they hear both kinds of sounds, human and heavenly, whether near or far.

segs.p: Parasattānaṁ parapuggalānaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti.
segs.e: They understand the minds of other beings and individuals, having encompassed them with their own mind.
They understand mind with greed as ‘mind with greed’,
and mind without greed as ‘mind without greed’.
They understand mind with hate …
mind without hate …
mind with delusion …
mind without delusion …
constricted mind …
scattered mind …
expansive mind …
unexpansive mind …
mind that is not supreme …
mind that is supreme …
mind immersed in samādhi …
mind not immersed in samādhi …
freed mind …
They understand unfreed mind as ‘unfreed mind’.

segs.p: Anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṁsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi anekepi saṁvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṁvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe: ‘amutrāsiṁ evaṁnāmo evaṅgotto evaṁvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṁsukhadukkhapaṭisaṁvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṁ; tatrāpāsiṁ evaṁnāmo evaṅgotto evaṁvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṁsukhadukkhapaṭisaṁvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti, iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati.
segs.e: They recollect many kinds of past lives, that is, one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand rebirths; many eons of the world contracting, many eons of the world expanding, many eons of the world contracting and expanding. They remember: ‘There, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn somewhere else. There, too, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn here.’ Thus they recollect their many past lives, with features and details.

segs.p: Dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti: ‘ime vata kho bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṁ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapannā; ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṁ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapannā’ti. Iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti.
segs.e: With clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds. ‘These dear beings did bad things by way of body, speech, and mind. They denounced the noble ones; they had wrong view; and they chose to act out of that wrong view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell. These dear beings, however, did good things by way of body, speech, and mind. They never denounced the noble ones; they had right view; and they chose to act out of that right view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.’ And so, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.

segs.p: Āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these ten qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 10.98
10. With Upāli
A Senior Mendicant

segs.p: “Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu yassaṁ yassaṁ disāyaṁ viharati, phāsuyeva viharati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a senior mendicant with ten qualities lives comfortably in whatever region they live.
What ten?
They are long standing and have long gone forth.
They’re ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, reinforcing them by recitation, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

segs.p: diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdho, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso,
segs.e: Both monastic codes have been passed down to them in detail, well analyzed, well mastered, well evaluated in both the rules and accompanying material.
They’re skilled in the instigation and settlement of disciplinary issues.

segs.p: dhammakāmo hoti piyasamudāhāro abhidhamme abhivinaye uḷārapāmojjo,
segs.e: They love the teachings and are a delight to converse with, being full of joy in the teaching and training.
They’re content with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: pāsādiko hoti abhikkantapaṭikkante susaṁvuto antaraghare nisajjāya,
segs.e: They look impressive when going out and coming back, and are well restrained when sitting in an inhabited area.

segs.p: catunnaṁ jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī,
segs.e: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

segs.p: āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu yassaṁ yassaṁ disāyaṁ viharati, phāsuyeva viharatī”ti.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with these ten qualities lives comfortably in whatever region they live.”
Numbered Discourses 10.99
10. With Upāli
With Upāli

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā upāli yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā upāli bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Upāli went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,
“Sir, I wish to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.”

segs.p: “Durabhisambhavāni hi kho, upāli, araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni.
segs.e: “Upāli, remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest are challenging.
It’s hard to maintain seclusion and hard to find joy in it.

segs.p: Ekatte haranti maññe mano vanāni samādhiṁ alabhamānassa bhikkhuno.
segs.e: Staying alone, the forests seem to rob the mind of a mendicant who isn’t immersed in samādhi.
If someone should say this,

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ samādhiṁ alabhamāno araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevissāmī’ti, tassetaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ:
segs.e: ‘Though I don’t have immersion, I’m going to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.’ You can expect that
they’ll sink down or float away.
Suppose there was a large lake,

segs.p: Atha āgaccheyya hatthināgo sattaratano vā aḍḍhaṭṭharatano vā.
segs.e: and along comes a bull elephant that’s three or three and a half meters tall.
He’d think,

segs.p: ‘yannūnāhaṁ imaṁ udakarahadaṁ ogāhetvā kaṇṇasandhovikampi khiḍḍaṁ kīḷeyyaṁ piṭṭhisandhovikampi khiḍḍaṁ kīḷeyyaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Why don’t I plunge into this lake and play around while washing my ears and back?

segs.p: Kaṇṇasandhovikampi khiḍḍaṁ kīḷitvā piṭṭhisandhovikampi khiḍḍaṁ kīḷitvā nhatvā ca pivitvā ca paccuttaritvā yena kāmaṁ pakkameyyan’ti.
segs.e: When I’ve bathed and drunk, I’ll emerge from the water and go wherever I want.’

segs.p: So taṁ udakarahadaṁ ogāhetvā kaṇṇasandhovikampi khiḍḍaṁ kīḷeyya piṭṭhisandhovikampi khiḍḍaṁ kīḷeyya;
segs.e: And that’s just what he does.

segs.p: kaṇṇasandhovikampi khiḍḍaṁ kīḷitvā piṭṭhisandhovikampi khiḍḍaṁ kīḷitvā nhatvā ca pivitvā ca paccuttaritvā yena kāmaṁ pakkameyya.

segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Mahā, upāli, attabhāvo gambhīre gādhaṁ vindati.
segs.e: Because his large incarnation finds a footing in the depths.

segs.p: Atha āgaccheyya saso vā biḷāro vā.
segs.e: Then along comes a rabbit or a cat.
They’d think,
‘What difference is there between me and a bull elephant?

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ imaṁ udakarahadaṁ ogāhetvā kaṇṇasandhovikampi khiḍḍaṁ kīḷeyyaṁ piṭṭhisandhovikampi khiḍḍaṁ kīḷeyyaṁ;
segs.e: Why don’t I plunge into this lake and play around while washing my ears and back?

segs.p: kaṇṇasandhovikampi khiḍḍaṁ kīḷitvā piṭṭhisandhovikampi khiḍḍaṁ kīḷitvā nhatvā ca pivitvā ca paccuttaritvā yena kāmaṁ pakkameyyan’ti.
segs.e: When I’ve bathed and drunk, I’ll emerge from the water and go wherever I want.’

segs.p: So taṁ udakarahadaṁ sahasā appaṭisaṅkhā pakkhandeyya.
segs.e: They jump into the lake rashly, without thinking.
You can expect that
they’ll sink down or float away.
Why is that?

segs.p: Paritto, upāli, attabhāvo gambhīre gādhaṁ na vindati.
segs.e: Because their little incarnation finds no footing in the depths.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, upāli, yo evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: If someone should say this,

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ samādhiṁ alabhamāno araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevissāmī’ti, tassetaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ:
segs.e: ‘Though I don’t have immersion, I’m going to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.’ You can expect that
they’ll sink down or float away.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, upāli, daharo kumāro mando uttānaseyyako sakena muttakarīsena kīḷati.
segs.e: Suppose there was a little baby boy playing in his own urine and feces.
What do you think, Upāli?
Isn’t that a totally foolish game?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Sa kho so, upāli, kumāro aparena samayena vuddhimanvāya indriyānaṁ paripākamanvāya
segs.e: “After some time that boy grows up and his faculties mature.

segs.p: yāni kānici kumārakānaṁ kīḷāpanakāni bhavanti, seyyathidaṁ—vaṅkakaṁ ghaṭikaṁ mokkhacikaṁ ciṅgulakaṁ pattāḷhakaṁ rathakaṁ dhanukaṁ, tehi kīḷati.
segs.e: He accordingly plays childish games such as toy plows, tip-cat, somersaults, pinwheels, toy measures, toy carts, and toy bows.
What do you think, Upāli?

segs.p: nanvāyaṁ khiḍḍā purimāya khiḍḍāya abhikkantatarā ca paṇītatarā cā”ti?
segs.e: Aren’t such games better than what he did before?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Sa kho so, upāli, kumāro aparena samayena vuddhimanvāya indriyānaṁ paripākamanvāya
segs.e: “After some time that boy grows up and his faculties mature further.
He accordingly amuses himself, supplied and provided with the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

segs.p: cakkhuviññeyyehi rūpehi iṭṭhehi kantehi manāpehi piyarūpehi kāmūpasaṁhitehi rajanīyehi,
segs.e: Sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.
Sounds known by the ear …
Smells known by the nose …
Tastes known by the tongue …

segs.p: kāyaviññeyyehi phoṭṭhabbehi iṭṭhehi kantehi manāpehi piyarūpehi kāmūpasaṁhitehi rajanīyehi.
segs.e: Touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.
What do you think, Upāli?

segs.p: nanvāyaṁ khiḍḍā purimāhi khiḍḍāhi abhikkantatarā ca paṇītatarā cā”ti?
segs.e: Aren’t such games better than what he did before?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Idha kho pana vo, upāli, tathāgato loke uppajjati arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā.
segs.e: “Now in this regard, Upāli, a Realized One arises in the world, perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.

segs.p: So imaṁ lokaṁ sadevakaṁ samārakaṁ sabrahmakaṁ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṁ pajaṁ sadevamanussaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti.
segs.e: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others.

segs.p: So dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
segs.e: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

segs.p: Taṁ dhammaṁ suṇāti gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā aññatarasmiṁ vā kule paccājāto.
segs.e: A householder hears that teaching, or a householder’s child, or someone reborn in a good family.

segs.p: So taṁ dhammaṁ sutvā tathāgate saddhaṁ paṭilabhati.
segs.e: They gain faith in the Realized One

segs.p: So tena saddhāpaṭilābhena samannāgato iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: and reflect:
‘Life at home is cramped and dirty, life gone forth is wide open.

segs.p: Nayidaṁ sukaraṁ agāraṁ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṁ ekantaparisuddhaṁ saṅkhalikhitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ carituṁ.
segs.e: It’s not easy for someone living at home to lead the spiritual life utterly full and pure, like a polished shell.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajeyyan’ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I shave off my hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness?’

segs.p: So aparena samayena appaṁ vā bhogakkhandhaṁ pahāya mahantaṁ vā bhogakkhandhaṁ pahāya appaṁ vā ñātiparivaṭṭaṁ pahāya mahantaṁ vā ñātiparivaṭṭaṁ pahāya kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajati.
segs.e: After some time they give up a large or small fortune, and a large or small family circle. They shave off hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: So evaṁ pabbajito samāno bhikkhūnaṁ sikkhāsājīvasamāpanno pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho lajjī dayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati.
segs.e: Once they’ve gone forth, they take up the training and livelihood of the mendicants. They give up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. They’re scrupulous and kind, living full of sympathy for all living beings.

segs.p: Adinnādānaṁ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti dinnādāyī dinnapāṭikaṅkhī; athenena sucibhūtena attanā viharati.
segs.e: They give up stealing. They take only what’s given, and expect only what’s given. They keep themselves clean by not thieving.

segs.p: Abrahmacariyaṁ pahāya brahmacārī hoti ārācārī virato methunā gāmadhammā.
segs.e: They give up unchastity. They are chaste, set apart, refraining from the vulgar act of sex.

segs.p: Musāvādaṁ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti saccavādī saccasandho theto paccayiko avisaṁvādako lokassa.
segs.e: They give up lying. They speak the truth and stick to the truth. They’re honest and dependable, and don’t trick the world with their words.

segs.p: Pisuṇaṁ vācaṁ pahāya pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, ito sutvā na amutra akkhātā imesaṁ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā na imesaṁ akkhātā amūsaṁ bhedāya. Iti bhinnānaṁ vā sandhātā sahitānaṁ vā anuppadātā, samaggārāmo samaggarato samagganandī; samaggakaraṇiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They give up backbiting. They don’t repeat in one place what they heard in another so as to divide people against each other. Instead, they reconcile those who are divided and support those who are united, delighting in harmony, loving harmony, speaking words that promote harmony.

segs.p: Pharusaṁ vācaṁ pahāya pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti. Yā sā vācā nelā kaṇṇasukhā pemanīyā hadayaṅgamā porī bahujanakantā bahujanamanāpā, tathārūpiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They give up harsh speech. They speak in a way that’s mellow, pleasing to the ear, endearing, going to the heart, polite, and likable and agreeable to the people.

segs.p: Samphappalāpaṁ pahāya samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti kālavādī bhūtavādī atthavādī dhammavādī vinayavādī, nidhānavatiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti kālena sāpadesaṁ pariyantavatiṁ atthasaṁhitaṁ.
segs.e: They give up talking nonsense. Their words are timely, true, and meaningful, in line with the teaching and training. They say things at the right time which are valuable, reasonable, succinct, and beneficial.
They refrain from injuring plants and seeds.
They eat in one part of the day, abstaining from eating at night and food at the wrong time.
They refrain from seeing shows of dancing, singing, and music.
They refrain from attiring and adorning themselves with garlands, fragrance, and makeup.
They refrain from high and luxurious beds.
They refrain from receiving gold and currency,
raw grains,
raw meat,
women and girls,
male and female bondservants,
goats and sheep,
chickens and pigs,
elephants, cows, horses, and mares,
and fields and land.
They refrain from running errands and messages;
buying and selling;
falsifying weights, metals, or measures;
bribery, fraud, cheating, and duplicity;
mutilation, murder, abduction, banditry, plunder, and violence.

segs.p: So santuṭṭho hoti kāyaparihārikena cīvarena kucchiparihārikena piṇḍapātena.
segs.e: They’re content with robes to look after the body and almsfood to look after the belly.
Wherever they go, they set out taking only these things.

segs.p: seyyathāpi nāma pakkhī sakuṇo yena yeneva ḍeti sapattabhārova ḍeti.
segs.e: They’re like a bird: wherever it flies, wings are its only burden.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti kāyaparihārikena cīvarena kucchiparihārikena piṇḍapātena. Yena yeneva pakkamati samādāyeva pakkamati.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant is content with robes to look after the body and almsfood to look after the belly. Wherever they go, they set out taking only these things.

segs.p: So iminā ariyena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato ajjhattaṁ anavajjasukhaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
segs.e: When they have this spectrum of noble ethics, they experience a blameless happiness inside themselves.

segs.p: So cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī.
segs.e: When they see a sight with their eyes, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

segs.p: Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ cakkhundriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati; rakkhati cakkhundriyaṁ, cakkhundriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: If the faculty of sight were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of sight, and achieving its restraint.
When they hear a sound with their ears …
When they smell an odor with their nose …
When they taste a flavor with their tongue …
When they feel a touch with their body …

segs.p: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī.
segs.e: When they know an idea with their mind, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

segs.p: Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ manindriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati; rakkhati manindriyaṁ, manindriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: If the faculty of mind were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of mind, and achieving its restraint.

segs.p: So iminā ariyena indriyasaṁvarena samannāgato ajjhattaṁ abyāsekasukhaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
segs.e: When they have this noble sense restraint, they experience an unsullied bliss inside themselves.

segs.p: So abhikkante paṭikkante sampajānakārī hoti, ālokite vilokite sampajānakārī hoti, samiñjite pasārite sampajānakārī hoti, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇe sampajānakārī hoti, asite pīte khāyite sāyite sampajānakārī hoti, uccārapassāvakamme sampajānakārī hoti, gate ṭhite nisinne sutte jāgarite bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī hoti.
segs.e: They act with situational awareness when going out and coming back; when looking ahead and aside; when bending and extending the limbs; when bearing the outer robe, bowl and robes; when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; when urinating and defecating; when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and keeping silent.

segs.p: So iminā ca ariyena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato, iminā ca ariyena indriyasaṁvarena samannāgato, iminā ca ariyena satisampajaññena samannāgato
segs.e: When they have this spectrum of noble ethics, this noble sense restraint, and this noble mindfulness and situational awareness,

segs.p: vivittaṁ senāsanaṁ bhajati araññaṁ rukkhamūlaṁ pabbataṁ kandaraṁ giriguhaṁ susānaṁ vanapatthaṁ abbhokāsaṁ palālapuñjaṁ.
segs.e: they frequent a secluded lodging—a wilderness, the root of a tree, a hill, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a forest, the open air, a heap of straw.

segs.p: So araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā.
segs.e: Gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, they sit down cross-legged, set their body straight, and bring mindfulness to the present.

segs.p: So abhijjhaṁ loke pahāya vigatābhijjhena cetasā viharati, abhijjhāya cittaṁ parisodheti.
segs.e: Giving up covetousness for the world, they meditate with a heart rid of covetousness, cleansing the mind of covetousness.

segs.p: Byāpādapadosaṁ pahāya abyāpannacitto viharati sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī, byāpādapadosā cittaṁ parisodheti.
segs.e: Giving up ill will and malevolence, they meditate with a mind rid of ill will, full of sympathy for all living beings, cleansing the mind of ill will.

segs.p: Thinamiddhaṁ pahāya vigatathinamiddho viharati ālokasaññī sato sampajāno, thinamiddhā cittaṁ parisodheti.
segs.e: Giving up dullness and drowsiness, they meditate with a mind rid of dullness and drowsiness, perceiving light, mindful and aware, cleansing the mind of dullness and drowsiness.

segs.p: Uddhaccakukkuccaṁ pahāya anuddhato viharati ajjhattaṁ vūpasantacitto, uddhaccakukkuccā cittaṁ parisodheti.
segs.e: Giving up restlessness and remorse, they meditate without restlessness, their mind settled internally, cleansing the mind of restlessness and remorse.

segs.p: Vicikicchaṁ pahāya tiṇṇavicikiccho viharati akathaṅkathī kusalesu dhammesu, vicikicchāya cittaṁ parisodheti.
segs.e: Giving up doubt, they meditate having gone beyond doubt, not undecided about skillful qualities, cleansing the mind of doubt.

segs.p: So ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe,
segs.e: They give up these five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom.

segs.p: vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Then, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, they enter and remain in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.
What do you think, Upāli?

segs.p: ‘nanvāyaṁ vihāro purimehi vihārehi abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā’”ti?
segs.e: Isn’t this state better than what they had before?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Imampi kho, upāli, mama sāvakā attani dhammaṁ sampassamānā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, no ca kho tāva anuppattasadatthā viharanti.
segs.e: “When my disciples see this quality inside themselves they frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest. But so far they haven’t achieved their heart’s goal.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, upāli, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, a mendicant enters and remains in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.
What do you think, Upāli?

segs.p: ‘nanvāyaṁ vihāro purimehi vihārehi abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā’”ti?
segs.e: Isn’t this state better than what they had before?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Imampi kho, upāli, mama sāvakā attani dhammaṁ sampassamānā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, no ca kho tāva anuppattasadatthā viharanti.
segs.e: “When my disciples see this quality inside themselves they frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest. But so far they haven’t achieved their heart’s goal.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, upāli, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā …pe… tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, with the fading away of rapture, a mendicant enters and remains in the third absorption. They meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’
What do you think, Upāli?

segs.p: ‘nanvāyaṁ vihāro purimehi vihārehi abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā’”ti?
segs.e: Isn’t this state better than what they had before?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Imampi kho, upāli, mama sāvakā attani dhammaṁ sampassamānā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, no ca kho tāva anuppattasadatthā viharanti.
segs.e: “When my disciples see this quality inside themselves they frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest. But so far they haven’t achieved their heart’s goal.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, upāli, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ …pe….
segs.e: Furthermore, with the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, a mendicant enters and remains in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness. …” …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, upāli, bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: “Furthermore, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, a mendicant enters and remains in the dimension of infinite space.
What do you think, Upāli?

segs.p: ‘nanvāyaṁ vihāro purimehi vihārehi abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā’”ti?
segs.e: Isn’t this state better than what they had before?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Imampi kho, upāli, mama sāvakā attani dhammaṁ sampassamānā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, no ca kho tāva anuppattasadatthā viharanti.
segs.e: “When my disciples see this quality inside themselves they frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest. But so far they haven’t achieved their heart’s goal.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, upāli, bhikkhu sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati …pe….
segs.e: Furthermore, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, a mendicant enters and remains in the dimension of infinite consciousness. …” …

segs.p: Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati …pe….
segs.e: “Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness. …” …

segs.p: Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘santametaṁ paṇītametan’ti nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: “Going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, aware that ‘this is peaceful, this is sublime’, they enter and remain in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.
What do you think, Upāli?

segs.p: ‘nanvāyaṁ vihāro purimehi vihārehi abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā’”ti?
segs.e: Isn’t this state better than what they had before?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Imampi kho, upāli, mama sāvakā attani dhammaṁ sampassamānā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, no ca kho tāva anuppattasadatthā viharanti.
segs.e: “When my disciples see this quality inside themselves they frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest. But so far they haven’t achieved their heart’s goal.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, upāli, bhikkhu sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharati; paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā honti.
segs.e: Furthermore, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, they enter and remain in the cessation of perception and feeling. And, having seen with wisdom, their defilements come to an end.
What do you think, Upāli?

segs.p: ‘nanvāyaṁ vihāro purimehi vihārehi abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā’”ti?
segs.e: Isn’t this state better than what they had before?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Imampi kho, upāli, mama sāvakā attani dhammaṁ sampassamānā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, anuppattasadatthā ca viharanti.
segs.e: “When my disciples see this quality inside themselves they frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest. And they have achieved their heart’s goal.
Come on, Upāli, stay with the Saṅgha.
If you stay with the Saṅgha you’ll be comfortable.”
Numbered Discourses 10.100
10. With Upāli
Cannot

segs.p: “Dasayime, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, without giving up ten things you can’t realize perfection.
What ten?

segs.p: Rāgaṁ, dosaṁ, mohaṁ, kodhaṁ, upanāhaṁ, makkhaṁ, paḷāsaṁ, issaṁ, macchariyaṁ, mānaṁ—
segs.e: Greed, hate, delusion, anger, acrimony, disdain, contempt, jealousy, stinginess, and conceit.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa dhamme appahāya abhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: Without giving up these ten things you can’t realize perfection.

segs.p: Dasayime, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: After giving up ten things you can realize perfection.
What ten?

segs.p: Rāgaṁ, dosaṁ, mohaṁ, kodhaṁ, upanāhaṁ, makkhaṁ, paḷāsaṁ, issaṁ, macchariyaṁ, mānaṁ—
segs.e: Greed, hate, delusion, anger, acrimony, disdain, contempt, jealousy, stinginess, and conceit.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa dhamme pahāya bhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātun”ti.
segs.e: After giving up these ten things you can realize perfection.”
Numbered Discourses 10.101
11. Perceptions for Ascetics
Perceptions for Ascetics

segs.p: “Tisso imā, bhikkhave, samaṇasaññā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta dhamme paripūrenti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when these three perceptions for ascetics are developed and cultivated they fulfill seven things.
What three?

segs.p: Vevaṇṇiyamhi ajjhupagato, parapaṭibaddhā me jīvikā, añño me ākappo karaṇīyoti—
segs.e: ‘I have secured freedom from class.’ ‘My livelihood is tied up with others.’ ‘My behavior should be different.’

segs.p: imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso samaṇasaññā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta dhamme paripūrenti.
segs.e: When these three perceptions for ascetics are developed and cultivated they fulfill seven things.
What seven?

segs.p: Santatakārī hoti santatavutti sīlesu, anabhijjhālu hoti, abyāpajjo hoti, anatimānī hoti, sikkhākāmo hoti, “idamatthan”tissa hoti jīvitaparikkhāresu, āraddhavīriyo ca viharati.
segs.e: Their deeds and behavior are always consistent with the precepts. They’re content, kind-hearted, and humble. They are eager to train. They use the necessities of life after reflecting on their purpose. They’re energetic.

segs.p: Imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso samaṇasaññā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ime satta dhamme paripūrentī”ti.
segs.e: When those three perceptions for ascetics are developed and cultivated they fulfill these seven things.”
Numbered Discourses 10.102
11. Perceptions for Ascetics
Awakening Factors

segs.p: “Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā tisso vijjā paripūrenti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when the seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they fulfill three knowledges.
What seven?

segs.p: Satisambojjhaṅgo, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pītisambojjhaṅgo, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, samādhisambojjhaṅgo, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo—
segs.e: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā tisso vijjā paripūrenti.
segs.e: When these seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they fulfill three knowledges.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati,
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant recollects their many kinds of past lives.

segs.p: seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo …pe… iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati.
segs.e: That is: one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand rebirths; many eons of the world contracting, many eons of the world expanding, many eons of the world contracting and expanding. They recollect their many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

segs.p: Dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena …pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti.
segs.e: With clairvoyance that is purified and surpasses the human, they understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.
They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā imā tisso vijjā paripūrentī”ti.
segs.e: When those seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they fulfill these three knowledges.”
Numbered Discourses 10.103
11. Perceptions for Ascetics
The Wrong Way

segs.p: “Micchattaṁ, bhikkhave, āgamma virādhanā hoti, no ārādhanā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, relying on the wrong way leads to failure, not success.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, micchattaṁ āgamma virādhanā hoti, no ārādhanā?
segs.e: And how does relying on the wrong way lead to failure, not success?

segs.p: Micchādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, micchāsaṅkappo pahoti, micchāsaṅkappassa micchāvācā pahoti, micchāvācassa micchākammanto pahoti, micchākammantassa micchāājīvo pahoti, micchāājīvassa micchāvāyāmo pahoti, micchāvāyāmassa micchāsati pahoti, micchāsatissa micchāsamādhi pahoti, micchāsamādhissa micchāñāṇaṁ pahoti, micchāñāṇissa micchāvimutti pahoti.
segs.e: Wrong view produces wrong purpose. Wrong purpose produces wrong speech. Wrong speech produces wrong action. Wrong action produces wrong livelihood. Wrong livelihood produces wrong effort. Wrong effort produces wrong mindfulness. Wrong mindfulness produces wrong immersion. Wrong immersion produces wrong knowledge. Wrong knowledge produces wrong freedom.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, micchattaṁ āgamma virādhanā hoti, no ārādhanā.
segs.e: That’s how relying on the wrong way leads to failure, not success.

segs.p: Sammattaṁ, bhikkhave, āgamma ārādhanā hoti, no virādhanā.
segs.e: Relying on the right way leads to success, not failure.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, sammattaṁ āgamma ārādhanā hoti, no virādhanā?
segs.e: And how does relying on the right way lead to success, not failure?

segs.p: Sammādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo pahoti, sammāsaṅkappassa sammāvācā pahoti, sammāvācassa sammākammanto pahoti, sammākammantassa sammāājīvo pahoti, sammāājīvassa sammāvāyāmo pahoti, sammāvāyāmassa sammāsati pahoti, sammāsatissa sammāsamādhi pahoti, sammāsamādhissa sammāñāṇaṁ pahoti, sammāñāṇissa sammāvimutti pahoti.
segs.e: Right view produces right purpose. Right purpose produces right speech. Right speech produces right action. Right action produces right livelihood. Right livelihood produces right effort.
