Right effort produces right mindfulness. Right mindfulness produces right immersion. Right immersion produces right knowledge. Right knowledge produces right freedom.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, sammattaṁ āgamma ārādhanā hoti, no virādhanā”ti.
segs.e: That’s how relying on the right way leads to success, not failure.”
Numbered Discourses 10.104
11. Perceptions for Ascetics
A Seed

segs.p: “Micchādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, purisapuggalassa micchāsaṅkappassa micchāvācassa micchākammantassa micchāājīvassa micchāvāyāmassa micchāsatissa micchāsamādhissa micchāñāṇissa micchāvimuttissa
segs.e: “Mendicants, consider an individual who has wrong view, purpose, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, immersion, knowledge, and freedom.

segs.p: yañca kāyakammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yañca vacīkammaṁ yañca manokammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yā ca cetanā yā ca patthanā yo ca paṇidhi ye ca saṅkhārā, sabbe te dhammā aniṭṭhāya akantāya amanāpāya ahitāya dukkhāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: Whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable, harmful, and suffering.
Why is that?
Because their view is bad.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, nimbabījaṁ vā kosātakibījaṁ vā tittakālābubījaṁ vā allāya pathaviyā nikkhittaṁ yañceva pathavirasaṁ upādiyati yañca āporasaṁ upādiyati, sabbaṁ taṁ tittakattāya kaṭukattāya asātattāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: Suppose a seed of neem, angled gourd, or bitter gourd was planted in moist earth. Whatever nutrients it takes up from the earth and water would lead to its bitter, acerbic, and unpleasant taste.
Why is that?
Because the seed is bad.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, micchādiṭṭhikassa purisapuggalassa micchāsaṅkappassa micchāvācassa micchākammantassa micchāājīvassa micchāvāyāmassa micchāsatissa micchāsamādhissa micchāñāṇissa micchāvimuttissa yañceva kāyakammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yañca vacīkammaṁ …
segs.e: In the same way, consider an individual who has wrong view, purpose, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, immersion, knowledge, and freedom.

segs.p: yañca manokammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yā ca cetanā yā ca patthanā yo ca paṇidhi ye ca saṅkhārā, sabbe te dhammā aniṭṭhāya akantāya amanāpāya ahitāya dukkhāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: Whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable, harmful, and suffering.
Why is that?
Because their view is bad.

segs.p: Sammādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, purisapuggalassa sammāsaṅkappassa sammāvācassa sammākammantassa sammāājīvassa sammāvāyāmassa sammāsatissa sammāsamādhissa sammāñāṇissa sammāvimuttissa yañceva kāyakammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yañca vacīkammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yañca manokammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yā ca cetanā yā ca patthanā yo ca paṇidhi ye ca saṅkhārā, sabbe te dhammā iṭṭhāya kantāya manāpāya hitāya sukhāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: Consider an individual who has right view, purpose, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, immersion, knowledge, and freedom. Whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is likable, desirable, agreeable, beneficial, and pleasant.
Why is that?
Because their view is good.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ucchubījaṁ vā sālibījaṁ vā muddikābījaṁ vā allāya pathaviyā nikkhittaṁ yañca pathavirasaṁ upādiyati yañca āporasaṁ upādiyati sabbaṁ taṁ sātattāya madhurattāya asecanakattāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: Suppose a seed of sugarcane, fine rice, or grape was planted in moist earth. Whatever nutrients it takes up from the earth and water would lead to its sweet, pleasant, delectable flavor.
Why is that?
Because the seed is good.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhikassa …pe… sammāvimuttissa yañceva kāyakammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yañca vacīkammaṁ …
segs.e: In the same way, consider an individual who has right view, purpose, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, immersion, knowledge, and freedom.

segs.p: yañca manokammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yā ca cetanā yā ca patthanā yo ca paṇidhi ye ca saṅkhārā, sabbe te dhammā iṭṭhāya kantāya manāpāya hitāya sukhāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: Whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is likable, desirable, agreeable, beneficial, and pleasant.
Why is that?
Because their view is good.”
Numbered Discourses 10.105
11. Perceptions for Ascetics
Knowledge

segs.p: “Avijjā, bhikkhave, pubbaṅgamā akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ samāpattiyā, anvadeva ahirikaṁ anottappaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, ignorance leads the attainment of unskillful qualities, with lack of conscience and prudence following along.

segs.p: Avijjāgatassa, bhikkhave, aviddasuno micchādiṭṭhi pahoti, micchādiṭṭhikassa micchāsaṅkappo pahoti, micchāsaṅkappassa micchāvācā pahoti, micchāvācassa micchākammanto pahoti, micchākammantassa micchāājīvo pahoti, micchāājīvassa micchāvāyāmo pahoti, micchāvāyāmassa micchāsati pahoti, micchāsatissa micchāsamādhi pahoti, micchāsamādhissa micchāñāṇaṁ pahoti, micchāñāṇissa micchāvimutti pahoti.
segs.e: An ignoramus, sunk in ignorance, produces wrong view. Wrong view produces wrong purpose. Wrong purpose produces wrong speech. Wrong speech produces wrong action. Wrong action produces wrong livelihood. Wrong livelihood produces wrong effort. Wrong effort produces wrong mindfulness. Wrong mindfulness produces wrong immersion. Wrong immersion produces wrong knowledge. Wrong knowledge produces wrong freedom.

segs.p: Vijjā, bhikkhave, pubbaṅgamā kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ samāpattiyā, anvadeva hirottappaṁ.
segs.e: Knowledge leads the attainment of skillful qualities, with conscience and prudence following along.

segs.p: Vijjāgatassa, bhikkhave, viddasuno sammādiṭṭhi pahoti, sammādiṭṭhikassa sammāsaṅkappo pahoti, sammāsaṅkappassa sammāvācā pahoti, sammāvācassa sammākammanto pahoti, sammākammantassa sammāājīvo pahoti, sammāājīvassa sammāvāyāmo pahoti, sammāvāyāmassa sammāsati pahoti, sammāsatissa sammāsamādhi pahoti, sammāsamādhissa sammāñāṇaṁ pahoti, sammāñāṇissa sammāvimutti pahotī”ti.
segs.e: A knowing one, firm in knowledge, produces right view. Right view produces right purpose. Right purpose produces right speech. Right speech produces right action. Right action produces right livelihood. Right livelihood produces right effort. Right effort produces right mindfulness. Right mindfulness produces right immersion. Right immersion produces right knowledge. Right knowledge produces right freedom.”
Numbered Discourses 10.106
11. Perceptions for Ascetics
Wearing Away
“Mendicants, there are these ten grounds for wearing away.
What ten?
For one of right view, wrong view is worn away.

segs.p: ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong view are worn away.

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right view, many skillful qualities are fully developed.
For one of right purpose, wrong purpose is worn away.

segs.p: ye ca micchāsaṅkappapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong purpose are worn away.

segs.p: sammāsaṅkappapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right purpose, many skillful qualities are fully developed.
For one of right speech, wrong speech is worn away.

segs.p: ye ca micchāvācāpaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong speech are worn away.

segs.p: sammāvācāpaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right speech, many skillful qualities are fully developed.
For one of right action, wrong action is worn away.

segs.p: ye ca micchākammantapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong action are worn away.

segs.p: sammākammantapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right action, many skillful qualities are fully developed.
For one of right livelihood, wrong livelihood is worn away.

segs.p: ye ca micchāājīvapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong livelihood are worn away.

segs.p: sammāājīvapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right livelihood, many skillful qualities are fully developed.
For one of right effort, wrong effort is worn away.

segs.p: ye ca micchāvāyāmapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong effort are worn away.

segs.p: sammāvāyāmapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right effort, many skillful qualities are fully developed.
For one of right mindfulness, wrong mindfulness is worn away.

segs.p: ye ca micchāsatipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong mindfulness are worn away.

segs.p: sammāsatipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right mindfulness, many skillful qualities are fully developed.
For one of right immersion, wrong immersion is worn away.

segs.p: ye ca micchāsamādhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong immersion are worn away.

segs.p: sammāsamādhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right immersion, many skillful qualities are fully developed.
For one of right knowledge, wrong knowledge is worn away.

segs.p: ye ca micchāñāṇapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong knowledge are worn away.

segs.p: sammāñāṇapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right knowledge, many skillful qualities are fully developed.
For one of right freedom, wrong freedom is worn away.

segs.p: ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong freedom are worn away.

segs.p: sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right freedom, many skillful qualities are fully developed.
These are the ten grounds for wearing away.”
Numbered Discourses 10.107
11. Perceptions for Ascetics
The Bone-Washing Ceremony
“Mendicants, in the southern lands there is a ceremony named ‘bone-washing’.

segs.p: Tattha hoti annampi pānampi khajjampi bhojjampi leyyampi peyyampi naccampi gītampi vāditampi.
segs.e: There they have food, drink, snacks, meals, refreshments, and beverages, as well as dancing, singing, and music.
There is such a washing, I don’t deny it.

segs.p: Tañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, dhovanaṁ hīnaṁ gammaṁ pothujjanikaṁ anariyaṁ anatthasaṁhitaṁ na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: But that washing is low, crude, ordinary, ignoble, and pointless. It doesn’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

segs.p: Ahañca kho, bhikkhave, ariyaṁ dhovanaṁ desessāmi, yaṁ dhovanaṁ ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattati, yaṁ dhovanaṁ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti, jarādhammā sattā jarāya parimuccanti, maraṇadhammā sattā maraṇena parimuccanti, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccanti.
segs.e: I will teach a noble washing that leads solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment. Relying on that washing, sentient beings who are liable to rebirth, old age, and death, to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are freed from all these things.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Katamañca taṁ, bhikkhave, ariyaṁ dhovanaṁ, yaṁ dhovanaṁ ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattati, yaṁ dhovanaṁ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti, jarādhammā sattā jarāya parimuccanti, maraṇadhammā sattā maraṇena parimuccanti, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccanti?
segs.e: “And what is that noble washing?
For one of right view, wrong view is washed away.

segs.p: ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa niddhotā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong view are washed away.

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right view, many skillful qualities are fully developed.
For one of right purpose, wrong purpose is washed away. …
For one of right speech, wrong speech is washed away. …
For one of right action, wrong action is washed away. …
For one of right livelihood, wrong livelihood is washed away. …
For one of right effort, wrong effort is washed away. …
For one of right mindfulness, wrong mindfulness is washed away. …
For one of right immersion, wrong immersion is washed away. …
For one of right knowledge, wrong knowledge is washed away. …
For one of right freedom, wrong freedom is washed away.

segs.p: ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa niddhotā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong freedom are washed away.

segs.p: sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right freedom, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho taṁ, bhikkhave, ariyaṁ dhovanaṁ ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattati, yaṁ dhovanaṁ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti, jarādhammā sattā jarāya parimuccanti, maraṇadhammā sattā maraṇena parimuccanti, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccantī”ti.
segs.e: This is the noble washing that leads solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment. Relying on this washing, sentient beings who are liable to rebirth, old age, and death, to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are freed from all these things.”
Numbered Discourses 10.108
11. Perceptions for Ascetics
Doctors

segs.p: “Tikicchakā, bhikkhave, virecanaṁ denti pittasamuṭṭhānānampi ābādhānaṁ paṭighātāya, semhasamuṭṭhānānampi ābādhānaṁ paṭighātāya, vātasamuṭṭhānānampi ābādhānaṁ paṭighātāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, doctors prescribe a purgative for eliminating illnesses stemming from disorders of bile, phlegm, and wind.
There is such a purgative, I don’t deny it.

segs.p: Tañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, virecanaṁ sampajjatipi vipajjatipi.
segs.e: But this kind of purgative sometimes works and sometimes fails.

segs.p: Ahañca kho, bhikkhave, ariyaṁ virecanaṁ desessāmi, yaṁ virecanaṁ sampajjatiyeva no vipajjati, yaṁ virecanaṁ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti, jarādhammā sattā jarāya parimuccanti, maraṇadhammā sattā maraṇena parimuccanti, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccanti.
segs.e: I will teach a noble purgative that works without fail. Relying on that purgative, sentient beings who are liable to rebirth, old age, and death, to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are freed from all these things.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Katamañca taṁ, bhikkhave, ariyaṁ virecanaṁ, yaṁ virecanaṁ sampajjatiyeva no vipajjati, yaṁ virecanaṁ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti, jarādhammā sattā jarāya parimuccanti, maraṇadhammā sattā maraṇena parimuccanti, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccanti?
segs.e: “And what is the noble purgative that works without fail?
For one of right view, wrong view is purged.

segs.p: ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa virittā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are purged.

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right view, many skillful qualities are fully developed.
For one of right purpose, wrong purpose is purged. …
For one of right speech, wrong speech is purged. …
For one of right action, wrong action is purged. …
For one of right livelihood, wrong livelihood is purged. …
For one of right effort, wrong effort is purged. …
For one of right mindfulness, wrong mindfulness is purged. …
For one of right immersion, wrong immersion is purged. …
For one of right knowledge, wrong knowledge is purged. …
For one of right freedom, wrong freedom is purged.

segs.p: ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa virittā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong freedom are purged.

segs.p: sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right freedom, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho taṁ, bhikkhave, ariyaṁ virecanaṁ yaṁ virecanaṁ sampajjatiyeva no vipajjati, yaṁ virecanaṁ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti …pe… sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccantī”ti.
segs.e: This is the noble purgative that works without fail. Relying on this purgative, sentient beings who are liable to rebirth, old age, and death, to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are freed from all these things.”
Numbered Discourses 10.109
11. Perceptions for Ascetics
Emetic

segs.p: “Tikicchakā, bhikkhave, vamanaṁ denti pittasamuṭṭhānānampi ābādhānaṁ paṭighātāya, semhasamuṭṭhānānampi ābādhānaṁ paṭighātāya, vātasamuṭṭhānānampi ābādhānaṁ paṭighātāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, doctors prescribe an emetic for eliminating illnesses stemming from disorders of bile, phlegm, and wind.
There is such an emetic, I don’t deny it.

segs.p: Tañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vamanaṁ sampajjatipi vipajjatipi.
segs.e: But this kind of emetic sometimes works and sometimes fails.

segs.p: Ahañca kho, bhikkhave, ariyaṁ vamanaṁ desessāmi, yaṁ vamanaṁ sampajjatiyeva no vipajjati, yaṁ vamanaṁ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti, jarādhammā sattā jarāya parimuccanti, maraṇadhammā sattā maraṇena parimuccanti, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccanti.
segs.e: I will teach a noble emetic that works without fail. Relying on that emetic, sentient beings who are liable to rebirth, old age, and death, to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are freed from all these things.
Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak. …

segs.p: Katamañca taṁ, bhikkhave, ariyaṁ vamanaṁ, yaṁ vamanaṁ sampajjatiyeva no vipajjati, yaṁ vamanaṁ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti …pe… sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccanti?
segs.e: And what is that noble emetic that works without fail?
For one of right view, wrong view is vomited up.

segs.p: ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa vantā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are vomited up.

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right view, many skillful qualities are fully developed.
For one of right purpose, wrong purpose is vomited up. …
For one of right speech, wrong speech is vomited up. …
For one of right action, wrong action is vomited up. …
For one of right livelihood, wrong livelihood is vomited up. …
For one of right effort, wrong effort is vomited up. …
For one of right mindfulness, wrong mindfulness is vomited up. …
For one of right immersion, wrong immersion is vomited up. …
For one of right knowledge, wrong knowledge is vomited up. …
For one of right freedom, wrong freedom is vomited up.

segs.p: ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa vantā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong freedom are vomited up.

segs.p: sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right freedom, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho taṁ, bhikkhave, ariyaṁ vamanaṁ yaṁ vamanaṁ sampajjatiyeva no vipajjati, yaṁ vamanaṁ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti …pe… sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccantī”ti.
segs.e: This is the noble emetic that works without fail. Relying on this emetic, sentient beings who are liable to rebirth, old age, and death, to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are freed from all these things.”
Numbered Discourses 10.110
11. Perceptions for Ascetics
Blown Away
“Mendicants, these ten qualities should be blown away.
What ten?
For one of right view, wrong view is blown away.

segs.p: ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa niddhantā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are blown away.

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right view, many skillful qualities are fully developed.
For one of right purpose, wrong purpose is blown away. …
For one of right speech, wrong speech is blown away. …
For one of right action, wrong action is blown away. …
For one of right livelihood, wrong livelihood is blown away. …
For one of right effort, wrong effort is blown away. …
For one of right mindfulness, wrong mindfulness is blown away. …
For one of right immersion, wrong immersion is blown away. …
For one of right knowledge, wrong knowledge is blown away. …
For one of right freedom, wrong freedom is blown away.

segs.p: ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa niddhantā honti;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong freedom are blown away.

segs.p: sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: And because of right freedom, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa niddhamanīyā dhammā”ti.
segs.e: These are the ten qualities that should be blown away.”
Numbered Discourses 10.111
11. Perceptions for Ascetics
An Adept (1st)

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:
“Sir, they speak of the one called ‘an adept’.
How is an adept mendicant defined?”

segs.p: “Idha, bhikkhu, bhikkhu asekhāya sammādiṭṭhiyā samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāsaṅkappena samannāgato hoti, asekhāya sammāvācāya samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammākammantena samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāājīvena samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāvāyāmena samannāgato hoti, asekhāya sammāsatiyā samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāsamādhinā samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāñāṇena samannāgato hoti, asekhāya sammāvimuttiyā samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: “Mendicant, it’s when a mendicant has an adept’s right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhu, bhikkhu asekho hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is an adept.”
Numbered Discourses 10.112
11. Perceptions for Ascetics
An Adept (2nd)
“Mendicants, there are ten qualities of an adept.
What ten?

segs.p: Asekhā sammādiṭṭhi, asekho sammāsaṅkappo, asekhā sammāvācā, asekho sammākammanto, asekho sammāājīvo, asekho sammāvāyāmo, asekhā sammāsati, asekho sammāsamādhi, asekhaṁ sammāñāṇaṁ, asekhā sammāvimutti—
segs.e: An adept’s right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa asekhiyā dhammā”ti.
segs.e: These are the ten qualities of an adept.”
Numbered Discourses 10.113
12. The Ceremony of Descent
Bad Principles (1st)
“Mendicants, you should know bad principles with bad results.
And you should know good principles with good results.

segs.p: Adhammañca viditvā anatthañca, dhammañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabbaṁ.
segs.e: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, adhammo ca anattho ca?
segs.e: And what are bad principles with bad results?

segs.p: Micchādiṭṭhi, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvācā, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo, micchāsati, micchāsamādhi, micchāñāṇaṁ, micchāvimutti—
segs.e: Wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong immersion, wrong knowledge, and wrong freedom.

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhammo ca anattho ca.
segs.e: These are called bad principles with bad results.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, dhammo ca attho ca?
segs.e: And what are good principles with good results?

segs.p: Sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi, sammāñāṇaṁ, sammāvimutti—
segs.e: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammo ca attho ca.
segs.e: These are called good principles with good results.
‘You should know bad principles with bad results.
And you should know good principles with good results.

segs.p: Adhammañca viditvā anatthañca, dhammañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabban’ti,
segs.e: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ, idametaṁ paṭicca vuttan”ti.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.”
Numbered Discourses 10.114
12. The Ceremony of Descent
Bad Principles (2nd)
“Mendicants, you should know bad principles and good principles.
And you should know bad results and good results.

segs.p: Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabbaṁ.
segs.e: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, adhammo, katamo ca dhammo, katamo ca anattho, katamo ca attho?
segs.e: So what are bad principles? What are good principles? What are bad results? And what are good results?
Wrong view is a bad principle.
Right view is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are bad results.

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right view are good results.
Wrong purpose is a bad principle.
Right purpose is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchāsaṅkappapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong purpose are bad results.

segs.p: sammāsaṅkappapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right purpose are good results.
Wrong speech is a bad principle.
Right speech is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchāvācāpaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong speech are bad results.

segs.p: sammāvācāpaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right speech are good results.
Wrong action is a bad principle.
Right action is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchākammantapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong action are bad results.

segs.p: sammākammantapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right action are good results.
Wrong livelihood is a bad principle.
Right livelihood is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchāājīvapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong livelihood are bad results.

segs.p: sammāājīvapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right livelihood are good results.
Wrong effort is a bad principle.
Right effort is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchāvāyāmapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong effort are bad results.

segs.p: sammāvāyāmapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right effort are good results.
Wrong mindfulness is a bad principle.
Right mindfulness is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchāsatipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong mindfulness are bad results.

segs.p: sammāsatipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right mindfulness are good results.
Wrong immersion is a bad principle.
Right immersion is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchāsamādhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong immersion are bad results.

segs.p: sammāsamādhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right immersion are good results.
Wrong knowledge is a bad principle.
Right knowledge is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchāñāṇapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong knowledge are bad results.

segs.p: sammāñāṇapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right knowledge are good results.
Wrong freedom is a bad principle.
Right freedom is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong freedom are bad results.

segs.p: sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right freedom are good results.
‘You should know bad principles and good principles.
And you should know bad results and good results.

segs.p: Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabban’ti,
segs.e: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ, idametaṁ paṭicca vuttan”ti.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.”
Numbered Discourses 10.115
12. The Ceremony of Descent
Bad Principles (3rd)
“Mendicants, you should know bad principles and good principles.
And you should know bad results and good results.

segs.p: Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabban”ti.
segs.e: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ pāvisi.
segs.e: When he had spoken, the Holy One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling.

segs.p: Atha kho tesaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi:
segs.e: Soon after the Buddha left, those mendicants considered,

segs.p: “idaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
segs.e: “The Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail.

segs.p: Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabban’ti.
Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajeyyā”ti?
segs.e: Who can explain in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha?”
Then they considered,

segs.p: “ayaṁ kho āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
segs.e: “This Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Buddha and esteemed by his sensible spiritual companions.

segs.p: Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
segs.e: He is capable of explaining in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha.

segs.p: Yannūna mayaṁ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāma.
segs.e: Let’s go to him, and ask him about this matter.

segs.p: Yathā no āyasmā ānando byākarissati tathā naṁ dhāressāmā”ti.
segs.e: As he answers, so we’ll remember it.”

segs.p: Atha kho te bhikkhū yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṁ sammodiṁsu.
segs.e: Then those mendicants went to Ānanda, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side. They told him what had happened, and said,

segs.p: “Idaṁ kho no, āvuso ānanda, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
Tesaṁ no, āvuso, amhākaṁ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi:
‘idaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho—
Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajeyyā’ti?
‘ayaṁ kho āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
Yannūna mayaṁ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāma.
Yathā no āyasmā ānando byākarissati tathā naṁ dhāressāmā’ti.

segs.e: “May Venerable Ānanda please explain this.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, āvuso, puriso sāratthiko sāragavesī sārapariyesanaṁ caramāno mahato rukkhassa tiṭṭhato sāravato atikkammeva mūlaṁ atikkamma khandhaṁ sākhāpalāse sāraṁ pariyesitabbaṁ maññeyya;
segs.e: “Reverends, suppose there was a person in need of heartwood. And while wandering in search of heartwood he’d come across a large tree standing with heartwood. But he’d pass over the roots and trunk, imagining that the heartwood should be sought in the branches and leaves.

segs.p: evaṁsampadamidaṁ āyasmantānaṁ satthari sammukhībhūte taṁ bhagavantaṁ atisitvā amhe etamatthaṁ paṭipucchitabbaṁ maññatha.
segs.e: Such is the consequence for the venerables. Though you were face to face with the Buddha, you bypassed him, imagining that you should ask me about this matter.

segs.p: So hāvuso, bhagavā jānaṁ jānāti passaṁ passati, cakkhubhūto ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto vattā pavattā atthassa ninnetā amatassa dātā dhammassāmī tathāgato.
segs.e: For he is the Buddha, the one who knows and sees. He is vision, he is knowledge, he is the manifestation of principle, he is the manifestation of divinity. He is the preacher, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the bestower of freedom from death, the lord of truth, the Realized One.

segs.p: So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṁ tumhe bhagavantaṁyeva upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyātha.
segs.e: That was the time to approach the Buddha and ask about this matter.

segs.p: Yathā vo bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṁ dhāreyyāthā”ti.
segs.e: You should have remembered it in line with the Buddha’s answer.”

segs.p: “Addhāvuso ānanda, bhagavā jānaṁ jānāti passaṁ passati cakkhubhūto ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto vattā pavattā atthassa ninnetā amatassa dātā dhammassāmī tathāgato.
segs.e: “Certainly he is the Buddha, the one who knows and sees. He is vision, he is knowledge, he is the manifestation of principle, he is the manifestation of divinity. He is the preacher, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the bestower of freedom from death, the lord of truth, the Realized One.

segs.p: So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṁ mayaṁ bhagavantaṁyeva upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāma,
segs.e: That was the time to approach the Buddha and ask about this matter.

segs.p: yathā no bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṁ dhāreyyāma.
segs.e: We should have remembered it in line with the Buddha’s answer.

segs.p: Api cāyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
segs.e: Still, Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Buddha and esteemed by his sensible spiritual companions.

segs.p: Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
segs.e: You are capable of explaining in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha.
Please explain this, if it’s no trouble.”
“Then listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” they replied.
Ānanda said this:

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
segs.e: “Reverends, the Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail:
‘You should know bad principles and good principles.
And you should know bad results and good results.

segs.p: Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabban’ti.
segs.e: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.’

segs.p: Katamo cāvuso, adhammo, katamo ca dhammo, katamo ca anattho, katamo ca attho?
segs.e: So what are bad principles? What are good principles? What are bad results? And what are good results?
Wrong view is a bad principle.
Right view is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are bad results.

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right view are good results.
Wrong purpose is a bad principle.
Right purpose is a good principle. …
Wrong speech is a bad principle.
Right speech is a good principle. …
Wrong action is a bad principle.
Right action is a good principle. …
Wrong livelihood is a bad principle.
Right livelihood is a good principle. …
Wrong effort is a bad principle.
Right effort is a good principle. …
Wrong mindfulness is a bad principle.
Right mindfulness is a good principle. …
Wrong immersion is a bad principle.
Right immersion is a good principle. …
Wrong knowledge is a bad principle.
Right knowledge is a good principle. …
Wrong freedom is a bad principle.
Right freedom is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong freedom are bad results.

segs.p: sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right freedom are good results.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
segs.e: The Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail:
‘You should know bad principles and good principles …

segs.p: tathā paṭipajjitabban’ti, imassa kho ahaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi.
segs.e: and practice accordingly.’ And this is how I understand the detailed meaning of this summary recital.

segs.p: Ākaṅkhamānā ca pana tumhe, āvuso, bhagavantaṁyeva upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyātha.
segs.e: If you wish, you may go to the Buddha and ask him about this.

segs.p: Yathā vo bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṁ dhāreyyāthā”ti.
segs.e: You should remember it in line with the Buddha’s answer.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” said those mendicants, approving and agreeing with what Ānanda said. Then they rose from their seats and went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. Then they said:

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho no bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
Tesaṁ no, bhante, amhākaṁ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi:
‘idaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho—
Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajeyyā’ti?
‘ayaṁ kho āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
Yannūna mayaṁ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāma.
Yathā no āyasmā ānando byākarissati tathā naṁ dhāressāmā’ti.
Atha kho mayaṁ, bhante, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamimhā; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etamatthaṁ apucchimhā.
segs.e: “Sir, we went to Ānanda and asked him about this matter.

segs.p: Tesaṁ no, bhante, āyasmatā ānandena imehi ākārehi imehi padehi imehi byañjanehi attho suvibhatto”ti.
segs.e: And Ānanda clearly explained the meaning to us in this manner, with these words and phrases.”
“Good, good, mendicants!
Ānanda is astute,
he has great wisdom.

segs.p: Mañcepi tumhe, bhikkhave, upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyātha, ahampi cetaṁ evamevaṁ byākareyyaṁ yathā taṁ ānandena byākataṁ.
segs.e: If you came to me and asked this question, I would answer it in exactly the same way as Ānanda.

segs.p: Eso ceva tassa attho evañca naṁ dhāreyyāthā”ti.
segs.e: That is what it means, and that’s how you should remember it.”
Numbered Discourses 10.116
12. The Ceremony of Descent
With Ajita

segs.p: Atha kho ajito paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the wanderer Ajita went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho ajito paribbājako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha,
“Worthy Gotama, we have a spiritual companion called ‘Astute’.

segs.p: Tena pañcamattāni cittaṭṭhānasatāni cintitāni, yehi aññatitthiyā upāraddhāva jānanti upāraddhasmā”ti.
segs.e: He has worked out around five hundred arguments by which followers of other religions will know when they’ve been refuted.”
Then the Buddha said to the mendicants,
“Mendicants, do you remember this Astute’s points?”
“Now is the time, Blessed One! Now is the time, Holy One!

segs.p: yaṁ bhagavā bhāseyya, bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.
segs.e: Let the Buddha speak and the mendicants will remember it.”

segs.p: “Tena hi, bhikkhave, suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, mendicants, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco adhammikena vādena adhammikaṁ vādaṁ abhiniggaṇhāti abhinippīḷeti, tena ca adhammikaṁ parisaṁ rañjeti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, take a certain someone who rebuts and quashes unprincipled statements with unprincipled statements. This delights an unprincipled assembly,

segs.p: Tena sā adhammikā parisā uccāsaddamahāsaddā hoti:
segs.e: who make a colossal racket:
‘He is truly astute! He is truly astute!’

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco adhammikena vādena dhammikaṁ vādaṁ abhiniggaṇhāti abhinippīḷeti, tena ca adhammikaṁ parisaṁ rañjeti.
segs.e: Someone else rebuts and quashes principled statements with unprincipled statements. This delights an unprincipled assembly,

segs.p: Tena sā adhammikā parisā uccāsaddamahāsaddā hoti:
segs.e: who make a colossal racket:
‘He is truly astute! He is truly astute!’

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco adhammikena vādena dhammikañca vādaṁ adhammikañca vādaṁ abhiniggaṇhāti abhinippīḷeti, tena ca adhammikaṁ parisaṁ rañjeti.
segs.e: Someone else rebuts and quashes principled and unprincipled statements with unprincipled statements. This delights an unprincipled assembly,

segs.p: Tena sā adhammikā parisā uccāsaddamahāsaddā hoti:
segs.e: who make a colossal racket:
‘He is truly astute! He is truly astute!’

segs.p: Adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo dhammo ca;
segs.e: Mendicants, you should know bad principles and good principles.
And you should know bad results and good results.

segs.p: Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabbaṁ.
segs.e: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, adhammo, katamo ca dhammo, katamo ca anattho, katamo ca attho?
segs.e: So what are bad principles? What are good principles? What are bad results? And what are good results?
Wrong view is a bad principle.
Right view is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are bad results.

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right view are good results.
Wrong purpose is a bad principle.
Right purpose is a good principle. …
Wrong speech is a bad principle.
Right speech is a good principle. …
Wrong action is a bad principle.
Right action is a good principle. …
Wrong livelihood is a bad principle.
Right livelihood is a good principle. …
Wrong effort is a bad principle.
Right effort is a good principle. …
Wrong mindfulness is a bad principle.
Right mindfulness is a good principle. …
Wrong immersion is a bad principle.
Right immersion is a good principle. …
Wrong knowledge is a bad principle.
Right knowledge is a good principle. …
Wrong freedom is a bad principle.
Right freedom is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong freedom are bad results.

segs.p: sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right freedom are good results.
‘You should know bad principles and good principles.
And you should know bad results and good results.

segs.p: Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabban’ti,
segs.e: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ, idametaṁ paṭicca vuttan”ti.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.”
Numbered Discourses 10.117
12. The Ceremony of Descent
With Saṅgārava

segs.p: Atha kho saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Saṅgārava the brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, orimaṁ tīraṁ, kiṁ pārimaṁ tīran”ti?
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, what is the near shore? And what is the far shore?”

segs.p: “Micchādiṭṭhi kho, brāhmaṇa, orimaṁ tīraṁ, sammādiṭṭhi pārimaṁ tīraṁ;
segs.e: “Wrong view is the near shore, brahmin, and right view is the far shore.

segs.p: micchāsaṅkappo orimaṁ tīraṁ, sammāsaṅkappo pārimaṁ tīraṁ;
segs.e: Wrong purpose is the near shore, and right purpose is the far shore.

segs.p: micchāvācā orimaṁ tīraṁ, sammāvācā pārimaṁ tīraṁ;
segs.e: Wrong speech is the near shore, and right speech is the far shore.

segs.p: micchākammanto orimaṁ tīraṁ, sammākammanto pārimaṁ tīraṁ;
segs.e: Wrong action is the near shore, and right action is the far shore.

segs.p: micchāājīvo orimaṁ tīraṁ, sammāājīvo pārimaṁ tīraṁ;
segs.e: Wrong livelihood is the near shore, and right livelihood is the far shore.

segs.p: micchāvāyāmo orimaṁ tīraṁ, sammāvāyāmo pārimaṁ tīraṁ;
segs.e: Wrong effort is the near shore, and right effort is the far shore.

segs.p: micchāsati orimaṁ tīraṁ, sammāsati pārimaṁ tīraṁ;
segs.e: Wrong mindfulness is the near shore, and right mindfulness is the far shore.

segs.p: micchāsamādhi orimaṁ tīraṁ, sammāsamādhi pārimaṁ tīraṁ;
segs.e: Wrong immersion is the near shore, and right immersion is the far shore.

segs.p: micchāñāṇaṁ orimaṁ tīraṁ, sammāñāṇaṁ pārimaṁ tīraṁ;
segs.e: Wrong knowledge is the near shore, and right knowledge is the far shore.

segs.p: micchāvimutti orimaṁ tīraṁ, sammāvimutti pārimaṁ tīranti.
segs.e: Wrong freedom is the near shore, and right freedom is the far shore.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, orimaṁ tīraṁ, idaṁ pārimaṁ tīranti.
segs.e: This is the near shore, and this is the far shore.
Few are those among humans
who cross to the far shore.
The rest just run around
on the near shore.
When the teaching is well explained,
the people who practice accordingly
will cross over
Death’s dominion so hard to pass.
Rid of dark qualities,
an astute person would develop the bright.
Having left home for homelessness
in seclusion, where joy is hard,
they’d long for satisfaction there.
Forsaking sensual pleasures, owning nothing,
an astute person would cleanse themselves
of mental corruptions.
And those whose minds are rightly developed
in the awakening factors;
who, letting go of attachments,
delight in not grasping—
with defilements ended, brilliant,
they are quenched in this world.”

With defilements ended, brilliant,
they are quenched in this world.”
Numbered Discourses 10.119
12. The Ceremony of Descent
The Ceremony of Descent (1st)

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo tadahuposathe sīsaṁnhāto navaṁ khomayugaṁ nivattho allakusamuṭṭhiṁ ādāya bhagavato avidūre ekamantaṁ ṭhito hoti.
segs.e: Now, at that time it was the sabbath. The brahmin Jānussoṇi had bathed his head and dressed in a new pair of linen robes. Holding a handful of fresh grass, he stood to one side not far from the Buddha.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā jāṇussoṇiṁ brāhmaṇaṁ tadahuposathe sīsaṁnhātaṁ navaṁ khomayugaṁ nivatthaṁ allakusamuṭṭhiṁ ādāya ekamantaṁ ṭhitaṁ.
segs.e: The Buddha saw him,
and said,

segs.p: “kiṁ nu tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, tadahuposathe sīsaṁnhāto navaṁ khomayugaṁ nivattho allakusamuṭṭhiṁ ādāya ekamantaṁ ṭhito?
segs.e: “Brahmin, why have you bathed your head and dressed in a new pair of linen robes? Why are you standing to one side holding a handful of fresh grass?
What’s going on today with the brahmin clan?”
“Worthy Gotama, today is the ceremony of descent for the brahmin clan.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇānaṁ paccorohaṇī hotī”ti?
segs.e: “But how do the brahmins observe the ceremony of descent?”

segs.p: “Idha, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā tadahuposathe sīsaṁnhātā navaṁ khomayugaṁ nivatthā allena gomayena pathaviṁ opuñjitvā haritehi kusehi pattharitvā antarā ca velaṁ antarā ca agyāgāraṁ seyyaṁ kappenti.
segs.e: “Well, worthy Gotama, on the sabbath the brahmins bathe their heads and dress in a new pair of linen robes. They make a heap of fresh cow dung and spread it with green grass. Then they make their beds between the boundary and the fire chamber.

segs.p: Te taṁ rattiṁ tikkhattuṁ paccuṭṭhāya pañjalikā aggiṁ namassanti:
segs.e: That night they rise three times and worship the fire with cupped palms:
‘We descend, lord! We descend, lord!’
And they serve the fire with abundant ghee, oil, and butter.

segs.p: Tassā ca rattiyā accayena paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena brāhmaṇe santappenti.
segs.e: And when the night has passed they serve the brahmins with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

segs.p: Evaṁ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇānaṁ paccorohaṇī hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how the brahmins observe the ceremony of descent.”

segs.p: “Aññathā kho, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇānaṁ paccorohaṇī hoti, aññathā ca pana ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hotī”ti.
segs.e: “The ceremony of descent observed by the brahmins is quite different from that observed in the training of the Noble One.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana, bho gotama, ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hoti?
segs.e: “But worthy Gotama, how is the ceremony of descent observed in the training of the Noble One?

segs.p: Sādhu me bhavaṁ gotamo tathā dhammaṁ desetu yathā ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hotī”ti.
segs.e: Worthy Gotama, please teach me this.”

segs.p: “Tena hi, brāhmaṇa, suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, brahmin, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bho”ti kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo bhagavato paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, worthy sir,” Jānussoṇi replied.
The Buddha said this:
“It’s when a noble disciple reflects:
‘Wrong view has a bad result
in both this life and the next.’
Reflecting like this, they give up wrong view,
they descend from wrong view.
‘Wrong purpose has a bad result
in both this life and the next.’
Reflecting like this, they give up wrong purpose,
they descend from wrong purpose.
‘Wrong speech has a bad result
in both this life and the next.’
Reflecting like this, they give up wrong speech,
they descend from wrong speech.
‘Wrong action has a bad result
in both this life and the next.’
Reflecting like this, they give up wrong action,
they descend from wrong action.
‘Wrong livelihood has a bad result
in both this life and the next.’
Reflecting like this, they give up wrong livelihood,
they descend from wrong livelihood.
‘Wrong effort has a bad result
in both this life and the next.’
Reflecting like this, they give up wrong effort,
they descend from wrong effort.
‘Wrong mindfulness has a bad result
in both this life and the next.’
Reflecting like this, they give up wrong mindfulness,
they descend from wrong mindfulness.
‘Wrong immersion has a bad result
in both this life and the next.’
Reflecting like this, they give up wrong immersion,
they descend from wrong immersion.
‘Wrong knowledge has a bad result
in both this life and the next.’
Reflecting like this, they give up wrong knowledge,
they descend from wrong knowledge.
‘Wrong freedom has a bad result
in both this life and the next.’
Reflecting like this, they give up wrong freedom,
they descend from wrong freedom.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hotī”ti.
segs.e: This is the ceremony of descent in the training of the Noble One.”

segs.p: “Aññathā, bho gotama, brāhmaṇānaṁ paccorohaṇī, aññathā ca pana ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hoti.
segs.e: “The ceremony of descent observed by the brahmins is quite different from that observed in the training of the Noble One.

segs.p: Imissā ca, bho gotama, ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇiyā brāhmaṇānaṁ paccorohaṇī kalaṁ nāgghati soḷasiṁ.
segs.e: And, worthy Gotama, the ceremony of descent observed by the brahmins is not worth a sixteenth part of a master of the ceremony of descent observed in the training of the Noble One.
Excellent, worthy Gotama! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Numbered Discourses 10.120
12. The Ceremony of Descent
The Ceremony of Descent (2nd)
“Mendicants, I will teach you the noble descent.
Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak. …
And what is the noble descent?
It’s when a noble disciple reflects:
‘Wrong view has a bad result
in both this life and the next.’
Reflecting like this, they give up wrong view,
they descend from wrong view.
‘Wrong purpose has a bad result …’ …
‘Wrong speech …’ …
‘Wrong action …’ …
‘Wrong livelihood …’ …
‘Wrong effort …’ …
‘Wrong mindfulness …’ …
‘Wrong immersion …’ …
‘Wrong knowledge …’ …
‘Wrong freedom has a bad result
in both this life and the next.’
Reflecting like this, they give up wrong freedom,
they descend from wrong freedom.
This is called the noble descent.”
Numbered Discourses 10.121
12. The Ceremony of Descent
Forerunner

segs.p: “Sūriyassa, bhikkhave, udayato etaṁ pubbaṅgamaṁ etaṁ pubbanimittaṁ, yadidaṁ—aruṇuggaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the dawn is the forerunner and harbinger of the sunrise.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ etaṁ pubbaṅgamaṁ etaṁ pubbanimittaṁ, yadidaṁ—sammādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: In the same way right view is the forerunner and harbinger of skillful qualities.

segs.p: Sammādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo pahoti, sammāsaṅkappassa sammāvācā pahoti, sammāvācassa sammākammanto pahoti, sammākammantassa sammāājīvo pahoti, sammāājīvassa sammāvāyāmo pahoti, sammāvāyāmassa sammāsati pahoti, sammāsatissa sammāsamādhi pahoti, sammāsamādhissa sammāñāṇaṁ pahoti, sammāñāṇissa sammāvimutti pahotī”ti.
segs.e: Right view produces right purpose. Right purpose produces right speech. Right speech produces right action. Right action produces right livelihood. Right livelihood produces right effort. Right effort produces right mindfulness. Right mindfulness produces right immersion. Right immersion produces right knowledge. Right knowledge produces right freedom.”
Numbered Discourses 10.122
12. The Ceremony of Descent
The Ending of Defilements

segs.p: “Dasayime, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā āsavānaṁ khayāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these ten things, when developed and cultivated, lead to the ending of defilements.
What ten?

segs.p: Sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi, sammāñāṇaṁ, sammāvimutti—
segs.e: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā āsavānaṁ khayāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These ten things, when developed and cultivated, lead to the ending of defilements.”
Numbered Discourses 10.123

“Mendicants, there are ten wrong ways.
What ten?

segs.p: Micchādiṭṭhi, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvācā, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo, micchāsati, micchāsamādhi, micchāñāṇaṁ, micchāvimutti—
segs.e: Wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong immersion, wrong knowledge, and wrong freedom.
These are the ten wrong ways.”

14. Good
Good
“Mendicants, I will teach you what is good and what is not good.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“And what, mendicants, is not good?

segs.p: Micchādiṭṭhi, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvācā, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo, micchāsati, micchāsamādhi, micchāñāṇaṁ, micchāvimutti—
segs.e: Wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong immersion, wrong knowledge, and wrong freedom.
This is called what is not good.
And what is good?

segs.p: Sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi, sammāñāṇaṁ, sammāvimutti—
segs.e: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.
This is called what is good.”

This is called what is not the teaching of the noble ones.
And what is the teaching of the noble ones?
Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.
This is called the teaching of the noble ones.”

The True Teaching
“I will teach you what is the true teaching and what is not the true teaching. …
And what is not the true teaching?
Wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong immersion, wrong knowledge, and wrong freedom.
This is called what is not the true teaching.
And what is the true teaching?
Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.
This is called the true teaching.”

The Teaching of the True Persons

16. Individuals
You Should Associate

segs.p: “Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato puggalo na sevitabbo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, you should not associate with an individual who has ten qualities.
What ten?

segs.p: Micchādiṭṭhiko hoti, micchāsaṅkappo hoti, micchāvāco hoti, micchākammanto hoti, micchāājīvo hoti, micchāvāyāmo hoti, micchāsati hoti, micchāsamādhi hoti, micchāñāṇī hoti, micchāvimutti hoti—
segs.e: Wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong immersion, wrong knowledge, and wrong freedom.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato puggalo na sevitabbo.
segs.e: You should not associate with an individual who has these ten qualities.

segs.p: Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato puggalo sevitabbo.
segs.e: You should associate with an individual who has ten qualities.
What ten?

segs.p: Sammādiṭṭhiko hoti, sammāsaṅkappo hoti, sammāvāco hoti, sammākammanto hoti, sammāājīvo hoti, sammāvāyāmo hoti, sammāsati hoti, sammāsamādhi hoti, sammāñāṇī hoti, sammāvimutti hoti—
segs.e: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato puggalo sevitabbo”ti.

16. Individuals
Frequenting, Etc.

segs.p: “Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato puggalo na bhajitabbo …pe…
segs.e: “Mendicants, you should not frequent an individual who has ten qualities. …
you should frequent …
you should not pay homage …
you should pay homage …
you should not venerate …
you should venerate …
you should not praise …
you should praise …
you should not respect …
you should respect …
you should not revere …
you should revere …
is not a success …
is a success …
is not pure …
is pure …
does not win over conceit …
wins over conceit …
does not grow in wisdom …
grows in wisdom …
brims with much wickedness …
brims with much merit.
What ten?

segs.p: Sammādiṭṭhiko hoti, sammāsaṅkappo hoti, sammāvāco hoti, sammākammanto hoti, sammāājīvo hoti, sammāvāyāmo hoti, sammāsati hoti, sammāsamādhi hoti, sammāñāṇī hoti, sammāvimutti hoti—

segs.e: An individual who has these ten qualities brims with much merit.”
Numbered Discourses 10.167
17. With Jāṇussoṇī
The Brahmin Ceremony of Descent

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo tadahuposathe sīsaṁnhāto navaṁ khomayugaṁ nivattho allakusamuṭṭhiṁ ādāya bhagavato avidūre ekamantaṁ ṭhito hoti.
segs.e: Now, at that time it was the sabbath. The brahmin Jānussoṇi had bathed his head and dressed in a new pair of linen robes. Holding a handful of fresh grass, he stood to one side not far from the Buddha.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā jāṇussoṇiṁ brāhmaṇaṁ tadahuposathe sīsaṁnhātaṁ navaṁ khomayugaṁ nivatthaṁ allakusamuṭṭhiṁ ādāya ekamantaṁ ṭhitaṁ.
segs.e: The Buddha saw him,
and said,

segs.p: “kiṁ nu tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, tadahuposathe sīsaṁnhāto navaṁ khomayugaṁ nivattho allakusamuṭṭhiṁ ādāya ekamantaṁ ṭhito?
segs.e: “Brahmin, why have you bathed your head and dressed in a new pair of linen robes? Why are you standing to one side holding a handful of fresh grass?
What’s going on today with the brahmin clan?”
“Worthy Gotama, today is the ceremony of descent for the brahmin clan.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇānaṁ paccorohaṇī hotī”ti?
segs.e: “But how do the brahmins observe the ceremony of descent?”

segs.p: “Idha, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā tadahuposathe sīsaṁnhātā navaṁ khomayugaṁ nivatthā allena gomayena pathaviṁ opuñjitvā haritehi kusehi pattharitvā antarā ca velaṁ antarā ca agyāgāraṁ seyyaṁ kappenti.
segs.e: “Well, worthy Gotama, on the sabbath the brahmins bathe their heads and dress in a new pair of linen robes. They make a heap of fresh cow dung and spread it with green grass. Then they make their beds between the boundary and the fire chamber.

segs.p: Te taṁ rattiṁ tikkhattuṁ paccuṭṭhāya pañjalikā aggiṁ namassanti:
segs.e: That night they rise three times and worship the fire with cupped palms:
‘We descend, lord! We descend, lord!’
And they serve the fire with abundant ghee, oil, and butter.

segs.p: Tassā ca rattiyā accayena paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena brāhmaṇe santappenti.
segs.e: And when the night has passed they serve the brahmins with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

segs.p: Evaṁ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇānaṁ paccorohaṇī hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how the brahmins observe the ceremony of descent.”

segs.p: “Aññathā kho, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇānaṁ paccorohaṇī hoti, aññathā ca pana ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hotī”ti.
segs.e: “The ceremony of descent observed by the brahmins is quite different from that observed in the training of the Noble One.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana, bho gotama, ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hoti?
segs.e: “But worthy Gotama, how is the ceremony of descent observed in the training of the Noble One?

segs.p: Sādhu me bhavaṁ gotamo tathā dhammaṁ desetu yathā ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hotī”ti.
segs.e: Worthy Gotama, please teach me this.”

segs.p: “Tena hi, brāhmaṇa, suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, brahmin, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bho”ti kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo bhagavato paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, worthy sir,” Jānussoṇi replied.
The Buddha said this:
“It’s when a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘pāṇātipātassa kho pāpako vipāko diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Killing living creatures has a bad result in the present life and in lives to come.’
Reflecting like this, they give up killing living creatures,
they descend from killing living creatures.
… ‘Stealing has a bad result
in the present life and in lives to come.’
Reflecting like this, they give up stealing,
they descend from stealing.
… ‘Sexual misconduct has a bad result
in the present life and in lives to come.’
Reflecting like this, they give up sexual misconduct,
they descend from sexual misconduct.
… ‘Lying has a bad result
in the present life and in lives to come.’
Reflecting like this, they give up lying,
they descend from lying.
… ‘Backbiting has a bad result
in the present life and in lives to come.’

segs.p: So iti paṭisaṅkhāya pisuṇaṁ vācaṁ pajahati;
segs.e: Reflecting like this, they give up backbiting,
they descend from backbiting.
… ‘Harsh speech has a bad result
in the present life and in lives to come.’

segs.p: So iti paṭisaṅkhāya pharusaṁ vācaṁ pajahati;
segs.e: Reflecting like this, they give up harsh speech,
they descend from harsh speech.
… ‘Talking nonsense has a bad result
in the present life and in lives to come.’
Reflecting like this, they give up talking nonsense,
they descend from talking nonsense.
… ‘Covetousness has a bad result
in the present life and in lives to come.’
Reflecting like this, they give up covetousness,
they descend from covetousness.
… ‘Ill will has a bad result
in the present life and in lives to come.’
Reflecting like this, they give up ill will,
they descend from ill will.
‘Wrong view has a bad result
in the present life and in lives to come.’
Reflecting like this, they give up wrong view,
they descend from wrong view.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hotī”ti.
segs.e: This is the ceremony of descent in the training of the Noble One.”

segs.p: “Aññathā kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇānaṁ paccorohaṇī hoti, aññathā ca pana ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hoti.
segs.e: “The ceremony of descent observed by the brahmins is quite different from that observed in the training of the Noble One.

segs.p: Imissā, bho gotama, ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇiyā brāhmaṇānaṁ paccorohaṇī kalaṁ nāgghati soḷasiṁ.
segs.e: And, worthy Gotama, the ceremony of descent observed by the brahmins is not worth a sixteenth part of the ceremony of descent observed in the training of the Noble One.
Excellent, worthy Gotama, excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Numbered Discourses 10.168
17. With Jānussoṇi
The Noble Descent
“Mendicants, I will teach you the noble descent.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“And what, mendicants, is the noble descent?
It’s when a noble disciple reflects:
‘Killing living creatures has a bad result
in the present life and in lives to come.’
Reflecting like this, they give up killing living creatures,
they descend from killing living creatures.
… ‘Stealing has a bad result
in the present life and in lives to come.’
Reflecting like this, they give up stealing,
they descend from stealing.
… ‘Sexual misconduct has a bad result …’ …
they descend from sexual misconduct.
… ‘Lying has a bad result …’ …
they descend from lying.
… ‘Backbiting has a bad result …’ …
they descend from backbiting.
… ‘Harsh speech has a bad result …’ …
they descend from harsh speech.
… ‘Talking nonsense has a bad result …’ …
they descend from talking nonsense.
… ‘Covetousness has a bad result …’ …
they descend from covetousness.
… ‘Ill will has a bad result …’ …
they descend from ill will.

segs.p: … ‘Micchādiṭṭhiyā kho pāpako vipāko diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcā’ti.
segs.e: … ‘Wrong view has a bad result both in the present life and in lives to come.’
Reflecting like this, they give up wrong view,
they descend from wrong view.
This is called the noble descent.”
Numbered Discourses 10.169
17. With Jānussoṇi
With Saṅgārava

segs.p: Atha kho saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Saṅgārava the brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, orimaṁ tīraṁ, kiṁ pārimaṁ tīran”ti?
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, what is the near shore? And what is the far shore?”

segs.p: “Pāṇātipāto kho, brāhmaṇa, orimaṁ tīraṁ, pāṇātipātā veramaṇī pārimaṁ tīraṁ.
segs.e: “Killing living creatures is the near shore, brahmin, and not killing living creatures is the far shore.

segs.p: Adinnādānaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, orimaṁ tīraṁ, adinnādānā veramaṇī pārimaṁ tīraṁ.
segs.e: Stealing is the near shore, and not stealing is the far shore.

segs.p: Kāmesumicchācāro orimaṁ tīraṁ, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī pārimaṁ tīraṁ.
segs.e: Sexual misconduct is the near shore, and refraining from sexual misconduct is the far shore.

segs.p: Musāvādo orimaṁ tīraṁ, musāvādā veramaṇī pārimaṁ tīraṁ.
segs.e: Lying is the near shore, and not lying is the far shore.

segs.p: Pisuṇā vācā orimaṁ tīraṁ, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī pārimaṁ tīraṁ.
segs.e: Divisive speech is the near shore, and refraining from divisive speech is the far shore.

segs.p: Pharusā vācā orimaṁ tīraṁ, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī pārimaṁ tīraṁ.
segs.e: Harsh speech is the near shore, and refraining from harsh speech is the far shore.

segs.p: Samphappalāpo orimaṁ tīraṁ, samphappalāpā veramaṇī pārimaṁ tīraṁ.
segs.e: Talking nonsense is the near shore, and refraining from talking nonsense is the far shore.

segs.p: Abhijjhā orimaṁ tīraṁ, anabhijjhā pārimaṁ tīraṁ.
segs.e: Covetousness is the near shore, and contentment is the far shore.

segs.p: Byāpādo orimaṁ tīraṁ, abyāpādo pārimaṁ tīraṁ.
segs.e: Ill will is the near shore, and good will is the far shore.

segs.p: Micchādiṭṭhi orimaṁ tīraṁ, sammādiṭṭhi pārimaṁ tīraṁ.
segs.e: Wrong view is the near shore, and right view is the far shore.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, orimaṁ tīraṁ, idaṁ pārimaṁ tīranti.
segs.e: This is the near shore, and this is the far shore.
Few are those among humans
who cross to the far shore.
The rest just run
around on the near shore.
When the teaching is well explained,
the people who practice accordingly
will cross over
Death’s dominion so hard to pass.
Rid of dark qualities,
an astute person would develop the bright.
Having left home for homelessness
in seclusion, where joy is hard,
they’d long for satisfaction there.
Forsaking sensual pleasures, owning nothing,
an astute person would cleanse themselves
of mental corruptions.
And those whose minds are rightly developed
in the awakening factors;
who, letting go of attachments,
delight in not grasping—
with defilements ended, brilliant,
they are quenched in this world.”
Numbered Discourses 10.170
