17. With Jānussoṇi
Bad Principles (1st)
“Mendicants, you should know bad principles with bad results.
And you should know good principles with good results.

segs.p: Adhammañca viditvā anatthañca, dhammañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabbaṁ.
segs.e: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, adhammo ca anattho ca?
segs.e: And what are bad principles with bad results?

segs.p: Pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṁ, kāmesumicchācāro, musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo, abhijjhā, byāpādo, micchādiṭṭhi—
segs.e: Killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical; covetousness, ill will, and wrong view.

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhammo ca anattho ca.
segs.e: These are called bad principles with bad results.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, dhammo ca attho ca?
segs.e: And what are good principles with good results?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī, musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī, anabhijjhā, abyāpādo, sammādiṭṭhi—
segs.e: Refraining from killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; refraining from speech that’s false, divisive, harsh, or nonsensical; contentment, good will, and right view.

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammo ca attho ca.
segs.e: These are called good principles with good results.
‘You should know bad principles with bad results.
And you should know good principles with good results.

segs.p: Adhammañca viditvā anatthañca, dhammañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabban’ti,
segs.e: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ, idametaṁ paṭicca vuttan”ti.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.”
Numbered Discourses 10.172
17. With Jānussoṇi
Bad Principles (2nd)
“Mendicants, you should know bad principles and good principles.
And you should know bad results and good results.

segs.p: Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabban”ti.
segs.e: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ pāvisi.
segs.e: When he had spoken, the Holy One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling.

segs.p: Atha kho tesaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi:
segs.e: Soon after the Buddha left, those mendicants considered,

segs.p: “idaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
segs.e: “The Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail.
‘You should know bad principles and good principles.
And you should know bad results and good results.

segs.p: Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabban’ti.
segs.e: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.’

segs.p: Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajeyyā”ti?
segs.e: Who can explain in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha?”
Then those mendicants thought,

segs.p: “ayaṁ kho āyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
segs.e: “This Venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Buddha and esteemed by his sensible spiritual companions.

segs.p: Pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
segs.e: He is capable of explaining in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha.

segs.p: Yannūna mayaṁ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ etamatthaṁ puccheyyāma.
segs.e: Let’s go to him, and ask him about this matter.

segs.p: Yathā no āyasmā mahākaccāno byākarissati tathā naṁ dhāressāmā”ti.
segs.e: As he answers, so we’ll remember it.”

segs.p: Atha kho te bhikkhū yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahākaccānena saddhiṁ sammodiṁsu.
segs.e: Then those mendicants went to Mahākaccāna, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side. They told him what had happened, and said,

segs.p: “Idaṁ kho no, āvuso kaccāna, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabban’ti.
Tesaṁ no, āvuso, amhākaṁ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi:
‘idaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho—
Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajeyyā’ti?
‘ayaṁ kho āyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
Pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
Yannūna mayaṁ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāma.
Yathā no āyasmā mahākaccāno byākarissati tathā naṁ dhāressāmā’ti.

segs.e: “May Venerable Mahākaccāna please explain this.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, āvuso, puriso sāratthiko sāraṁ gavesī sārapariyesanaṁ caramāno mahato rukkhassa tiṭṭhato sāravato atikkammeva mūlaṁ atikkamma khandhaṁ sākhāpalāse sāraṁ pariyesitabbaṁ maññeyya.
segs.e: “Reverends, suppose there was a person in need of heartwood. And while wandering in search of heartwood he’d come across a large tree standing with heartwood. But he’d pass over the roots and trunk, imagining that the heartwood should be sought in the branches and leaves.

segs.p: Evaṁsampadamidaṁ āyasmantānaṁ satthari sammukhībhūte taṁ bhagavantaṁ atisitvā amhe etamatthaṁ paṭipucchitabbaṁ maññatha.
segs.e: Such is the consequence for the venerables. Though you were face to face with the Buddha, you bypassed him, imagining that you should ask me about this matter.

segs.p: So hāvuso, bhagavā jānaṁ jānāti passaṁ passati cakkhubhūto ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto vattā pavattā atthassa ninnetā amatassa dātā dhammassāmī tathāgato.
segs.e: For he is the Buddha, the one who knows and sees. He is vision, he is knowledge, he is the manifestation of principle, he is the manifestation of divinity. He is the preacher, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the bestower of freedom from death, the lord of truth, the Realized One.

segs.p: So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṁ tumhe bhagavantaṁyeva upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyātha.
segs.e: That was the time to approach the Buddha and ask about this matter.

segs.p: Yathā vo bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṁ dhāreyyāthā”ti.
segs.e: You should have remembered it in line with the Buddha’s answer.”

segs.p: “Addhā, āvuso kaccāna, bhagavā jānaṁ jānāti passaṁ passati cakkhubhūto ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto vattā pavattā atthassa ninnetā amatassa dātā dhammassāmī tathāgato.
segs.e: “Certainly he is the Buddha, the one who knows and sees. He is vision, he is knowledge, he is the manifestation of principle, he is the manifestation of divinity. He is the preacher, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the bestower of freedom from death, the lord of truth, the Realized One.

segs.p: So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṁ mayaṁ bhagavantaṁyeva upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāma.
segs.e: That was the time to approach the Buddha and ask about this matter.

segs.p: Yathā no bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṁ dhāreyyāma.
segs.e: We should have remembered it in line with the Buddha’s answer.

segs.p: Api cāyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
segs.e: Still, Venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Buddha and esteemed by his sensible spiritual companions.

segs.p: Pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
segs.e: He is capable of explaining in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha.
Please explain this, if it’s no trouble.”

segs.p: “Tena hāvuso, suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, reverends, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahākaccānassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” they replied.
Mahākaccāna said this:

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
segs.e: “Reverends, the Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail:
‘You should know bad principles and good principles …
and practice accordingly.’

segs.p: Katamo cāvuso, adhammo; katamo ca dhammo?
segs.e: So what are bad principles? What are good principles?

segs.p: Katamo ca anattho, katamo ca attho?
segs.e: What are bad results? And what are good results?
Killing living creatures is a bad principle.
Not killing living creatures is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca pāṇātipātapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by killing living creatures are bad results.

segs.p: pāṇātipātā veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of not killing living creatures are good results.
Stealing is a bad principle.
Not stealing is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca adinnādānapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by stealing are bad results.

segs.p: adinnādānā veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of not stealing are good results.
Sexual misconduct is a bad principle.
Refraining from sexual misconduct is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca kāmesumicchācārapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by sexual misconduct are bad results.

segs.p: kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of refraining from sexual misconduct are good results.
Lying is a bad principle.
Not lying is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca musāvādapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by lying are bad results.

segs.p: musāvādā veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of not lying are good results.
Backbiting is a bad principle.
Refraining from divisive speech is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca pisuṇāvācāpaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by backbiting are bad results.

segs.p: pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of refraining from divisive speech are good results.
Harsh speech is a bad principle.
Refraining from harsh speech is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca pharusāvācāpaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by harsh speech are bad results.

segs.p: pharusāya vācāya veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of refraining from harsh speech are good results.
Talking nonsense is a bad principle.
Refraining from talking nonsense is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca samphappalāpapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by talking nonsense are bad results.

segs.p: samphappalāpā veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of refraining from talking nonsense are good results.
Covetousness is a bad principle.
Contentment is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca abhijjhāpaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by covetousness are bad results.

segs.p: anabhijjhāpaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of contentment are good results.
Ill will is a bad principle.
Good will is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca byāpādapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by ill will are bad results.

segs.p: abyāpādapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of good will are good results.
Wrong view is a bad principle.
Right view is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are bad results.

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right view are good results.

segs.p: ‘Yaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho—
segs.e: The Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail:
‘You should know bad principles and good principles …
and practice accordingly.’

segs.p: Imassa kho ahaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi.
segs.e: And this is how I understand the detailed meaning of this summary recital.

segs.p: Ākaṅkhamānā ca pana tumhe, āvuso, bhagavantaṁyeva upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyātha.
segs.e: If you wish, you may go to the Buddha and ask him about this.

segs.p: Yathā no bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṁ dhāreyyāthā”ti.
segs.e: You should remember it in line with the Buddha’s answer.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahākaccānassa bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” said those mendicants, approving and agreeing with what Mahākaccāna said. Then they rose from their seats and went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. Then they said:

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho no, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
Tesaṁ no, bhante, amhākaṁ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi:
‘idaṁ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṅkhittena uddesaṁ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṁ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ paviṭṭho:
Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajeyyā’ti?
‘ayaṁ kho āyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṁvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṁ sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
Pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajituṁ.
Yannūna mayaṁ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyāma.
Yathā no āyasmā mahākaccāno byākarissati tathā naṁ dhāressāmā’ti.
Atha kho mayaṁ, bhante, yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkamimhā; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ etamatthaṁ apucchimhā.
segs.e: “Sir, we went to Mahākaccāna and asked him about this matter.

segs.p: Tesaṁ no, bhante, āyasmatā mahākaccānena imehi akkharehi imehi padehi imehi byañjanehi attho suvibhatto”ti.
segs.e: And Mahākaccāna clearly explained the meaning to us in this manner, with these words and phrases.”
“Good, good, mendicants!

segs.p: Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, mahākaccāno. Mahāpañño, bhikkhave, mahākaccāno.
segs.e: Mahākaccāna is astute, he has great wisdom.

segs.p: Mañcepi tumhe, bhikkhave, upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṁ paṭipuccheyyātha, ahampi cetaṁ evamevaṁ byākareyyaṁ yathā taṁ mahākaccānena byākataṁ.
segs.e: If you came to me and asked this question, I would answer it in exactly the same way as Mahākaccāna.

segs.p: Eso ceva tassa attho. Evañca naṁ dhāreyyāthā”ti.
segs.e: That is what it means, and that’s how you should remember it.”
Numbered Discourses 10.173
17. With Jānussoṇi
Bad Principles (3rd)
“Mendicants, you should know bad principles and good principles.
And you should know bad results and good results.

segs.p: Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabbaṁ.
segs.e: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, adhammo, katamo ca dhammo;
segs.e: So what are bad principles? What are good principles? What are bad results? And what are good results?

segs.p: katamo ca anattho, katamo ca attho?

segs.e: Killing living creatures is a bad principle.
Refraining from killing living creatures is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca pāṇātipātapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by killing living creatures are bad results.

segs.p: pāṇātipātā veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of not killing living creatures are good results.
Stealing is a bad principle.
Refraining from stealing is a good principle. …
Sexual misconduct is a bad principle.
Refraining from sexual misconduct is a good principle. …
Lying is a bad principle.
Refraining from lying is a good principle. …
Backbiting is a bad principle.
Refraining from divisive speech is a good principle. …
Harsh speech is a bad principle.
Refraining from harsh speech is a good principle. …
Talking nonsense is a bad principle.
Refraining from talking nonsense is a good principle. …
Covetousness is a bad principle.
Contentment is a good principle. …
Ill will is a bad principle.
Good will is a good principle. …
Wrong view is a bad principle.
Right view is a good principle.

segs.p: ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṁ anattho;
segs.e: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are bad results.

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti, ayaṁ attho.
segs.e: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right view are good results.
‘You should know bad principles and good principles.
And you should know bad results and good results.

segs.p: Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabban’ti,
segs.e: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ, idametaṁ paṭicca vuttan”ti.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.”
Numbered Discourses 10.174
17. With Jānussoṇi
Sources of Deeds
“Mendicants, I say that killing living creatures is threefold:
caused by greed, hate, or delusion.
I say that stealing is threefold:
caused by greed, hate, or delusion.
I say that sexual misconduct is threefold:
caused by greed, hate, or delusion.
I say that lying is threefold:
caused by greed, hate, or delusion.
I say that backbiting is threefold:
caused by greed, hate, or delusion.
I say that harsh speech is threefold:
caused by greed, hate, or delusion.
I say that talking nonsense is threefold:
caused by greed, hate, or delusion.
I say that covetousness is threefold:
caused by greed, hate, or delusion.
I say that ill will is threefold:
caused by greed, hate, or delusion.
I say that wrong view is threefold:
caused by greed, hate, or delusion.

segs.p: Iti kho, bhikkhave, lobho kammanidānasambhavo, doso kammanidānasambhavo, moho kammanidānasambhavo.
segs.e: And so greed, hate, and delusion are sources and origins for deeds.

segs.p: Lobhakkhayā kammanidānasaṅkhayo, dosakkhayā kammanidānasaṅkhayo, mohakkhayā kammanidānasaṅkhayo”ti.
segs.e: With the ending of greed, hate, and delusion, the sources of deeds are ended.”
Numbered Discourses 10.175
17. With Jānussoṇi
The Bypass

segs.p: “Saparikkamano ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammo, nāyaṁ dhammo aparikkamano.
segs.e: “Mendicants, this teaching provides a bypass, it doesn’t lack a bypass.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, saparikkamano ayaṁ dhammo, nāyaṁ dhammo aparikkamano?
segs.e: And how does this teaching provide a bypass, not lacking a bypass?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātissa, bhikkhave, pāṇātipātā veramaṇī parikkamanaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Not killing living creatures bypasses killing living creatures.

segs.p: Adinnādāyissa, bhikkhave, adinnādānā veramaṇī parikkamanaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Not stealing bypasses stealing.

segs.p: Kāmesumicchācārissa, bhikkhave, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī parikkamanaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Refraining from sexual misconduct bypasses sexual misconduct.

segs.p: Musāvādissa, bhikkhave, musāvādā veramaṇī parikkamanaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Not lying bypasses lying.

segs.p: Pisuṇavācassa, bhikkhave, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī parikkamanaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Refraining from divisive speech bypasses divisive speech.

segs.p: Pharusavācassa, bhikkhave, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī parikkamanaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Refraining from harsh speech bypasses harsh speech.

segs.p: Samphappalāpissa, bhikkhave, samphappalāpā veramaṇī parikkamanaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Refraining from talking nonsense bypasses talking nonsense.
Contentment bypasses covetousness.
Good will bypasses ill will.
Right view bypasses wrong view.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, saparikkamano ayaṁ dhammo, nāyaṁ dhammo aparikkamano”ti.
segs.e: That’s how this teaching provides a bypass, it doesn’t lack a bypass.”
Numbered Discourses 10.176
17. With Jānussoṇi
With Cunda
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā pāvāyaṁ viharati cundassa kammāraputtassa ambavane.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Pāvā in Cunda the smith’s mango grove.

segs.p: Atha kho cundo kammāraputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho cundaṁ kammāraputtaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Cunda the smith went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,
“Cunda, whose purity do you believe in?”

segs.p: “Brāhmaṇā, bhante, pacchābhūmakā kamaṇḍalukā sevālamālikā aggiparicārikā udakorohakā soceyyāni paññapenti; tesāhaṁ soceyyāni rocemī”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, I believe in the purity advocated by the western brahmins garlanded with aquatic flowers who carry pitchers, serve the sacred flame, and immerse themselves in water.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana, cunda, brāhmaṇā pacchābhūmakā kamaṇḍalukā sevālamālikā aggiparicārikā udakorohakā soceyyāni paññapentī”ti?
segs.e: “But Cunda, what kind of purity do these western brahmins advocate?”

segs.p: “Idha, bhante, brāhmaṇā pacchābhūmakā kamaṇḍalukā sevālamālikā aggiparicārikā udakorohakā. Te sāvakaṁ evaṁ samādapenti:
segs.e: “The western brahmins encourage their disciple like this:

segs.p: ‘ehi tvaṁ, ambho purisa, kālasseva uṭṭhahantova sayanamhā pathaviṁ āmaseyyāsi;
segs.e: ‘Please, my man, rising early you should stroke the earth from your bed.

segs.p: no ce pathaviṁ āmaseyyāsi, allāni gomayāni āmaseyyāsi;
segs.e: If you don’t stroke the earth, stroke fresh cow dung.

segs.p: no ce allāni gomayāni āmaseyyāsi, haritāni tiṇāni āmaseyyāsi;
segs.e: If you don’t stroke fresh cow dung, stroke green grass.

segs.p: no ce haritāni tiṇāni āmaseyyāsi, aggiṁ paricareyyāsi;
segs.e: If you don’t stroke green grass, serve the sacred flame.

segs.p: no ce aggiṁ paricareyyāsi, pañjaliko ādiccaṁ namasseyyāsi;
segs.e: If you don’t serve the sacred flame, revere the sun with cupped palms.

segs.p: no ce pañjaliko ādiccaṁ namasseyyāsi, sāyatatiyakaṁ udakaṁ oroheyyāsī’ti.
segs.e: If you don’t revere the sun with cupped palms, immerse yourself in water three times, including at dusk.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhante, brāhmaṇā pacchābhūmakā kamaṇḍalukā sevālamālikā aggiparicārikā udakorohakā soceyyāni paññapenti; tesāhaṁ soceyyāni rocemī”ti.
segs.e: The western brahmins advocate this kind of purity.”

segs.p: “Aññathā kho, cunda, brāhmaṇā pacchābhūmakā kamaṇḍalukā sevālamālikā aggiparicārikā udakorohakā soceyyāni paññapenti, aññathā ca pana ariyassa vinaye soceyyaṁ hotī”ti.
segs.e: “The purity advocated by the western brahmins is quite different from that in the training of the Noble One.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana, bhante, ariyassa vinaye soceyyaṁ hoti?
segs.e: “But what, sir, is purity in the training of the Noble One?

segs.p: Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā tathā dhammaṁ desetu yathā ariyassa vinaye soceyyaṁ hotī”ti.
segs.e: Sir, please teach me this.”

segs.p: “Tena hi, cunda, suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, brahmin, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho cundo kammāraputto bhagavato paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” Cunda replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Cunda, impurity is threefold by way of body,
fourfold by way of speech,
and threefold by way of mind.

segs.p: Kathañca, cunda, tividhaṁ kāyena asoceyyaṁ hoti?
segs.e: And how is impurity threefold by way of body?

segs.p: Idha, cunda, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtesu.
segs.e: It’s when someone kills living creatures. They’re violent, bloody-handed, a hardened killer, merciless to all living beings.

segs.p: Adinnādāyī hoti. Yaṁ taṁ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṁ gāmagataṁ vā araññagataṁ vā taṁ adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādātā hoti.
segs.e: They steal. With the intention to commit theft, they take the wealth or belongings of others from village or wilderness.

segs.p: Kāmesumicchācārī hoti. Yā tā māturakkhitā piturakkhitā mātāpiturakkhitā bhāturakkhitā bhaginirakkhitā ñātirakkhitā gottarakkhitā dhammarakkhitā sasāmikā saparidaṇḍā antamaso mālāguḷaparikkhittāpi, tathārūpāsu cārittaṁ āpajjitā hoti.
segs.e: They commit sexual misconduct. They have relations with women who have their mother, father, both mother and father, brother, sister, relatives, or clan as guardian. They have relations with a woman who is protected on principle, or who has a husband, or whose violation is punishable by law, or even one who has been garlanded as a token of betrothal.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, cunda, tividhaṁ kāyena asoceyyaṁ hoti.
segs.e: This is the threefold impurity by way of body.

segs.p: Kathañca, cunda, catubbidhaṁ vācāya asoceyyaṁ hoti?
segs.e: And how is impurity fourfold by way of speech?

segs.p: Idha, cunda, ekacco musāvādī hoti. Sabhaggato vā parisaggato vā ñātimajjhagato vā pūgamajjhagato vā rājakulamajjhagato vā abhinīto sakkhipuṭṭho: ‘ehambho purisa, yaṁ jānāsi taṁ vadehī’ti, so ajānaṁ vā āha: ‘jānāmī’ti, jānaṁ vā āha: ‘na jānāmī’ti; apassaṁ vā āha: ‘passāmī’ti, passaṁ vā āha: ‘na passāmī’ti. Iti attahetu vā parahetu vā āmisakiñcikkhahetu vā sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: It’s when someone lies. They’re summoned to a council, an assembly, a family meeting, a guild, or to the royal court, and asked to bear witness: ‘Please, my friend, say what you know.’ Not knowing, they say ‘I know.’ Knowing, they say ‘I don’t know.’ Not seeing, they say ‘I see.’ And seeing, they say ‘I don’t see.’ So they deliberately lie for the sake of themselves or another, or for some trivial worldly reason.

segs.p: Pisuṇavāco hoti. Ito sutvā amutra akkhātā imesaṁ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā imesaṁ akkhātā amūsaṁ bhedāya. Iti samaggānaṁ vā bhettā, bhinnānaṁ vā anuppadātā, vaggārāmo vaggarato vagganandī vaggakaraṇiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They backbite. They repeat in one place what they heard in another so as to divide people against each other. And so they divide those who are harmonious, supporting division, delighting in division, loving division, speaking words that promote division.

segs.p: Pharusavāco hoti. Yā sā vācā aṇḍakā kakkasā parakaṭukā parābhisajjanī kodhasāmantā asamādhisaṁvattanikā, tathārūpiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They speak harshly. They use the kinds of words that are cruel, nasty, hurtful, offensive, bordering on anger, not leading to immersion.

segs.p: Samphappalāpī hoti akālavādī abhūtavādī anatthavādī adhammavādī avinayavādī; anidhānavatiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti akālena anapadesaṁ apariyantavatiṁ anatthasaṁhitaṁ.
segs.e: They talk nonsense. Their speech is untimely, and is neither factual nor beneficial. It has nothing to do with the teaching or the training. Their words have no value, and are untimely, unreasonable, rambling, and pointless.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, cunda, catubbidhaṁ vācāya asoceyyaṁ hoti.
segs.e: This is the fourfold impurity by way of speech.

segs.p: Kathañca, cunda, tividhaṁ manasā asoceyyaṁ hoti?
segs.e: And how is impurity threefold by way of mind?

segs.p: Idha, cunda, ekacco abhijjhālu hoti. Yaṁ taṁ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṁ taṁ abhijjhātā hoti: ‘aho vata yaṁ parassa taṁ mamassā’ti.
segs.e: It’s when someone is covetous. They covet the wealth and belongings of others: ‘Oh, if only their belongings were mine!’

segs.p: Byāpannacitto hoti paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo: ‘ime sattā haññantu vā bajjhantu vā ucchijjantu vā vinassantu vā mā vā ahesun’ti.
segs.e: They have ill will and malicious intentions: ‘May these sentient beings be killed, slaughtered, slain, destroyed, or annihilated!’
They have wrong view. Their perspective is distorted:

segs.p: ‘natthi dinnaṁ, natthi yiṭṭhaṁ, natthi hutaṁ, natthi sukaṭadukkaṭānaṁ kammānaṁ phalaṁ vipāko, natthi ayaṁ loko, natthi paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṁ parañca lokaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti.
segs.e: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, cunda, manasā tividhaṁ asoceyyaṁ hoti.
segs.e: This is the threefold impurity by way of mind.
These are the ten ways of doing unskillful deeds.

segs.p: Imehi kho, cunda, dasahi akusalehi kammapathehi samannāgato kālasseva uṭṭhahantova sayanamhā pathaviñcepi āmasati, asuciyeva hoti; no cepi pathaviṁ āmasati, asuciyeva hoti.
segs.e: When you have these ten ways of doing unskillful deeds, then if you rise early, whether or not you stroke the earth from your bed, you’re still impure.

segs.p: Allāni cepi gomayāni āmasati, asuciyeva hoti; no cepi allāni gomayāni āmasati, asuciyeva hoti.
segs.e: Whether or not you stroke fresh cow dung, you’re still impure.

segs.p: Haritāni cepi tiṇāni āmasati, asuciyeva hoti; no cepi haritāni tiṇāni āmasati, asuciyeva hoti.
segs.e: Whether or not you stroke green grass, you’re still impure.

segs.p: Aggiñcepi paricarati, asuciyeva hoti, no cepi aggiṁ paricarati, asuciyeva hoti.
segs.e: Whether or not you serve the sacred flame, you’re still impure.

segs.p: Pañjaliko cepi ādiccaṁ namassati, asuciyeva hoti; no cepi pañjaliko ādiccaṁ namassati, asuciyeva hoti.
segs.e: Whether or not you revere the sun with cupped palms, you’re still impure.

segs.p: Sāyatatiyakañcepi udakaṁ orohati, asuciyeva hoti; no cepi sāyatatiyakaṁ udakaṁ orohati, asuciyeva hoti.
segs.e: Whether or not you immerse yourself in water three times, you’re still impure.
Why is that?

segs.p: Ime, cunda, dasa akusalakammapathā asucīyeva honti asucikaraṇā ca.
segs.e: These ten ways of doing unskillful deeds are impure and make things impure.

segs.p: Imesaṁ pana, cunda, dasannaṁ akusalānaṁ kammapathānaṁ samannāgamanahetu nirayo paññāyati, tiracchānayoni paññāyati, pettivisayo paññāyati, yā vā panaññāpi kāci duggatiyo.
segs.e: It’s because of those who do these ten kinds of unskillful deeds that hell, the animal realm, the ghost realm, or any other bad places are found.

segs.p: Tividhaṁ kho, cunda, kāyena soceyyaṁ hoti;
segs.e: Cunda, purity is threefold by way of body,
fourfold by way of speech,
and threefold by way of mind.

segs.p: Kathaṁ, cunda, tividhaṁ kāyena soceyyaṁ hoti?
segs.e: And how is purity threefold by way of body?

segs.p: Idha, cunda, ekacco pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho, lajjī dayāpanno, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati.
segs.e: It’s when someone gives up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. They’re scrupulous and kind, living full of sympathy for all living beings.

segs.p: Adinnādānaṁ pahāya, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti. Yaṁ taṁ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṁ gāmagataṁ vā araññagataṁ vā, na taṁ adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādātā hoti.
segs.e: They give up stealing. They don’t, with the intention to commit theft, take the wealth or belongings of others from village or wilderness.

segs.p: Kāmesumicchācāraṁ pahāya, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti yā tā māturakkhitā piturakkhitā mātāpiturakkhitā bhāturakkhitā bhaginirakkhitā ñātirakkhitā gottarakkhitā dhammarakkhitā sasāmikā saparidaṇḍā antamaso mālāguḷaparikkhittāpi, tathārūpāsu na cārittaṁ āpajjitā hoti.
segs.e: They give up sexual misconduct. They don’t have relations with women who have their mother, father, both mother and father, brother, sister, relatives, or clan as guardian. They don’t have relations with a woman who is protected on principle, or who has a husband, or whose violation is punishable by law, or even one who has been garlanded as a token of betrothal.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, cunda, tividhaṁ kāyena soceyyaṁ hoti.
segs.e: This is the threefold purity by way of body.

segs.p: Kathañca, cunda, catubbidhaṁ vācāya soceyyaṁ hoti?
segs.e: And how is purity fourfold by way of speech?

segs.p: Idha, cunda, ekacco musāvādaṁ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti. Sabhaggato vā parisaggato vā ñātimajjhagato vā pūgamajjhagato vā rājakulamajjhagato vā abhinīto sakkhipuṭṭho: ‘ehambho purisa, yaṁ jānāsi taṁ vadehī’ti, so ajānaṁ vā āha: ‘na jānāmī’ti, jānaṁ vā āha: ‘jānāmī’ti, apassaṁ vā āha: ‘na passāmī’ti, passaṁ vā āha: ‘passāmī’ti. Iti attahetu vā parahetu vā āmisakiñcikkhahetu vā na sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: It’s when someone gives up lying. They’re summoned to a council, an assembly, a family meeting, a guild, or to the royal court, and asked to bear witness: ‘Please, my friend, say what you know.’ Not knowing, they say ‘I don’t know.’ Knowing, they say ‘I know.’ Not seeing, they say ‘I don’t see.’ And seeing, they say ‘I see.’ So they don’t deliberately lie for the sake of themselves or another, or for some trivial worldly reason.

segs.p: Pisuṇaṁ vācaṁ pahāya, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti—na ito sutvā amutra akkhātā imesaṁ bhedāya, na amutra vā sutvā imesaṁ akkhātā amūsaṁ bhedāya. Iti bhinnānaṁ vā sandhātā sahitānaṁ vā anuppadātā samaggārāmo samaggarato samagganandī samaggakaraṇiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They give up backbiting. They don’t repeat in one place what they heard in another so as to divide people against each other. Instead, they reconcile those who are divided and support those who are united, delighting in harmony, loving harmony, speaking words that promote harmony.

segs.p: Pharusaṁ vācaṁ pahāya, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti. Yā sā vācā nelā kaṇṇasukhā pemanīyā hadayaṅgamā porī bahujanakantā bahujanamanāpā, tathārūpiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They give up harsh speech. They speak in a way that’s mellow, pleasing to the ear, endearing, going to the heart, polite, and likable and agreeable to the people.

segs.p: Samphappalāpaṁ pahāya, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti kālavādī bhūtavādī atthavādī dhammavādī vinayavādī;
segs.e: They give up talking nonsense. Their words are timely, true, and meaningful, in line with the teaching and training.

segs.p: nidhānavatiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti kālena sāpadesaṁ pariyantavatiṁ atthasaṁhitaṁ.
segs.e: They say things at the right time which are valuable, reasonable, succinct, and beneficial.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, cunda, catubbidhaṁ vācāya soceyyaṁ hoti.
segs.e: This is the fourfold purity by way of speech.

segs.p: Kathañca, cunda, tividhaṁ manasā soceyyaṁ hoti?
segs.e: And how is purity threefold by way of mind?

segs.p: Idha, cunda, ekacco anabhijjhālu hoti. Yaṁ taṁ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṁ taṁ anabhijjhitā hoti: ‘aho vata yaṁ parassa taṁ mamassā’ti.
segs.e: It’s when someone is content. They don’t covet the wealth and belongings of others: ‘Oh, if only their belongings were mine!’

segs.p: Abyāpannacitto hoti appaduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo: ‘ime sattā averā hontu abyāpajjā, anīghā sukhī attānaṁ pariharantū’ti.
segs.e: They have a kind heart and loving intentions: ‘May these sentient beings live free of enmity and ill will, untroubled and happy!’
They have right view, an undistorted perspective:

segs.p: ‘atthi dinnaṁ, atthi yiṭṭhaṁ, atthi hutaṁ, atthi sukaṭadukkaṭānaṁ kammānaṁ phalaṁ vipāko, atthi ayaṁ loko, atthi paro loko, atthi mātā, atthi pitā, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṁ parañca lokaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti.
segs.e: ‘There is meaning in giving, sacrifice, and offerings. There are fruits and results of good and bad deeds. There is an afterlife. There are such things as mother and father, and beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there are ascetics and brahmins who are rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describe the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, cunda, tividhaṁ manasā soceyyaṁ hoti.
segs.e: This is the threefold purity by way of mind.
These are the ten ways of doing skillful deeds.

segs.p: Imehi kho, cunda, dasahi kusalehi kammapathehi samannāgato kālasseva uṭṭhahantova sayanamhā pathaviñcepi āmasati, suciyeva hoti; no cepi pathaviṁ āmasati, suciyeva hoti.
segs.e: When you have these ten ways of doing skillful deeds, then if you rise early, whether or not you stroke the earth from your bed, you’re still pure.

segs.p: Allāni cepi gomayāni āmasati, suciyeva hoti; no cepi allāni gomayāni āmasati, suciyeva hoti.
segs.e: Whether or not you stroke fresh cow dung, you’re still pure.

segs.p: Haritāni cepi tiṇāni āmasati, suciyeva hoti; no cepi haritāni tiṇāni āmasati, suciyeva hoti.
segs.e: Whether or not you stroke green grass, you’re still pure.

segs.p: Aggiñcepi paricarati, suciyeva hoti; no cepi aggiṁ paricarati, suciyeva hoti.
segs.e: Whether or not you serve the sacred flame, you’re still pure.

segs.p: Pañjaliko cepi ādiccaṁ namassati, suciyeva hoti; no cepi pañjaliko ādiccaṁ namassati, suciyeva hoti.
segs.e: Whether or not you revere the sun with cupped palms, you’re still pure.

segs.p: Sāyatatiyakañcepi udakaṁ orohati, suciyeva hoti; no cepi sāyatatiyakaṁ udakaṁ orohati, suciyeva hoti.
segs.e: Whether or not you immerse yourself in water three times, you’re still pure.
Why is that?

segs.p: Ime, cunda, dasa kusalakammapathā sucīyeva honti sucikaraṇā ca.
segs.e: These ten ways of doing skillful deeds are pure and make things pure.

segs.p: Imesaṁ pana, cunda, dasannaṁ kusalānaṁ kammapathānaṁ samannāgamanahetu devā paññāyanti, manussā paññāyanti, yā vā panaññāpi kāci sugatiyo”ti.
segs.e: It’s because of those who do these ten kinds of skillful deeds that gods, humans, or any other good places are found.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, cundo kammāraputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Cunda the smith said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, sir! Excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ, bhante, bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

17. With Jānussoṇi
With Jānussoṇi

segs.p: Atha kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin Jānussoṇi went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha,
“We who are known as brahmins
give gifts and perform memorial rites for the dead:

segs.p: ‘idaṁ dānaṁ petānaṁ ñātisālohitānaṁ upakappatu, idaṁ dānaṁ petā ñātisālohitā paribhuñjantū’ti.
segs.e: ‘May this gift aid my departed relatives and kin. May they partake of this gift.’

segs.p: Kacci taṁ, bho gotama, dānaṁ petānaṁ ñātisālohitānaṁ upakappati;
segs.e: But does this gift really aid departed relatives and kin?

segs.p: kacci te petā ñātisālohitā taṁ dānaṁ paribhuñjantī”ti?
segs.e: Do they actually partake of it?”
“It aids them if the conditions are right, brahmin, but not if the conditions are wrong.”

segs.p: “Katamaṁ pana, bho gotama, ṭhānaṁ, katamaṁ aṭṭhānan”ti?
segs.e: “Then, worthy Gotama, what are the right and wrong conditions?”

segs.p: “Idha, brāhmaṇa, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, pisuṇavāco hoti, pharusavāco hoti, samphappalāpī hoti, abhijjhālu hoti, byāpannacitto hoti, micchādiṭṭhiko hoti.
segs.e: “Brahmin, take someone who kills living creatures, steals, and commits sexual misconduct. They use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re covetous, malicious, with wrong view.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in hell.

segs.p: Yo nerayikānaṁ sattānaṁ āhāro, tena so tattha yāpeti, tena so tattha tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: There they survive feeding on the food of the hell beings.

segs.p: Idampi kho, brāhmaṇa, aṭṭhānaṁ yattha ṭhitassa taṁ dānaṁ na upakappati.
segs.e: The conditions there are wrong, so the gift does not aid the one who lives there.

segs.p: Idha pana, brāhmaṇa, ekacco pāṇātipātī …pe… micchādiṭṭhiko hoti.
segs.e: Take someone else who kills living creatures … and has wrong view.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā tiracchānayoniṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the animal realm.

segs.p: Yo tiracchānayonikānaṁ sattānaṁ āhāro, tena so tattha yāpeti, tena so tattha tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: There they survive feeding on the food of the beings in the animal realm.

segs.p: Idampi kho, brāhmaṇa, aṭṭhānaṁ yattha ṭhitassa taṁ dānaṁ na upakappati.
segs.e: The conditions there too are wrong, so the gift does not aid the one who lives there.

segs.p: Idha pana, brāhmaṇa, ekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, anabhijjhālu hoti, abyāpannacitto hoti, sammādiṭṭhiko hoti.
segs.e: Take someone else who doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, or commit sexual misconduct. They don’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re contented, kind-hearted, with right view.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā manussānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the human realm.

segs.p: Yo manussānaṁ āhāro, tena so tattha yāpeti, tena so tattha tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: There they survive feeding on human food.

segs.p: Idampi kho, brāhmaṇa, aṭṭhānaṁ yattha ṭhitassa taṁ dānaṁ na upakappati.
segs.e: The conditions there too are wrong, so the gift does not aid the one who lives there.

segs.p: Idha pana, brāhmaṇa, ekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti …pe… sammādiṭṭhiko hoti.
segs.e: Take someone else who doesn’t kill living creatures … and has right view.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods.

segs.p: Yo devānaṁ āhāro, tena so tattha yāpeti, tena so tattha tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: There they survive feeding on the food of the gods.

segs.p: Idampi, brāhmaṇa, aṭṭhānaṁ yattha ṭhitassa taṁ dānaṁ upakappati.
segs.e: The conditions there too are wrong, so the gift does not aid the one who lives there.

segs.p: Idha pana, brāhmaṇa, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti …pe… micchādiṭṭhiko hoti.
segs.e: Take someone else who kills living creatures … and has wrong view.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā pettivisayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the ghost realm.

segs.p: Yo pettivesayikānaṁ sattānaṁ āhāro, tena so tattha yāpeti, tena so tattha tiṭṭhati, yaṁ vā panassa ito anuppavecchanti mittāmaccā vā ñātisālohitā vā, tena so tattha yāpeti, tena so tattha tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: There they survive feeding on the food of the beings in the ghost realm. Or else they survive feeding on what friends and colleagues, relatives and kin provide them with from here.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, ṭhānaṁ yattha ṭhitassa taṁ dānaṁ upakappatī”ti.
segs.e: The conditions there are right, so the gift aids the one who lives there.”

segs.p: “Sace pana, bho gotama, so peto ñātisālohito taṁ ṭhānaṁ anupapanno hoti, ko taṁ dānaṁ paribhuñjatī”ti?
segs.e: “But worthy Gotama, who partakes of that gift if the departed relative is not reborn in that place?”

segs.p: “Aññepissa, brāhmaṇa, petā ñātisālohitā taṁ ṭhānaṁ upapannā honti, te taṁ dānaṁ paribhuñjantī”ti.
segs.e: “Other departed relatives reborn there will partake of that gift.”

segs.p: “Sace pana, bho gotama, so ceva peto ñātisālohito taṁ ṭhānaṁ anupapanno hoti aññepissa ñātisālohitā petā taṁ ṭhānaṁ anupapannā honti, ko taṁ dānaṁ paribhuñjatī”ti?
segs.e: “But who partakes of the gift when neither that relative nor other relatives have been reborn in that place?”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānaṁ kho etaṁ, brāhmaṇa, anavakāso yaṁ taṁ ṭhānaṁ vivittaṁ assa iminā dīghena addhunā yadidaṁ petehi ñātisālohitehi.
segs.e: “It’s impossible, brahmin, it cannot happen that that place is vacant of departed relatives in all this long time.
It’s never fruitless for the donor.”
“Does the worthy Gotama propose this even when the conditions are wrong?”
“I propose this even when the conditions are wrong.

segs.p: Idha, brāhmaṇa, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, pisuṇavāco hoti, pharusavāco hoti, samphappalāpī hoti, abhijjhālu hoti, byāpannacitto hoti, micchādiṭṭhiko hoti;
segs.e: Take someone who kills living creatures, steals, and commits sexual misconduct. They use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re covetous, malicious, with wrong view.

segs.p: so dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṁ pānaṁ vatthaṁ yānaṁ mālāgandhavilepanaṁ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ.
segs.e: They give to ascetics or brahmins such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā hatthīnaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of elephants.

segs.p: So tattha lābhī hoti annassa pānassa mālānānālaṅkārassa.
segs.e: There they get to have food and drink, garlands and various adornments.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, idha pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavāco pharusavāco samphappalāpī abhijjhālu byāpannacitto micchādiṭṭhiko, tena so kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā hatthīnaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: Since in this life they killed living creatures … and had wrong view, they were reborn in the company of elephants.

segs.p: Yañca kho so dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṁ pānaṁ vatthaṁ yānaṁ mālāgandhavilepanaṁ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ, tena so tattha lābhī hoti annassa pānassa mālānānālaṅkārassa.
segs.e: Since they gave to ascetics or brahmins … they get to have food and drink, garlands and various adornments.

segs.e: Take someone else who kills living creatures … and has wrong view.

segs.e: They give to ascetics or brahmins …

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā assānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati …pe…
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of horses. …

segs.p: So tattha lābhī hoti mānusakānaṁ pañcannaṁ kāmaguṇānaṁ.
segs.e: There they get to have the five kinds of human sensual stimulation.

segs.e: Since they gave to ascetics or brahmins … they get to have the five kinds of heavenly sensual stimulation.
It’s never fruitless for the donor.”
“It’s incredible, worthy Gotama, it’s amazing,

segs.p: Yāvañcidaṁ, bho gotama, alameva dānāni dātuṁ, alaṁ saddhāni kātuṁ, yatra hi nāma dāyakopi anipphalo”ti.
segs.e: This is quite enough to justify giving gifts and performing memorial rites for the dead, since it’s never fruitless for the donor.”
“That’s so true, brahmin. It’s never fruitless for the donor.”
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

18. Good
Good
“Mendicants, I will teach you what is good and what is not good.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“And what, mendicants, is not good?

segs.p: Pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṁ, kāmesumicchācāro, musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo, abhijjhā, byāpādo, micchādiṭṭhi—
segs.e: Killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical; covetousness, ill will, and wrong view.
This is called what is not good.
And what is good?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī, musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī, anabhijjhā, abyāpādo, sammādiṭṭhi—
segs.e: Refraining from killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; refraining from speech that’s false, divisive, harsh, or nonsensical; contentment, good will, and right view.
This is called what is good.”

wrong view.

19. The Noble Path
Principles That Should Be Activated

segs.p: “Uppādetabbañca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṁ desessāmi na uppādetabbañca.
segs.e: “I will teach you the principle to activate and the principle not to activate. …

segs.p: katamo ca, bhikkhave, na uppādetabbo dhammo?
segs.e: And what is the principle not to activate?
Killing living creatures …
wrong view.

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, na uppādetabbo dhammo.

20. Another Chapter on Individuals

segs.p: “Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato puggalo na sevitabbo.

segs.p: Pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, pisuṇavāco hoti, pharusavāco hoti, samphappalāpī hoti, abhijjhālu hoti, byāpannacitto hoti, micchādiṭṭhiko hoti—

segs.e: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, or commit sexual misconduct. They don’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. They’re contented, kind-hearted, with right view.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato puggalo sevitabbo.
segs.e: You should associate with an individual who possesses these ten qualities.”

Numbered Discourses 10.211
21. The Body Born of Deeds
Heaven and Hell (1st)

segs.p: “Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Someone with ten qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What ten?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti, luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtesu.
segs.e: It’s when someone kills living creatures. They’re violent, bloody-handed, a hardened killer, merciless to all living beings.

segs.p: Adinnādāyī hoti, yaṁ taṁ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṁ gāmagataṁ vā araññagataṁ vā, taṁ adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādātā hoti.
segs.e: They steal. With the intention to commit theft, they take the wealth or belongings of others from village or wilderness.

segs.p: Kāmesu micchācārī hoti, yā tā māturakkhitā piturakkhitā mātāpiturakkhitā bhāturakkhitā bhaginirakkhitā ñātirakkhitā gottarakkhitā dhammarakkhitā sasāmikā saparidaṇḍā antamaso mālāguḷaparikkhittāpi, tathārūpāsu cārittaṁ āpajjitā hoti.
segs.e: They commit sexual misconduct. They have relations with women who have their mother, father, both mother and father, brother, sister, relatives, or clan as guardian. They have relations with a woman who is protected on principle, or who has a husband, or whose violation is punishable by law, or even one who has been garlanded as a token of betrothal.

segs.p: Musāvādī hoti, sabhaggato vā parisaggato vā ñātimajjhagato vā pūgamajjhagato vā rājakulamajjhagato vā abhinīto sakkhipuṭṭho: ‘ehambho purisa, yaṁ jānāsi taṁ vadehī’ti, so ajānaṁ vā āha: ‘jānāmī’ti, jānaṁ vā āha: ‘na jānāmī’ti, apassaṁ vā āha: ‘passāmī’ti, passaṁ vā āha: ‘na passāmī’ti. Iti attahetu vā parahetu vā āmisakiñcikkhahetu vā sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They lie. They’re summoned to a council, an assembly, a family meeting, a guild, or to the royal court, and asked to bear witness: ‘Please, my man, say what you know.’ Not knowing, they say ‘I know.’ Knowing, they say ‘I don’t know.’ Not seeing, they say ‘I see.’ And seeing, they say ‘I don’t see.’ So they deliberately lie for the sake of themselves or another, or for some trivial worldly reason.

segs.p: Pisuṇavāco hoti, ito sutvā amutra akkhātā imesaṁ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā imesaṁ akkhātā amūsaṁ bhedāya. Iti samaggānaṁ vā bhettā bhinnānaṁ vā anuppadātā vaggārāmo vaggarato vagganandī, vaggakaraṇiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They backbite. They repeat in one place what they heard in another so as to divide people against each other. And so they divide those who are harmonious, supporting division, delighting in division, loving division, speaking words that promote division.

segs.p: Pharusavāco hoti, yā sā vācā aṇḍakā kakkasā parakaṭukā parābhisajjanī kodhasāmantā asamādhisaṁvattanikā, tathārūpiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They speak harshly. They use the kinds of words that are cruel, nasty, hurtful, offensive, bordering on anger, not leading to immersion.

segs.p: Samphappalāpī hoti, akālavādī abhūtavādī anatthavādī adhammavādī avinayavādī, anidhānavatiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti akālena anapadesaṁ apariyantavatiṁ anatthasaṁhitaṁ.
segs.e: They talk nonsense. Their speech is untimely, and is neither factual nor beneficial. It has nothing to do with the teaching or the training. Their words have no value, and are untimely, unreasonable, rambling, and pointless.

segs.p: Abhijjhālu hoti, yaṁ taṁ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṁ taṁ abhijjhātā hoti: ‘aho vata yaṁ parassa taṁ mama assā’ti.
segs.e: They’re covetous. They covet the wealth and belongings of others: ‘Oh, if only their belongings were mine!’

segs.p: Byāpannacitto hoti, paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo: ‘ime sattā haññantu vā bajjhantu vā ucchijjantu vā vinassantu vā mā vā ahesun’ti.
segs.e: They have ill will and malicious intentions: ‘May these sentient beings be killed, slaughtered, slain, destroyed, or annihilated!’
They have wrong view. Their perspective is distorted:

segs.p: ‘natthi dinnaṁ, natthi yiṭṭhaṁ, natthi hutaṁ, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṁ kammānaṁ phalaṁ vipāko, natthi ayaṁ loko, natthi paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṁ parañca lokaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti.
segs.e: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: Someone with these ten qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: Someone with ten qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What ten?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho lajjī dayāpanno, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati.
segs.e: It’s when someone gives up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. They’re scrupulous and kind, living full of sympathy for all living beings.

segs.p: Adinnādānaṁ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti. Yaṁ taṁ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṁ gāmagataṁ vā araññagataṁ vā, na taṁ adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādātā hoti.
segs.e: They give up stealing. They don’t, with the intention to commit theft, take the wealth or belongings of others from village or wilderness.

segs.p: Kāmesumicchācāraṁ pahāya kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti. Yā tā māturakkhitā …pe… antamaso mālāguḷaparikkhittāpi, tathārūpāsu na cārittaṁ āpajjitā hoti.
segs.e: They give up sexual misconduct. They don’t have relations with women who have their mother, father, both mother and father, brother, sister, relatives, or clan as guardian. They don’t have relations with a woman who is protected on principle, or who has a husband, or whose violation is punishable by law, or even one who has been garlanded as a token of betrothal.

segs.p: Musāvādaṁ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti. Sabhaggato vā parisaggato vā ñātimajjhagato vā pūgamajjhagato vā rājakulamajjhagato vā abhinīto sakkhipuṭṭho: ‘ehambho purisa, yaṁ jānāsi taṁ vadehī’ti, so ajānaṁ vā āha: ‘na jānāmī’ti, jānaṁ vā āha: ‘jānāmī’ti, apassaṁ vā āha: ‘na passāmī’ti, passaṁ vā āha: ‘passāmī’ti. Iti attahetu vā parahetu vā āmisakiñcikkhahetu vā na sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They give up lying. They’re summoned to a council, an assembly, a family meeting, a guild, or to the royal court, and asked to bear witness: ‘Please, my man, say what you know.’ Not knowing, they say ‘I don’t know.’ Knowing, they say ‘I know.’ Not seeing, they say ‘I don’t see.’ And seeing, they say ‘I see.’ So they don’t deliberately lie for the sake of themselves or another, or for some trivial worldly reason.

segs.p: Pisuṇavācaṁ pahāya pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti—na ito sutvā amutra akkhātā imesaṁ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā imesaṁ akkhātā amūsaṁ bhedāya. Iti bhinnānaṁ vā sandhātā sahitānaṁ vā anuppadātā samaggārāmo samaggarato samagganandī, samaggakaraṇiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They give up backbiting. They don’t repeat in one place what they heard in another so as to divide people against each other. Instead, they reconcile those who are divided and support those who are united, delighting in harmony, loving harmony, speaking words that promote harmony.

segs.p: Pharusavācaṁ pahāya pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti. Yā sā vācā nelā kaṇṇasukhā pemanīyā hadayaṅgamā porī bahujanakantā bahujanamanāpā, tathārūpiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They give up harsh speech. They speak in a way that’s mellow, pleasing to the ear, endearing, going to the heart, polite, and likable and agreeable to the people.

segs.p: Samphappalāpaṁ pahāya samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti kālavādī bhūtavādī, atthavādī dhammavādī vinayavādī, nidhānavatiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti kālena sāpadesaṁ pariyantavatiṁ atthasaṁhitaṁ.
segs.e: They give up talking nonsense. Their words are timely, true, and meaningful, in line with the teaching and training. They say things at the right time which are valuable, reasonable, succinct, and beneficial.

segs.p: Anabhijjhālu hoti. Yaṁ taṁ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṁ taṁ anabhijjhātā hoti: ‘aho vata yaṁ parassa taṁ mama assā’ti.
segs.e: They’re content. They don’t covet the wealth and belongings of others: ‘Oh, if only their belongings were mine!’

segs.p: Abyāpannacitto hoti appaduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo: ‘ime sattā averā hontu abyāpajjā anīghā, sukhī attānaṁ pariharantū’ti.
segs.e: They have a kind heart and loving intentions: ‘May these sentient beings live free of enmity and ill will, untroubled and happy!’
They have right view, an undistorted perspective:

segs.p: ‘atthi dinnaṁ, atthi yiṭṭhaṁ, atthi hutaṁ, atthi sukaṭadukkaṭānaṁ kammānaṁ phalaṁ vipāko, atthi ayaṁ loko, atthi paro loko, atthi mātā, atthi pitā, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṁ parañca lokaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti.
segs.e: ‘There is meaning in giving, sacrifice, and offerings. There are fruits and results of good and bad deeds. There is an afterlife. There are such things as mother and father, and beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there are ascetics and brahmins who are rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describe the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these ten qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
