21. The Body Born of Deeds
Creepy Creatures
“Mendicants, I will teach you an exposition of the teaching on creepy creatures.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“What is the exposition of the teaching on creepy creatures?

segs.p: Kammassakā, bhikkhave, sattā kammadāyādā kammayonī kammabandhū kammapaṭisaraṇā, yaṁ kammaṁ karonti—
segs.e: Sentient beings are the owners of their deeds and heir to their deeds. Deeds are their womb, their relative, and their refuge.

segs.p: kalyāṇaṁ vā pāpakaṁ vā—tassa dāyādā bhavanti.
segs.e: They shall be the heir of whatever deeds they do, whether good or bad.

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho, adayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtesu.
segs.e: Take a certain someone who kills living creatures. They’re violent, bloody-handed, a hardened killer, merciless to all living beings.

segs.p: So saṁsappati kāyena, saṁsappati vācāya, saṁsappati manasā.
segs.e: They’re creepy in body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Tassa jimhaṁ kāyakammaṁ hoti, jimhaṁ vacīkammaṁ, jimhaṁ manokammaṁ, jimhā gati, jimhupapatti.
segs.e: Doing crooked deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, their destiny and rebirth are crooked.

segs.p: Jimhagatikassa kho panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, jimhupapattikassa dvinnaṁ gatīnaṁ aññataraṁ gatiṁ vadāmi—
segs.e: Someone whose destiny and rebirth is crooked is reborn in one of two places, I say:

segs.p: ye vā ekantadukkhā nirayā yā vā saṁsappajātikā tiracchānayoni.
segs.e: in an absolutely painful hell, or among the species of creepy animals.

segs.p: Katamā ca sā, bhikkhave, saṁsappajātikā tiracchānayoni?
segs.e: And what are the species of creepy animals?

segs.p: Ahi vicchikā satapadī nakulā biḷārā mūsikā ulūkā, ye vā panaññepi keci tiracchānayonikā sattā manusse disvā saṁsappanti.
segs.e: Snakes, scorpions, centipedes, mongooses, cats, mice, owls, or whatever other species of animal that creep away when they see humans.

segs.p: Iti kho, bhikkhave, bhūtā bhūtassa upapatti hoti.
segs.e: This is how a being is born from a being.
For your deeds determine your rebirth,
and when you’re reborn contacts strike you.
This is why I say that sentient beings are heirs to their deeds.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco adinnādāyī hoti …pe…
segs.e: Take someone else who steals …
commits sexual misconduct …
lies …
backbites …
speaks harshly …
indulges in talking nonsense …
is covetous …
has cruel intentions …
has wrong view …

segs.p: So saṁsappati kāyena, saṁsappati vācāya, saṁsappati manasā.
segs.e: They’re creepy in body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Tassa jimhaṁ kāyakammaṁ hoti, jimhaṁ vacīkammaṁ, jimhaṁ manokammaṁ, jimhā gati, jimhupapatti.
segs.e: Doing crooked deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, their destiny and rebirth are crooked.

segs.p: Jimhagatikassa kho panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, jimhupapattikassa dvinnaṁ gatīnaṁ aññataraṁ gatiṁ vadāmi—
segs.e: Someone whose destiny and rebirth is crooked is reborn in one of two places, I say:

segs.p: ye vā ekantadukkhā nirayā yā vā saṁsappajātikā tiracchānayoni.
segs.e: in an absolutely painful hell, or among the species of creepy animals.

segs.p: Katamā ca sā, bhikkhave, saṁsappajātikā tiracchānayoni?
segs.e: And what are the species of creepy animals?

segs.p: Ahi vicchikā satapadī nakulā biḷārā mūsikā ulūkā, ye vā panaññepi keci tiracchānayonikā sattā manusse disvā saṁsappanti.
segs.e: Snakes, scorpions, centipedes, mongooses, cats, mice, owls, or whatever other species of animal that creep away when they see humans.

segs.p: Iti kho, bhikkhave, bhūtā bhūtassa upapatti hoti,
segs.e: This is how a being is born from a being.
For your deeds determine your rebirth,
and when you’re reborn contacts strike you.
This is why I say that sentient beings are heirs to their deeds.

segs.p: Kammassakā, bhikkhave, sattā kammadāyādā kammayonī kammabandhū kammapaṭisaraṇā, yaṁ kammaṁ karonti—
segs.e: Sentient beings are the owners of their deeds and heir to their deeds. Deeds are their womb, their relative, and their refuge.

segs.p: kalyāṇaṁ vā pāpakaṁ vā—tassa dāyādā bhavanti.
segs.e: They shall be the heir of whatever deeds they do, whether good or bad.

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho, lajjī dayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati.
segs.e: Take a certain someone who gives up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. They’re scrupulous and kind, living full of sympathy for all living beings.

segs.p: So na saṁsappati kāyena, na saṁsappati vācāya, na saṁsappati manasā.
segs.e: They’re not creepy in body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Tassa uju kāyakammaṁ hoti, uju vacīkammaṁ, uju manokammaṁ, uju gati, ujupapatti.
segs.e: Doing virtuous deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, their destiny and rebirth is virtuous.

segs.p: Ujugatikassa kho panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, ujupapattikassa dvinnaṁ gatīnaṁ aññataraṁ gatiṁ vadāmi—
segs.e: Someone whose destiny and rebirth is virtuous is reborn in one of two places, I say:

segs.p: ye vā ekantasukhā saggā yāni vā pana tāni uccākulāni khattiyamahāsālakulāni vā brāhmaṇamahāsālakulāni vā gahapatimahāsālakulāni vā aḍḍhāni mahaddhanāni mahābhogāni pahūtajātarūparajatāni pahūtavittūpakaraṇāni pahūtadhanadhaññāni.
segs.e: in a heaven of absolute happiness, or in an eminent well-to-do family of aristocrats, brahmins, or householders—rich, affluent, and wealthy, with lots of gold and silver, lots of property and assets, and lots of money and grain.

segs.p: Iti kho, bhikkhave, bhūtā bhūtassa upapatti hoti.
segs.e: This is how a being is born from a being.
For your deeds determine your rebirth,
and when you’re reborn contacts strike you.
This is why I say that sentient beings are heirs to their deeds.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco adinnādānaṁ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti …pe…
segs.e: Take someone else who gives up stealing …
sexual misconduct …
lying …

segs.p: pisuṇaṁ vācaṁ pahāya pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti …
segs.e: backbiting …

segs.p: pharusaṁ vācaṁ pahāya pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti …
segs.e: harsh speech …
talking nonsense …
They’re content …
kind hearted …
they have right view …

segs.p: ye imañca lokaṁ parañca lokaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti.
So na saṁsappati kāyena, na saṁsappati vācāya, na saṁsappati manasā.
segs.e: They’re not creepy in body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Tassa uju kāyakammaṁ hoti, uju vacīkammaṁ, uju manokammaṁ, uju gati, ujupapatti.
segs.e: Doing virtuous deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, their destiny and rebirth is virtuous.

segs.p: Ujugatikassa kho pana ahaṁ, bhikkhave, ujupapattikassa dvinnaṁ gatīnaṁ aññataraṁ gatiṁ vadāmi—
segs.e: Someone whose destiny and rebirth is virtuous is reborn in one of two places, I say:

segs.p: ye vā ekantasukhā saggā yāni vā pana tāni uccākulāni khattiyamahāsālakulāni vā brāhmaṇamahāsālakulāni vā gahapatimahāsālakulāni vā aḍḍhāni mahaddhanāni mahābhogāni pahūtajātarūparajatāni pahūtavittūpakaraṇāni pahūtadhanadhaññāni.
segs.e: in a heaven of absolute happiness, or in an eminent well-to-do family of aristocrats, brahmins, or householders—rich, affluent, and wealthy, with lots of gold and silver, lots of property and assets, and lots of money and grain.

segs.p: Iti kho, bhikkhave, bhūtā bhūtassa upapatti hoti.
segs.e: This is how a being is born from a being.
For your deeds determine your rebirth,
and when you’re reborn contacts strike you.
This is why I say that sentient beings are heirs to their deeds.

segs.p: Kammassakā, bhikkhave, sattā kammadāyādā kammayonī kammabandhū kammapaṭisaraṇā, yaṁ kammaṁ karonti—
segs.e: Sentient beings are the owners of their deeds and heir to their deeds. Deeds are their womb, their relative, and their refuge.

segs.p: kalyāṇaṁ vā pāpakaṁ vā—tassa dāyādā bhavanti.
segs.e: They shall be the heir of whatever deeds they do, whether good or bad.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho so, bhikkhave, saṁsappanīyapariyāyo dhammapariyāyo”ti.
segs.e: This is the exposition of the teaching on creepy creatures.”
Numbered Discourses 10.217
21. The Body Born of Deeds
Intentional (1st)

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṁ kammānaṁ katānaṁ upacitānaṁ appaṭisaṁveditvā byantībhāvaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I don’t say that intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated are eliminated without being experienced.

segs.p: Tañca kho diṭṭheva dhamme upapajje vā apare vā pariyāye.
segs.e: And that may be in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

segs.p: Na tvevāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṁ kammānaṁ katānaṁ upacitānaṁ appaṭisaṁveditvā dukkhassantakiriyaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: But in any case, there is no making an end of suffering without experiencing intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated, I say.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti;
segs.e: Now, there are three kinds of corruption and failure of bodily action that have unskillful intention, with suffering as their outcome and result.

segs.p: catubbidhā vacīkammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti;
segs.e: There are four kinds of corruption and failure of verbal action that have unskillful intention, with suffering as their outcome and result.

segs.p: tividhā manokammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti.
segs.e: There are three kinds of corruption and failure of mental action that have unskillful intention, with suffering as their outcome and result.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti?
segs.e: And what are the three kinds of corruption and failure of bodily action?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti, luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtesu.
segs.e: It’s when someone kills living creatures. They’re violent, bloody-handed, a hardened killer, merciless to all living beings.

segs.p: Adinnādāyī hoti, yaṁ taṁ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṁ gāmagataṁ vā araññagataṁ vā, taṁ adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādātā hoti.
segs.e: They steal. With the intention to commit theft, they take the wealth or belongings of others from village or wilderness.

segs.p: Kāmesumicchācārī hoti, yā tā māturakkhitā …pe… antamaso mālāguḷaparikkhittāpi, tathārūpāsu cārittaṁ āpajjitā hoti.
segs.e: They commit sexual misconduct. They have relations with women who have their mother, father, both mother and father, brother, sister, relatives, or clan as guardian. They have relations with a woman who is protected on principle, or who has a husband, or whose violation is punishable by law, or even one who has been garlanded as a token of betrothal.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti.
segs.e: These are the three kinds of corruption and failure of bodily action.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, catubbidhā vacīkammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti?
segs.e: And what are the four kinds of corruption and failure of verbal action?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco musāvādī hoti. Sabhaggato vā parisaggato vā ñātimajjhagato vā pūgamajjhagato vā rājakulamajjhagato vā abhinīto sakkhipuṭṭho
segs.e: It’s when someone lies. They’re summoned to a council, an assembly, a family meeting, a guild, or to the royal court, and asked to bear witness:

segs.p: ‘ehambho purisa, yaṁ jānāsi taṁ vadehī’ti, so ajānaṁ vā āha: ‘jānāmī’ti, jānaṁ vā āha: ‘na jānāmī’ti, apassaṁ vā āha: ‘passāmī’ti, passaṁ vā āha: ‘na passāmī’ti, iti attahetu vā parahetu vā āmisakiñcikkhahetu vā sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: ‘Please, my man, say what you know.’ Not knowing, they say ‘I know.’ Knowing, they say ‘I don’t know.’ Not seeing, they say ‘I see.’ And seeing, they say ‘I don’t see.’ So they deliberately lie for the sake of themselves or another, or for some trivial worldly reason.

segs.p: Pisuṇavāco hoti, ito sutvā amutra akkhātā imesaṁ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā imesaṁ akkhātā amūsaṁ bhedāya. Iti samaggānaṁ vā bhettā bhinnānaṁ vā anuppadātā vaggārāmo vaggarato vagganandī, vaggakaraṇiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They backbite. They repeat in one place what they heard in another so as to divide people against each other. And so they divide those who are harmonious, supporting division, delighting in division, loving division, speaking words that promote division.

segs.p: Pharusavāco hoti, yā sā vācā aṇḍakā kakkasā parakaṭukā parābhisajjanī kodhasāmantā. Asamādhisaṁvattanikā, tathārūpiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They speak harshly. They use the kinds of words that are cruel, nasty, hurtful, offensive, bordering on anger, not leading to immersion.

segs.p: Samphappalāpī hoti, akālavādī abhūtavādī anatthavādī adhammavādī avinayavādī, anidhānavatiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti akālena anapadesaṁ apariyantavatiṁ anatthasaṁhitaṁ.
segs.e: They talk nonsense. Their speech is untimely, and is neither factual nor beneficial. It has nothing to do with the teaching or the training. Their words have no value, and are untimely, unreasonable, rambling, and pointless.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, catubbidhā vacīkammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti.
segs.e: These are the four kinds of corruption and failure of verbal action.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, tividhā manokammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti?
segs.e: And what are the three kinds of corruption and failure of mental action?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco abhijjhālu hoti. Yaṁ taṁ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṁ, taṁ abhijjhātā hoti: ‘aho vata, yaṁ parassa taṁ mama assā’ti.
segs.e: It’s when someone is covetous. They covet the wealth and belongings of others: ‘Oh, if only their belongings were mine!’

segs.p: Byāpannacitto hoti, paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo: ‘ime sattā haññantu vā bajjhantu vā ucchijjantu vā vinassantu vā mā vā ahesun’ti.
segs.e: They have ill will and malicious intentions: ‘May these sentient beings be killed, slaughtered, slain, destroyed, or annihilated!’
They have wrong view. Their perspective is distorted:

segs.p: ‘natthi dinnaṁ …pe… ye imañca lokaṁ parañca lokaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti.
segs.e: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tividhā manokammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti.
segs.e: These are the three kinds of corruption and failure of mental action.

segs.p: Tividhakāyakammantasandosabyāpattiakusalasañcetanikāhetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjanti; catubbidhavacīkammantasandosabyāpattiakusalasañcetanikāhetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjanti; tividhamanokammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikāhetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjanti.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, sentient beings are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell because of these three kinds of corruption and failure of bodily action, these four kinds of corruption and failure of verbal action, or these three kinds of corruption and failure of mental action that have unskillful intention, with suffering as their outcome and result.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, apaṇṇako maṇi uddhaṅkhitto yena yeneva patiṭṭhāti suppatiṭṭhitaṁyeva patiṭṭhāti;
segs.e: It’s like throwing sure-bet dice: they always fall the right side up.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tividhakāyakammantasandosabyāpattiakusalasañcetanikāhetu vā sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjanti; catubbidhavacīkammantasandosabyāpattiakusalasañcetanikāhetu vā sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjanti; tividhamanokammantasandosabyāpattiakusalasañcetanikāhetu vā sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjantīti.
segs.e: In the same way, when their body breaks up, after death, sentient beings are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell because of these three kinds of corruption and failure of bodily action, these four kinds of corruption and failure of verbal action, or these three kinds of corruption and failure of mental action that have unskillful intention, with suffering as their outcome and result.

segs.p: Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṁ kammānaṁ katānaṁ upacitānaṁ appaṭisaṁveditvā byantībhāvaṁ vadāmi,
segs.e: I don’t say that intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated are eliminated without being experienced.

segs.p: tañca kho diṭṭheva dhamme upapajje vā apare vā pariyāye.
segs.e: And that may be in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

segs.p: Na tvevāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṁ kammānaṁ katānaṁ upacitānaṁ appaṭisaṁveditvā dukkhassantakiriyaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: But in any case, there is no making an end of suffering without experiencing intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated, I say.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti;
segs.e: Now, there are three kinds of successful bodily action that have skillful intention, with happiness as their outcome and result.

segs.p: catubbidhā vacīkammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti;
segs.e: There are four kinds of successful verbal action that have skillful intention, with happiness as their outcome and result.

segs.p: tividhā manokammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti.
segs.e: There are three kinds of successful mental action that have skillful intention, with happiness as their outcome and result.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti?
segs.e: And what are the three kinds of successful bodily action?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho lajjī dayāpanno, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati …pe….
segs.e: It’s when someone gives up killing living creatures. They renounce the rod and the sword. They’re scrupulous and kind, living full of sympathy for all living beings.

segs.p: Adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, yaṁ taṁ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṁ gāmagataṁ vā araññagataṁ vā, na taṁ adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādātā hoti.
segs.e: They don’t steal. They don’t, with the intention to commit theft, take the wealth or belongings of others from village or wilderness.

segs.p: Kāmesumicchācāraṁ pahāya, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti. Yā tā māturakkhitā …pe… antamaso mālāguḷaparikkhittāpi, tathārūpāsu na cārittaṁ āpajjitā hoti.
segs.e: They give up sexual misconduct. They don’t have relations with women who have their mother, father, both mother and father, brother, sister, relatives, or clan as guardian. They don’t have relations with a woman who is protected on principle, or who has a husband, or whose violation is punishable by law, or even one who has been garlanded as a token of betrothal.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti.
segs.e: These are the three kinds of successful bodily action.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, catubbidhā vacīkammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti?
segs.e: And what are the four kinds of successful verbal action?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco musāvādaṁ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti. Sabhaggato vā parisaggato vā ñātimajjhagato vā pūgamajjhagato vā rājakulamajjhagato vā abhinīto sakkhipuṭṭho ‘ehambho purisa, yaṁ jānāsi taṁ vadehī’ti, so ajānaṁ vā āha: ‘na jānāmī’ti, jānaṁ vā āha: ‘jānāmī’ti, apassaṁ vā āha: ‘na passāmī’ti, passaṁ vā āha: ‘passāmī’ti, iti attahetu vā parahetu vā āmisakiñcikkhahetu vā na sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: It’s when someone gives up lying. They’re summoned to a council, an assembly, a family meeting, a guild, or to the royal court, and asked to bear witness: ‘Please, my friend, say what you know.’ Not knowing, they say ‘I don’t know.’ Knowing, they say ‘I know.’ Not seeing, they say ‘I don’t see.’ And seeing, they say ‘I see.’ So they don’t deliberately lie for the sake of themselves or another, or for some trivial worldly reason.

segs.p: Pisuṇaṁ vācaṁ pahāya, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti—na ito sutvā amutra akkhātā imesaṁ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā na imesaṁ akkhātā amūsaṁ bhedāya. Iti bhinnānaṁ vā sandhātā sahitānaṁ vā anuppadātā samaggārāmo samaggarato samagganandiṁ, samaggakaraṇiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They give up backbiting. They don’t repeat in one place what they heard in another so as to divide people against each other. Instead, they reconcile those who are divided and support those who are united, delighting in harmony, loving harmony, speaking words that promote harmony.

segs.p: Pharusaṁ vācaṁ pahāya, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti. Yā sā vācā nelā kaṇṇasukhā pemanīyā hadayaṅgamā porī bahujanakantā bahujanamanāpā, tathārūpiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: They give up harsh speech. They speak in a way that’s mellow, pleasing to the ear, endearing, going to the heart, polite, and likable and agreeable to the people.

segs.p: Samphappalāpaṁ pahāya, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti kālavādī bhūtavādī atthavādī dhammavādī vinayavādī, nidhānavatiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā hoti kālena sāpadesaṁ pariyantavatiṁ atthasaṁhitaṁ.
segs.e: They give up talking nonsense. Their words are timely, true, and meaningful, in line with the teaching and training. They say things at the right time which are valuable, reasonable, succinct, and beneficial.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, catubbidhā vacīkammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti.
segs.e: These are the four kinds of successful verbal action.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, tividhā manokammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti?
segs.e: And what are the three kinds of successful mental action?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco anabhijjhālu hoti. Yaṁ taṁ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṁ taṁ anabhijjhātā hoti: ‘aho vata, yaṁ parassa taṁ mamassā’ti.
segs.e: It’s when someone is content. They don’t covet the wealth and belongings of others: ‘Oh, if only their belongings were mine!’

segs.p: Abyāpannacitto hoti appaduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo: ‘ime sattā averā hontu abyāpajjā anīghā, sukhī attānaṁ pariharantū’ti.
segs.e: They have a kind heart and loving intentions: ‘May these sentient beings live free of enmity and ill will, untroubled and happy!’
They have right view, an undistorted perspective:

segs.p: ‘atthi dinnaṁ, atthi yiṭṭhaṁ …pe… ye imañca lokaṁ parañca lokaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti.
segs.e: ‘There is meaning in giving, sacrifice, and offerings. There are fruits and results of good and bad deeds. There is an afterlife. There are such things as mother and father, and beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there are ascetics and brahmins who are rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describe the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tividhā manokammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti.
segs.e: These are the three kinds of successful mental action.

segs.p: Tividhakāyakammantasampattikusalasañcetanikāhetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti; catubbidhavacīkammantasampattikusalasañcetanikāhetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti; tividhamanokammantasampattikusalasañcetanikāhetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, sentient beings are reborn in a good place, in heaven because of these three kinds of successful bodily action, these four kinds of successful verbal action, or these three kinds of successful mental action that have skillful intention, with happiness as their outcome and result.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, apaṇṇako maṇi uddhaṅkhitto yena yeneva patiṭṭhāti suppatiṭṭhitaṁyeva patiṭṭhāti;
segs.e: It’s like throwing unfaling dice: they always fall the right side up.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tividhakāyakammantasampattikusalasañcetanikāhetu vā sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti; catubbidhavacīkammantasampattikusalasañcetanikāhetu vā sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti; tividhamanokammantasampattikusalasañcetanikāhetu vā sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti.
segs.e: In the same way, when their body breaks up, after death, sentient beings are reborn in a good place, in heaven because of these three kinds of successful bodily action, these four kinds of successful verbal action, or these three kinds of successful mental action that have skillful intention, with happiness as their outcome and result.

segs.p: Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṁ kammānaṁ katānaṁ upacitānaṁ appaṭisaṁveditvā byantībhāvaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: I don’t say that intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated are eliminated without being experienced.

segs.p: Tañca kho diṭṭheva dhamme upapajje vā apare vā pariyāye.
segs.e: And that may be in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

segs.p: Na tvevāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṁ kammānaṁ katānaṁ upacitānaṁ appaṭisaṁveditvā dukkhassantakiriyaṁ vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: But in any case, there is no making an end of suffering without experiencing intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated, I say.”

21. The Body Born of Deeds
The Body Born of Deeds

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṁ kammānaṁ katānaṁ upacitānaṁ appaṭisaṁveditvā byantībhāvaṁ vadāmi,
segs.e: “Mendicants, I don’t say that intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated are eliminated without being experienced.

segs.p: tañca kho diṭṭheva dhamme upapajje vā apare vā pariyāye.
segs.e: And that may be in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

segs.p: Na tvevāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṁ kammānaṁ katānaṁ upacitānaṁ appaṭisaṁveditvā dukkhassantakiriyaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: But in any case, there is no making an end of suffering without experiencing intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated, I say.

segs.p: Sa kho so, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako evaṁ vigatābhijjho vigatabyāpādo asammūḷho sampajāno paṭissato mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati tathā dutiyaṁ tathā tatiyaṁ tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.
segs.e: That noble disciple is rid of desire, rid of ill will, unconfused, aware, and mindful. They meditate spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.
They understand:

segs.p: ‘pubbe kho me idaṁ cittaṁ parittaṁ ahosi abhāvitaṁ, etarahi pana me idaṁ cittaṁ appamāṇaṁ subhāvitaṁ. Yaṁ kho pana kiñci pamāṇakataṁ kammaṁ, na taṁ tatrāvasissati na taṁ tatrāvatiṭṭhatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Formerly my mind was limited and undeveloped. Now it’s limitless and well developed. Whatever limited deeds I’ve done don’t remain or persist there.’
What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: daharatagge ce so ayaṁ kumāro mettaṁ cetovimuttiṁ bhāveyya, api nu kho pāpakammaṁ kareyyā”ti?
segs.e: Suppose a child had developed the heart’s release by love from their childhood on. Would they still do any bad deed?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Akarontaṁ kho pana pāpakammaṁ api nu kho dukkhaṁ phuseyyā”ti?
segs.e: “Not doing any bad deed, would they still experience any suffering?”
“No, sir.

segs.p: Akarontañhi, bhante, pāpakammaṁ kuto dukkhaṁ phusissatī”ti.
segs.e: For if they don’t do any bad deed, from where would suffering afflict them?”

segs.p: “Bhāvetabbā kho panāyaṁ, bhikkhave, mettācetovimutti itthiyā vā purisena vā.
segs.e: “This heart’s release by love should be developed by women or men.

segs.p: Itthiyā vā, bhikkhave, purisassa vā nāyaṁ kāyo ādāya gamanīyo.
segs.e: For neither women nor men take this body with them when they go.
The mind is what’s inside mortal beings.
They understand:

segs.p: ‘yaṁ kho me idaṁ kiñci pubbe iminā karajakāyena pāpakammaṁ kataṁ, sabbaṁ taṁ idha vedanīyaṁ;
segs.e: ‘Whatever bad deeds I have done in the past with this deed-born body I will experience here.
It will not follow me to my next life.’

segs.p: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, mettā cetovimutti anāgāmitāya saṁvattati, idha paññassa bhikkhuno uttari vimuttiṁ appaṭivijjhato.
segs.e: The heart’s release by love developed in this way leads to non-return for a wise mendicant here who has not penetrated to a higher freedom.
They meditate spreading a heart full of compassion …
They meditate spreading a heart full of rejoicing …

segs.p: upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati tathā dutiyaṁ tathā tatiyaṁ tathā catutthaṁ.
segs.e: They meditate spreading a heart full of equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth.

segs.p: Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.

They understand:

“No, sir.”

“No, sir.

segs.e: For if they don’t do any bad deed, from where would suffering afflict them?”

segs.p: “Bhāvetabbā kho panāyaṁ, bhikkhave, upekkhā cetovimutti itthiyā vā purisena vā.
segs.e: “This heart’s release by equanimity should be developed by women or men.

segs.p: Itthiyā vā, bhikkhave, purisassa vā nāyaṁ kāyo ādāya gamanīyo.
segs.e: For neither women nor men take this body with them when they go.
The mind is what’s inside mortal beings.
They understand:

segs.e: ‘Whatever bad deeds I have done in the past with this deed-born body I will experience here.
It will not follow me to my next life.’

segs.p: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, upekkhā cetovimutti anāgāmitāya saṁvattati, idha paññassa bhikkhuno uttari vimuttiṁ appaṭivijjhato”ti.
segs.e: The heart’s release by equanimity developed in this way leads to non-return for a wise mendicant here who has not penetrated to a higher freedom.”
Numbered Discourses 10.220
21. The Body Born of Deeds
Unprincipled Conduct

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then a certain brahmin went up to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjantī”ti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, worthy Gotama, what is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell?”

segs.p: “Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu kho, brāhmaṇa, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjantī”ti.
segs.e: “Unprincipled and immoral conduct is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

segs.p: “Ko pana, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjantī”ti?
segs.e: “But what is the cause, worthy Gotama, what is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm?”

segs.p: “Dhammacariyāsamacariyāhetu kho, brāhmaṇa, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjantī”ti.
segs.e: “Principled and moral conduct is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

segs.p: “Na kho ahaṁ imassa bhoto gotamassa saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi.
segs.e: “I don’t understand the detailed meaning of what the worthy Gotama has said in brief.

segs.p: Sādhu me bhavaṁ gotamo tathā dhammaṁ desetu yathāhaṁ imassa bhoto gotamassa saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājāneyyan”ti.
segs.e: Please, worthy Gotama, teach me this matter so I can understand the detailed meaning.”

segs.p: “Tena hi, brāhmaṇa, suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, brahmin, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bho”ti kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavato paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, worthy sir,” the brahmin replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Brahmin, unprincipled and immoral conduct is threefold by way of body,
fourfold by way of speech,
and threefold by way of mind.

segs.p: Kathañca, brāhmaṇa, tividhā kāyena adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti …pe…
segs.e: And how is unprincipled and immoral conduct threefold by way of body? …

segs.p: evaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, tividhā kāyena adhammacariyā visamacariyā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how unprincipled and immoral conduct is threefold by way of body.

segs.p: Kathañca, brāhmaṇa, catubbidhā vācāya adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti …pe…
segs.e: And how is unprincipled and immoral conduct fourfold by way of speech? …

segs.p: evaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, catubbidhā vācāya adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how unprincipled and immoral conduct is fourfold by way of speech.

segs.p: Kathañca, brāhmaṇa, tividhā manasā adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti …pe…
segs.e: And how is unprincipled and immoral conduct threefold by way of mind? …

segs.p: evaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, tividhā manasā adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how unprincipled and immoral conduct is threefold by way of mind.

segs.p: Evaṁ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu kho, brāhmaṇa, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjanti.
segs.e: That’s how unprincipled and immoral conduct is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.
Principled and moral conduct is threefold by way of body,
fourfold by way of speech,
and threefold by way of mind.

segs.p: Kathañca, brāhmaṇa, tividhā kāyena dhammacariyāsamacariyā hoti …pe…
segs.e: And how is principled and moral conduct threefold by way of body? …

segs.p: evaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, tividhā kāyena dhammacariyāsamacariyā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how principled and moral conduct is threefold by way of body.

segs.p: Kathañca, brāhmaṇa, catubbidhā vācāya dhammacariyāsamacariyā hoti …pe…
segs.e: And how is principled and moral conduct fourfold by way of speech? …

segs.p: evaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, catubbidhā vācāya dhammacariyāsamacariyā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how principled and moral conduct is fourfold by way of speech.

segs.p: Kathañca, brāhmaṇa, tividhā manasā dhammacariyāsamacariyā hoti …pe…
segs.e: And how is principled and moral conduct threefold by way of mind? …

segs.p: evaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, tividhā manasā dhammacariyāsamacariyā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how principled and moral conduct is threefold by way of mind.

segs.p: Evaṁ dhammacariyāsamacariyāhetu kho, brāhmaṇa, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjantī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how principled and moral conduct is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

22. Similarity
Untitled Discourse on Ten Qualities

segs.p: “Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Someone with ten qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What ten?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, pisuṇavāco hoti, pharusavāco hoti, samphappalāpī hoti, abhijjhālu hoti, byāpannacitto hoti, micchādiṭṭhiko hoti—
segs.e: They kill living creatures, steal, and commit sexual misconduct. They use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re covetous, malicious, with wrong view.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: Someone with these ten qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: Someone with ten qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What ten?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, anabhijjhālu hoti, abyāpannacitto hoti, sammādiṭṭhiko hoti—
segs.e: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, or commit sexual misconduct. They don’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. They’re contented, kind-hearted, with right view.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.

23. Abbreviated Texts Beginning With Greed
Untitled Discourse on Greed (1st)
“For insight into greed, ten things should be developed.
What ten?

segs.p: Asubhasaññā, maraṇasaññā, āhāre paṭikūlasaññā, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññā, aniccasaññā, anicce dukkhasaññā, dukkhe anattasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā, nirodhasaññā—
segs.e: The perceptions of ugliness, death, repulsiveness of food, dissatisfaction with the whole world, impermanence, suffering in impermanence, and not-self in suffering, giving up, fading away, and cessation.

segs.p: rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime dasa dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these ten things should be developed.”

“For insight into greed, ten things should be developed.
What ten?

segs.p: Aniccasaññā, anattasaññā, āhāre paṭikūlasaññā, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññā, aṭṭhikasaññā, puḷavakasaññā, vinīlakasaññā, vipubbakasaññā, vicchiddakasaññā, uddhumātakasaññā—
segs.e: The perceptions of impermanence, not-self, repulsiveness of food, dissatisfaction with the whole world, a skeleton, a worm-infested corpse, a livid corpse, a festering corpse,  a split open corpse, and a bloated corpse.

segs.p: rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime dasa dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these ten things should be developed.”
Numbered Discourses 10.239
23. Abbreviated Texts Beginning With Greed
Untitled Discourse on Greed (3rd)
“For insight into greed, ten things should be developed.
What ten?

segs.p: Sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi, sammāñāṇaṁ, sammāvimutti—
segs.e: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

segs.p: rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime dasa dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these ten things should be developed.”
